sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: Whom do Minnesota's traffic statutes govern, and across which roadways?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Minnesota's traffic laws cover every person who drives on a public road anywhere in the state.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: Under what five road, lane, or safety conditions may you leave the right side of a wide roadway?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: On roads of sufficient width you keep to the right side unless you are passing a vehicle going your way, the right side is closed for construction or repair, the road has three marked lanes, signs make it one-way, or you are moving over for a stopped authorized vehicle under the Move Over Law.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: What two boundaries does Minnesota's basic speed law set using current conditions and posted signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Under the basic speed law your speed must be reasonable for the current weather, traffic and road conditions, and the posted limit is the highest speed allowed on that road.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: How does the law treat creeping below a posted minimum speed limit when roads and weather are normal?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Where a minimum speed limit is posted, driving below it under normal conditions is illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: With no sign posted and ideal conditions, what is Minnesota's statutory speed limit inside an alley?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Unless signs say otherwise, the speed limit in an alley under ideal conditions is ten miles per hour

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: Unless signs say otherwise, what is the ideal-condition speed limit on urban or town roads in Minnesota?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Unless signs say otherwise, the speed limit on urban or town roads under ideal conditions is thirty miles per hour

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: Where no sign stands outside alleys and urban streets, what default speed limit covers everywhere else?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Unless signs say otherwise, the speed limit under ideal conditions is fifty-five miles per hour in every location not otherwise listed.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: How must you adjust your driving inside school zones when kids are out and inside work zones?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: In a school zone you must slow down when children are present, and in a work or construction zone you must slow down and drive carefully.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: What three numbers summarize Minnesota's unposted default speed ladder, and what overrides them?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: The three default limits under ideal conditions are ten miles per hour in alleys, thirty miles per hour on urban or town roads and fifty-five miles per hour everywhere else, and posted signs override all three.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: Under what exact road-type, posted-limit, and maneuver rules does Minnesota allow ten over the limit?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: On two-lane highways posted at fifty-five miles per hour or higher you may go up to ten miles per hour over the limit, but only while lawfully passing another vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: What three things worsen simultaneously as your driving speed climbs?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Driving faster shortens the time you have to react, raises the odds of a crash and makes serious injury or death in a crash more likely.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: What legal privilege does a driver lose by barreling into an intersection above the speed limit?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: A driver who reaches an intersection at an unlawful speed gives up the right-of-way they would have had at a lawful speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: At how many miles per hour above the posted limit do extra Minnesota speeding fines kick in?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Speeding can bring a fine, and extra fines apply when you drive twenty miles per hour or more above the posted limit.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: What license penalty hits anyone caught driving faster than one hundred miles per hour in Minnesota?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Driving faster than one hundred miles per hour leads to revocation of your driving privileges for at least six months.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: What must you do near a stopped flashing emergency vehicle, and what minimum surcharge hits violators?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: You must slow down when approaching or passing a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing emergency lights, and breaking this rule adds a surcharge of at least twenty-five dollars to the speeding fine.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How does the penalty at twenty-plus over the limit escalate if you push past one hundred miles per hour?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Going twenty miles per hour or more over the limit adds extra fines, while going over one hundred miles per hour costs your driving privileges for at least six months.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: Besides raising crash odds, how does high speed change what your eyes take in?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: Higher speed narrows your field of vision as well as raising the risk of a crash.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: Around what five people or warning markers in the roadway—plus weather and rough pavement—must you drop speed?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: Watch for flag persons, pedestrians, barricades, flares or reflectors in the roadway and reduce speed for them, as well as in bad weather and on poor road surfaces.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: Which five road widths, alignments, or crossings require easing off your speed in advance?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Reduce speed on narrow or winding roads and as you near a curve, the top of a hill or a railroad crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: What two traction changes demand slower speeds whenever pavement turns to gravel or dirt?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: On gravel or dirt roads slow down, because stopping takes longer and the vehicle skids more easily in a turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: What two custom restrictions often appear on bridge approaches that drivers must watch for?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Bridges may carry their own speed limits and No Passing signs, and you must watch for and obey them.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: At least how far ahead of a turn must your blinker start, and how long does it stay flashing?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Turn on your signal at least one hundred feet before you turn, and keep it on until the turn or lane change is finished.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: When may hand and arm gestures be used in Minnesota, and in what two situations are they invalid?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: In daylight you may use hand and arm signals along with or in place of turn signals, but not at night or in a vehicle that hides your hand from other drivers.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: Why must you rely strictly on electric turn signals at night or in wide-body vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.memory_hook: Nighttime and wide bodies hide arms
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Hand and arm signals are a daylight option only; at night, or when your vehicle hides your arm, rely on the turn signals.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: Do traffic lanes still exist on unmarked or snow-covered asphalt, and how must you hold your path?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: A traffic lane exists whether or not it is marked, and you must stay inside one lane without weaving or straddling the markings.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: What three-way space check and physical head move must come before switching lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Before changing lanes make sure there is room beside, behind and ahead of you, and turn your head to check the new lane instead of relying only on mirrors.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: What structural car parts create permanent blind spots, and what two glass issues create temporary ones?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Blind spots are areas your mirrors cannot show; the vehicle's design and roof pillars decide where they are, and a dirty windshield or glare can add temporary ones.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.front: Whose blind spots must you avoid pacing inside—especially on multi-lane highways?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.expected_back: Stay out of other drivers' blind spots, and pay special attention to them near commercial vehicles.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: Because improper turns cause so many crashes, when should you move into your turn lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Improper turns cause many crashes, so move into the correct lane well before the point where you will turn.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: What wrong-lane mistake must you never make, and what scan and finish rule govern every turn?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Never make a sudden turn from the wrong lane, watch for traffic or obstacles on the road you are entering, and always end the turn in the correct lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: How should you hold your wheels and right foot while waiting for a gap to turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: While you wait to turn, keep the wheels pointed straight and your foot on the brake so a rear-end hit is less likely to shove you into oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: Waiting to turn left on green in Minnesota, how far into the intersection do you pull, and when might your gap come?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: When waiting to turn left on a green light with traffic coming toward you, pull into the intersection until your body lines up with the curb line, and you may only get to turn once the light turns yellow.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: How should you respond right away when the car directly ahead flicks on a left turn signal?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: If the car ahead is signaling a left turn, slow down and get ready to stop.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: Where do you start a left turn on marked or unmarked roads, and in which lane do you finish?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: For a left turn, check behind you and signal, move into the lane nearest the center line, or just right of the road's center if lanes are unmarked, look both ways, yield if needed, and finish in the first lane to the right of the center line.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: How do you set up, scan, and finish a textbook right-hand turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: For a right turn, check behind you and signal, move close to the right curb, look both ways, yield if needed, and finish in the lane next to the curb.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.front: How do left-turn and right-turn finish lanes contrast, and what steering technique applies to both?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.expected_back: A left turn ends in the first lane to the right of the center line, while a right turn ends in the lane next to the curb, and both use hand-over-hand steering.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: What lane rule governs intersections marked with two or more parallel turning lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Where signs or lane markings show two or more turning lanes, stay in your own lane all the way through the turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: What lane, stop, sign, and scanning steps are required before turning right on a red light?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: Many intersections allow a right turn on red after a complete stop in the correct lane, unless a No Turn on Red sign is posted, and only after checking every direction for pedestrians and traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: Under what sole street layout—and after what two checks—is turning left on red legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: A left turn on red is allowed in certain cases only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after a complete stop and once the intersection is clear.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: What requirement do right-on-red and left-on-red share, and how do their street rules differ?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: A right turn on red is allowed at many intersections, but a left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, and both need a complete stop first.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: While edging up for a right turn on red, what unexpected oncoming movement must you watch out for?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: When you turn right on red, watch for oncoming drivers turning left in front of you, since their green arrow may come on before your light turns green.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.front: Whom must every red-light turner yield to, and what overrides turning on red altogether?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.expected_back: Whenever you turn on a red light, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and where a No Turn on Red sign is posted, wait for the green light.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.front: What two advantages lead engineers to build roundabouts in place of four-way stops?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.expected_back: Roundabouts are built to move traffic better and to make intersections safer than ordinary four-way stops.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: What speed, lane-choice, yielding, and sign checks belong on your approach to a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: As you approach a roundabout, slow down, pick your lane before entering if it has more than one lane, yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing, and watch for signs or markings that require or forbid certain moves.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: Whom must you yield to—and from which direction does circulating traffic come—before entering a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: Enter a roundabout only after yielding to vehicles already circulating and after all traffic coming from your left has cleared.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: Which direction do you circulate inside a roundabout, and what three maneuvers are banned inside it?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: Inside a roundabout drive counterclockwise to your exit and never stop, pass or change lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: What must you do if an ambulance or fire rig approaches while you are circulating inside a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in a roundabout, leave the roundabout right away and then pull over.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: Which long, wide, or hitched vehicles are legally allowed to straddle lanes through a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: Any combination vehicle, or a vehicle over forty feet long or more than ten feet wide, may leave its lane as needed to get through a roundabout while watching other traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.front: When two large trucks enter a multi-lane roundabout side by side, which truck must yield?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.expected_back: Entering cars yield to cars already in the roundabout, but when two large vehicles go through a multi-lane roundabout side by side, the driver on the right yields to the one on the left, slowing or stopping if needed.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: What deadly crash type are J-turn intersections engineered to slash on four-lane divided highways?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: J-turns exist to cut deaths and injuries from broadside crashes on four-lane divided highways.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: How does a side-street driver cross straight or go left at a Minnesota J-turn intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: At a J-turn every side-street driver turns right; to cross or go left you stop completely, turn right onto the highway, move into the marked left-turn lane at the median opening and make a U-turn.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.front: When turning right into a J-turn with clear highway lanes, may you sweep straight across into the left-turn bay?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.expected_back: During the right turn at a J-turn you may cross both lanes into the left-turn lane in a single motion when it is safe, which shortens your time in the through lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: What priority rule governs the final U-turn phase of a J-turn before re-entering highway lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: When finishing the U-turn at a J-turn you must yield to oncoming traffic, stopping if needed, before entering the through lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.front: How may you cross a standard rural divided highway when its center median is wide enough to hold your car?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.expected_back: When a rural divided highway has enough room between its roadways, you may cross one half, wait in the middle to the right of center, and cross the second half when it is safe.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.front: Beyond two-stage crossing steps, what extra gap cushion must you allow when turning left onto a divided highway?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.expected_back: Turning left onto a divided highway follows the same steps as crossing it, and you must leave enough room that you do not slow oncoming traffic while you speed up.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.front: What motion defines a U-turn, and what traffic condition and sign rule govern whether it is legal?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.expected_back: A U-turn reverses your direction with a half-circle turn, is allowed only when it will not disrupt other traffic, and is forbidden wherever a No U-Turn sign is posted.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: On which highways—and inside what hilltop or curve sight distance—are U-turns banned in Minnesota?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: U-turns are banned on interstate freeways, and also near hilltops or on curves where drivers coming toward you could not see you from one thousand feet away.

sec05-card-sec05-R22.front: On a road with two or more lanes going your way, how wide may you swing to complete a tight U-turn?
sec05-card-sec05-R22.expected_back: On a roadway with two or more lanes in your direction, you may swing into the farthest lane and briefly use the shoulder to finish a U-turn when needed.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.front: Where must you position your vehicle on a single-lane direction road if moving slowly enough to create a hazard?
sec05-card-sec05-R23.expected_back: With only one lane in your direction, a driver going slowly enough to create a hazard must stay as close as possible to the right curb or road edge.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: On highways with multiple lanes in your direction, how should you use the right-hand and left-most lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: On highways with more than one lane in your direction, use the right-hand lane when one is available, and leave the left-most lane to let another vehicle pass when practical.

sec05-card-sec05-R24.front: What five situations make driving outside the right-hand highway lane completely legal?
sec05-card-sec05-R24.expected_back: You may use a lane other than the right-hand lane when passing, preparing a left turn at an intersection or into a driveway, preparing a left-side exit from an expressway, freeway or interstate, driving an authorized emergency vehicle, or following a traffic control device, a peace officer or work zone directions.

sec05-card-sec05-R27.front: When does passing demand extra caution, and what front-and-rear checks come before pulling left?
sec05-card-sec05-R27.expected_back: Take extra care passing at night, in poor visibility or on slippery roads, and before passing make sure oncoming traffic is far enough away and that nobody behind you is starting to pass.

sec05-card-sec05-R28.front: How do you signal both ends of a pass, and what mirror sight tells you to pull back right?
sec05-card-sec05-R28.expected_back: Signal left before moving out to pass and signal right after passing, then return to the right lane once the whole vehicle you passed shows in your rearview mirror.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.front: In Minnesota, before closing within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must you be back in your right lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.expected_back: After passing you must be back on the right side of the road before you come within one hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-R25.front: Which two separate Minnesota passing laws both rely on the exact one-hundred-foot measurement?
sec05-card-sec05-R25.memory_hook: Oncoming return and four no-pass spots
sec05-card-sec05-R25.expected_back: On the passing page one hundred feet appears twice: you must be back in the right lane before you are within one hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle, and you may not pass within one hundred feet of an intersection, underpass, tunnel or railroad crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.front: How do No Passing signs, a solid yellow stripe on your side, and double solid yellow lines restrict overtaking?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.expected_back: You may not pass where a No Passing Zone sign is posted or where a solid yellow line is on your side of the center line, and double solid yellow lines forbid passing in both directions.

sec05-card-sec05-R26.front: How does a single solid yellow stripe on your side differ in reach from double solid yellow lines?
sec05-card-sec05-R26.expected_back: A single solid yellow line on your side bans passing for you, while a double solid yellow line bans passing for drivers in both directions.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.front: At least how many feet of clear road ahead must you see before passing on any hill or curve?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.expected_back: Never pass on a hill or curve unless you can clearly see at least seven hundred feet of road ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.front: Within one hundred feet of which four roadway structures or crossings is passing strictly illegal?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.expected_back: Passing is not allowed within one hundred feet of an intersection, an underpass, a tunnel or a railroad crossing.

sec05-card-sec05-R29.front: When must you abort starting a pass, and what must you do while someone overtakes you?
sec05-card-sec05-R29.expected_back: Do not pass when you are about to meet an oncoming vehicle, and when someone is passing you, stay in your lane and do not speed up.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.front: In what three road or left-turn situations is passing on the right legal when safe?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.expected_back: You may pass on the right only when it is safe and the vehicle ahead is turning or about to turn left, or the road has room for two or more lanes of moving traffic each way, or it is a one-way road wide enough for two or more lanes with nothing in the way.

sec05-card-sec05-R30.front: May you dip into a bike lane, paved shoulder, or gravel edge to pass a left-turning car on the right?
sec05-card-sec05-R30.expected_back: A pass on the right must stay on the main roadway: using a bike lane, the shoulder or the unpaved edge to get around a vehicle is not allowed.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.front: Who is the sole exception allowed to reverse on a freeway, and what criminal charges can street backing bring?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.expected_back: Backing up on freeways or expressways is not allowed except for emergency vehicles on duty, and backing on public roads can lead to a reckless or careless driving charge.

sec05-card-sec05-R31.front: Into which lane should you reverse when backing out of a driveway, and what crossing move is off-limits?
sec05-card-sec05-R31.expected_back: Leaving a driveway in reverse, back only into the closest lane and then pull forward, and never reverse into or across traffic lanes unless you are sure it is safe.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Where must you come to a halt at a steady red light, and when may you proceed?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: A steady red light means stop: halt at the stop line, before the crosswalk or before entering the intersection, and wait for the light to change.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Under what conditions may you turn right on a red light, and what posted sign blocks it?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: After stopping for a red light you may turn right once the intersection is clear and traffic is allowed in that direction, unless a No Turn on Red sign tells you to wait for green.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: Under what exact street-direction and yielding rules may a Minnesota driver turn left on red?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: On red you may turn left from a one-way road onto a one-way cross street only after a full stop, once the intersection is clear, after yielding to pedestrians and vehicles, and only if traffic on the new street moves solely in the direction you are turning.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: What starting step do right-on-red and left-on-red share, and what extra road restriction applies only to left-on-red?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Both turns on red begin with a complete stop, but the left turn on red is limited to turning from a one-way road onto a one-way cross street, a condition the right turn on red does not carry.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: What must you do at a red arrow, and when may you move in the arrow's direction?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: A red arrow means stop at the stop line, before the crosswalk or before the intersection, and you may go in the arrow's direction only when it turns green.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: How does a steady red arrow match a steady red ball, and how is its reach narrower?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: A red arrow and a steady red light both require a full stop at the stop line, but the red arrow controls only the movement in its direction.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: What three steps—stopping, yielding, and proceeding—govern a flashing red traffic light?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: At a flashing red light, stop completely, yield to vehicles and pedestrians who got to the intersection before you, and continue when it is clear.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: Contrast when you may enter the intersection after stopping for a steady red light versus a flashing red light?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: A steady red light holds you until the light changes, while a flashing red light works like a stop sign, letting you go after a full stop once the intersection is clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: What does a steady yellow light or arrow warn, and how do you decide between stopping and continuing?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: A steady yellow light or arrow means the signal is about to turn red, so do not enter the intersection if you can stop safely, and otherwise go through with caution.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: If you are already waiting inside an intersection to turn when yellow changes to red, what must you do?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: If you are waiting in the intersection to turn when the light goes from yellow to red, finish the turn as soon as it is safe, and do not back up.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: How should you drive through a flashing yellow light or flashing yellow arrow?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: A flashing yellow light or arrow means go through with caution and yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: To whom must a driver yield when turning left or making a U-turn on a flashing yellow signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: On a flashing yellow, a driver turning left or making a U-turn must yield to oncoming vehicles near enough to be an immediate hazard.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: Contrast what a steady yellow signal announces against what a flashing yellow signal instructs?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: A steady yellow tells you the light is about to turn red, while a flashing yellow tells you to go through with caution and yield to anyone already in the intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: Even with a circular green light, to which three groups must you still yield before going or turning?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: On a green light you may cross once the intersection is clear, but you still yield to vehicles or pedestrians in it, to oncoming traffic when turning left, and to pedestrians crossing in front of you when turning either way.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What turning right and conflict protection does a illuminated green arrow provide?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: A green arrow means you may turn in its direction, and the turn should be protected from oncoming or crossing traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: When turning left, how does your oncoming-traffic duty change between a circular green light and a green arrow?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: A green light lets you go but leaves you to yield to oncoming traffic on a left turn, while a green arrow gives you a turn that should be protected from oncoming or crossing traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: What safety check should pedestrians still make when the Walk signal lights up, and what if it changes mid-crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: Pedestrians must obey pedestrian signals, and when the Walk signal shows they should still check that crossing is safe, then may finish crossing once they have started.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: How does a flashing raised hand or Don't Walk signal treat pedestrians on the curb versus those mid-crosswalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: When the raised hand or Don't Walk signal flashes, pedestrians should not start crossing, but anyone already in the intersection may finish at a normal pace.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: What must pedestrians on the sidewalk and anyone caught mid-street do when Don't Walk turns steady?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: When the raised hand or Don't Walk signal is steady, pedestrians should not try to cross, and anyone already crossing should get to the nearest safe spot as quickly and safely as they can.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: Compare pedestrian rules across Walk, flashing Don't Walk, and steady Don't Walk?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: There are stop and go signals for pedestrians: Walk lets them start after checking it is safe, a flashing Don't Walk means do not start but finish if already crossing, and a steady Don't Walk means do not cross and get to safety if already in the street.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: What traffic management purpose do overhead lane-use control signals serve, and do standard signs still apply?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Lane use control signals let the same lane carry traffic from different directions at different times, and you must still follow every other sign and signal that applies.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: What does a steady downward-pointing green arrow suspended above a travel lane tell you?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: A steady downward green arrow over a lane means you may drive in that lane.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: Contrast a steady downward green arrow above a lane against a steady red X?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: A steady downward green arrow means you may use the lane, and a steady red X means you may not.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: What is happening when a steady yellow X lights up above your lane, and how should you respond?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: A steady yellow X over a lane means a lane-control change is under way, so prepare to move safely into another lane before a steady red X appears.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: On a freeway, what does a steady downward-pointing yellow arrow over your lane announce?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: A steady downward yellow arrow over a freeway lane means that lane will close, so prepare to move safely into another lane.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: What shared lane action do an overhead steady yellow X and downward-pointing steady yellow arrow call for, and why?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: A steady yellow X and a steady downward yellow arrow both tell you to prepare to leave the lane, the first because a lane-control change is coming and the second because the freeway lane will close.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: Which single maneuver does a flashing yellow X over a lane allow, and why is caution essential?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: A flashing yellow X over a lane means you may use it to turn left, with caution, because drivers from the other direction may be turning left in the same lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: What does a flashing downward yellow arrow above a freeway lane permit?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: A flashing downward yellow arrow over a freeway lane means you may use the lane, but with caution.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: Contrast how you may use a lane under a flashing yellow X versus a flashing downward yellow arrow?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: A flashing yellow X lets you use the lane only for a left turn, while a flashing downward yellow arrow lets you drive in the freeway lane with caution.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: What rule applies whenever a steady red X illuminates over a lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: A steady red X over a lane means you may not drive in that lane.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: What are freeway ramp meters, and how do they manage merging traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: Ramp meters are red, yellow and green signal lights on freeway entrance ramps that control the flow of merging traffic, working like intersection signals.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: At an active freeway ramp meter, how many vehicles are allowed to go on each green light?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: At a metered freeway ramp only one car may go on each green light, so drivers take turns entering the highway.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: In pavement markings, what traffic-direction rule distinguishes white lines from yellow lines?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: Pavement markings direct and regulate traffic, with white lines for traffic going the same way and yellow lines for traffic going opposite ways.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: Which relative flow of traffic do white pavement lines separate?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: What do regular white dashed lines allow, and what do shorter, thicker white dashes warn?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: White dashed lines mean you may change lanes, while shorter, thicker white dashes mean the lane is ending.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: How does the shape of white dashed lines shift when your travel lane is about to end?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: Ordinary white dashes allow lane changes, but shorter and thicker white dashes warn that your lane is ending.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: What lane-change guidance does a single solid white line give, and what four other features does solid white mark?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: A solid white line means you should not change lanes, and solid white lines also mark crosswalks, stop lines, parking stalls and the edges of the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: What strict rule applies where double solid white lines separate same-direction lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Double solid white lines mean you must not change lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: How does the strength of the rule escalate from a single solid white line to double solid white lines?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: A single solid white line says you should not change lanes, while double solid white lines say you must not.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: Which two rider types may use a lane marked by a solid white line and bicycle symbol, and heading which way?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: A solid white line with a bicycle symbol marks space only for bicycles and electric-assist bicycles, and riders there must travel the same direction as the traffic beside them.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: What relationship between traffic streams do yellow pavement markings indicate?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: How do a solid yellow centerline and a broken dashed yellow centerline differ for overtaking?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: A solid yellow line means you must not pass, while yellow dashes mean you may pass.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.front: Is overtaking allowed inside a no-passing zone, and which yellow line marks that restriction?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.expected_back: Passing in a no-passing zone is illegal, and a solid yellow line marks where you must not pass.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: When a centerline pairs a solid yellow stripe alongside yellow dashes, which stripe governs you?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: Where a solid yellow line runs on one side and dashes on the other, follow the marking on your own lane's side.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: Who is allowed to pass across a double solid yellow centerline?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines forbid passing no matter which side of them you are driving on.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.front: Compare passing rights on a two-lane road marked with single yellow dashes versus dashes paired with one solid line?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.expected_back: On a two-lane, two-way road divided by yellow dashes, drivers in either lane may pass, but where one side has a solid yellow line, drivers in that lane may not.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: On an undivided highway with two lanes each way separated by double solid yellow lines, may you cross yellow to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: On a road with two lanes each way separated by two solid yellow lines, do not cross those lines to pass.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.front: When a two-lane two-way road carries no-passing markings for both directions, which drivers may overtake?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.expected_back: On a two-lane road with two-way traffic marked so that passing is barred in both directions, nobody may pass whichever way they are driving.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.front: When a physical solid divider separates a two-way multilane highway, what road feature is missing along the inner edges?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.expected_back: A multilane road with traffic in both directions may be separated by a solid traffic divider, and such a road has no shoulders at its inner edges.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: What do white lane arrows near intersections require, and how do multi-arrow lanes differ?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: White turn arrows near intersections, sometimes with the word only, mean a vehicle in that lane must turn, though some lanes show several arrows that allow turning or going straight.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: Why are dedicated intersection turn lanes bordered by a solid white stripe next to through lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: Solid white lines separate turn lanes from through lanes to discourage lane changes close to the intersection.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: How is a shared center left-turn-only lane painted, and which directions may enter it to turn left?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: A center left-turn-only lane between opposing traffic is marked by parallel solid and dashed yellow lines, sometimes with white arrows, and drivers from either direction may use it to turn left onto a road or driveway.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.front: On a two-way three-lane street, what single purpose belongs to the middle lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.expected_back: On a three-lane road with traffic in both directions, the center lane is reserved for drivers turning left from either direction.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: What yellow lines border a reversible lane, and when may you cross into it?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: Reversible lanes, used to keep rush-hour traffic moving, are bounded by dashed double yellow lines that you may cross only when the overhead signal for the lane shows a green arrow or a sign allows it.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.front: Distinguish the yellow stripes of a shared center left-turn lane from those of a reversible lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.expected_back: A center turn lane is marked by parallel solid and dashed yellow lines, while a reversible lane is bounded by dashed double yellow lines that need a green overhead arrow or a sign before you cross.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: How many occupants qualify a car for a carpool lane, how is it marked, and where does it usually sit?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: Carpool lanes are only for vehicles with two or more occupants, are marked with a diamond or Carpool Only signs, and usually sit on the far left of a freeway.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.front: Which paint colors may separate a freeway carpool lane from general-purpose lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.expected_back: Carpool lanes may be separated from other freeway lanes by combinations of white or yellow lines.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.front: What role do large words painted directly on the roadway—like School Zone Ahead—play?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.expected_back: Words painted on the pavement, such as School Zone Ahead, warn of conditions ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.front: When a traffic officer directs an intersection, how do their hand signals rank against lights, signs, and paint?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.expected_back: When an officer is directing traffic, obey the officer's hand signals instead of the traffic signals, signs or pavement markings.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.front: Who may direct traffic on occasion alongside police, and whose commands take top priority when an officer is present?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.expected_back: Law enforcement officers, and on some occasions other individuals, direct traffic, and when an officer is present the officer's hand signals come before signals, signs and pavement markings.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.front: Which hand gesture and whistle blast do most traffic officers pair together to command a stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.expected_back: Most traffic officers signal stop by raising one hand with the palm toward the vehicle and giving one long whistle blast.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.front: How do traffic officers signal you to start or keep moving, and what tool helps after dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.expected_back: Officers signal you to start or keep moving with a hand motion and a series of short whistle blasts, and may use a flashlight when light is low.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.front: Contrast a traffic officer's whistle and hand cues between stop and go?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.expected_back: A long whistle blast with a raised palm means stop, and a series of short blasts with a hand motion means go.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: How does Minnesota treat holding a driver's license, and what can take it away?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: Driving in Minnesota is a privilege that you can lose by breaking certain laws or failing to meet certain requirements.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: Which violations land on your Minnesota DVS record, and what restrictions can serious or repeat offenses trigger?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: DVS keeps a record of your driving that includes violations in Minnesota and in other states, and serious or repeated violations can lead to losing your privilege or to limits on where, when and what you may drive.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: Where can a Minnesota driver request a personal copy of their driving record?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: You can get a copy of your own driving record from the state's online DVS service.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: What are Minnesota's three ways of withdrawing a license, and how do you learn the steps back?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: A license can be withdrawn in three ways: suspension, revocation or cancellation, and DPS then mails a notice of withdrawal listing the reinstatement requirements.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: Which official publication details how commercial driver's license holders lose CDL privileges?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: Commercial driver's license holders can lose those privileges for certain driving offenses, and the Minnesota Commercial Driver's License Manual covers those rules.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: Which pattern of traffic tickets, or single crash-linked conviction, can suspend your Minnesota license?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: Repeatedly breaking traffic laws, or a conviction for a violation that contributed to a crash causing death, injury or serious property damage, can lead to suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: When does a traffic violation committed outside Minnesota trigger a license suspension back home?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: A traffic offense committed in another state can lead to suspension if it would be grounds for suspension in Minnesota.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: Which court fitness ruling or unreported health issue can suspend your driving privileges?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: A court finding that you are legally unfit to drive, or failing to report a medical condition that would cancel your privileges, can lead to suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: Within what lookback window does a second conviction for passing a red-flashing school bus bring suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: Failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights within five years of an earlier conviction for the same offense can lead to suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: How do missed court appearances, unpaid vehicle fines, or traffic misdemeanors affect your license?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Failing to appear in court or to pay a fine for a motor vehicle violation when required, or a misdemeanor conviction under Minnesota traffic law, can lead to suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: Does Minnesota require multiple misdemeanor traffic convictions before suspension becomes possible, or can one suffice?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: Even one misdemeanor conviction for breaking a Minnesota traffic law is listed as a possible ground for suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: What license action can follow when a court finds someone under twenty-one drove after consuming alcohol?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: A driver under twenty-one whom a court finds drove while or after consuming alcohol can have their license suspended.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: What happens to your driving privileges if you are convicted of stealing gasoline?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: A conviction for theft of gasoline can lead to suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: May you ever let a friend borrow your license or permit, and what penalty covers unlawful license lending?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: Letting anyone else use your license or permit is illegal, and using or lending a license for an illegal act can bring a suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Which three credential or exam-room frauds carry a Minnesota license suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Having a fake or altered license, applying fraudulently for a license or ID card, or taking any part of the license exam for someone else can lead to suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: If someone else takes part of your license exam for you, who faces suspension under Minnesota rules?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.memory_hook: Both applicant and stand-in risk suspension
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Allowing someone else to take any part of the license exam for you is a suspension ground, just like taking it for someone else.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: What can happen to your driver's license if you give a false identity to a police officer?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: Falsely identifying yourself to a police officer can lead to suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: Using or lending your ID to buy tobacco or alcohol for which underage groups can suspend your license?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Using or lending a license, permit or ID card to buy tobacco for someone under eighteen or alcohol for someone under twenty-one can lead to suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: How can falling behind on court-ordered child support affect your Minnesota driver's license?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Failing to pay court-ordered child support can lead to a license suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: What happens if a check written for a state or license-agent fee bounces, and when does the suspension lift?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Paying a state or license agent fee with a bad check brings a suspension that is lifted once the check and related fees are fully paid.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: Which stronger withdrawal hits a driver who fails or refuses an alcohol or controlled-substance test?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Refusing a test for alcohol or a controlled substance, or failing that test, can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: What license withdrawal follows a conviction for impaired driving, vehicular manslaughter, or another crime behind the wheel?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: A conviction for driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol, or for manslaughter or another crime committed while driving, can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: What happens to your driving privileges after any felony conviction in which a motor vehicle was used?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: A conviction for a felony in which a motor vehicle was used can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: Exceeding what exact speed threshold on conviction can revoke your Minnesota driver's license?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: A conviction for driving faster than one hundred miles per hour can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: What license withdrawal can follow a conviction for fleeing a police officer?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: A conviction for fleeing a police officer can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: Failing to perform which three post-crash duties, especially after injury or death, can revoke your license?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: Failing to stop, identify yourself and give aid after a crash, especially one causing death or injury, can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: Which false statements about vehicle ownership or operation can trigger license revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: Lying under oath, signing a false legal document about a vehicle's ownership or operation, or making a false statement to DPS about it can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: How many jailable traffic pleas or bail forfeitures within one year can revoke your Minnesota license?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Pleading guilty or forfeiting bail for three violations in one year of Minnesota traffic laws or ordinances that require a jail sentence on conviction can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: How can driving or lending a vehicle lacking Minnesota no-fault insurance cost you your license?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: Driving a vehicle you know lacks no-fault insurance, or owning an uninsured vehicle and knowingly driving it or letting others drive it, can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: If you borrow a friend's car while knowing the owner carries zero no-fault insurance, what withdrawal threatens you?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: A misdemeanor conviction for driving while knowing the vehicle's owner lacked no-fault insurance is a revocation ground.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: Which severity of school-bus red-light conviction escalates penalty status to license revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: A gross misdemeanor conviction for failing to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: What license penalty can follow a conviction for possessing or selling controlled substances while operating a vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: A conviction for selling or possessing a controlled substance while operating a motor vehicle can lead to revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: When does an out-of-state driving offense count toward revoking your Minnesota license?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: A traffic offense in another state can count toward revocation in Minnesota when it would be grounds for revocation if committed here.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: What must you complete after a suspension period ends, and when is a brand-new license application required?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: After a suspension ends, privileges may be reinstated once all requirements are met, including paying the reinstatement fee, and you must apply for a new license if it expired or your name or address changed.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: Once a revocation term finishes, what notice items, testing step, and application are mandatory?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: After a revocation period ends you must meet every requirement on the withdrawal notice, show proper identification at the written or road test, and apply for a new license once testing is complete.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: Contrast getting your privileges back after a suspension versus returning from a revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Reinstatement after a suspension has requirements that include paying the reinstatement fee, while reinstatement after a revocation requires meeting every item on the withdrawal notice, testing with proper identification, and applying for a new license.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: Who may qualify for a Minnesota limited license, and what timing hurdle often applies first?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: A limited license may be issued to some drivers whose privileges are revoked or suspended, but only after they meet requirements that include any mandatory waiting period.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: Which four essential destinations or family errands may a Minnesota limited license cover?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: A limited license allows travel only to and from work, chemical dependency treatment or counseling, and a post-secondary school where you are enrolled, plus driving household dependents for medical, educational or nutritional needs.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: Can someone apply for a Minnesota limited license as an everyday starter card or use it for casual errands?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: A limited license is available only to some drivers whose privileges were suspended or revoked, never as a general license, and its trips are restricted to the listed purposes.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: Under what overarching rule does DPS cancel a license, and what disability or testing examples trigger it?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: A license may be canceled when you have no legal right to it, for example if a mental or physical disability makes you unable to drive safely or you fail a test DPS legally requests.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: How long does cancellation last if you put false or misleading facts on a Minnesota license application?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: Giving false or misleading information on a license application brings a cancellation of sixty days or until the correct information is provided, whichever is longer.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: Beyond disabilities, failed DPS retests, and false applications, what two legal grounds bring license cancellation?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: A license may also be canceled when cancellation is a legal punishment for a crime, or when you do not qualify for a license under Minnesota law.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: What central question decides most license cancellations, alongside specific criminal punishments?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: The core test for cancellation is whether you have a legal right to the license issued to you, though cancellation can also be the legal punishment for certain crimes.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: What book should you read and what four basic parts should you check regularly before driving on public roads?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Before driving on public roads, make sure the vehicle is fully equipped and in good condition, read the owner's manual, and regularly check the lights, wipers, horn and tires.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: What three setup and seating habits must happen right when you climb in before rolling?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: When you get in, adjust your seat and mirrors, seat passengers where they do not block your view or interfere with driving, and buckle up and have every passenger do the same.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: At least how many independent brake systems must every car and truck carry, and what are they?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Every car and truck must have at least two separate brake systems, such as the foot brake and the parking or emergency brake.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: How do front-and-rear bumper requirements differ between private passenger cars and pickups or vans?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Private passenger vehicles must have front and rear bumpers, while pickup trucks and vans need a front bumper plus either a rear bumper or reflectors.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: Under what condition may a pickup truck or van legally skip having a rear bumper?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: A private passenger car needs bumpers front and rear, but a pickup or van may use reflectors in place of a rear bumper as long as it has a front bumper.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Which audible warning device must every standard vehicle carry, and which three sound makers are off-limits?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: A vehicle must have a working horn, and bells, sirens and whistles are reserved for emergency vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: For what sole safety reason should you sound your horn, and what two casual uses are banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Use the horn to avoid a crash, never needlessly or to announce that you have arrived.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: From glass and exhaust to rear lamps and belts, what core items must a street-legal Minnesota car carry?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: The required-equipment diagram lists wipers, safety glass, a rearview mirror, horn, plates with a plate light, two ways to brake, high and low beam headlights, turn signals, bumpers, seat belts, a muffler, and a red taillight with red reflectors and a stop light.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Aside from motorcycles, what front headlamp and rear brake-lamp setup must every motor vehicle have?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Every motor vehicle except a motorcycle needs two white headlights that work on both high and low beam and red taillights that light up when the brake pedal is pressed.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: At least how many feet ahead must your high-beam headlights illuminate objects on the roadway?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: High beams must light up objects on the road at least three hundred fifty feet ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Why must you replace a cracked headlight housing even if the bulb inside still glows?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Damaged headlights must be replaced, because a cracked lens lets in moisture and dust that cut light output and add glare for other drivers.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: Up to what share of light output can grimy headlights lose, and how often should you wipe them?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Dirty headlights can cut light output by as much as seventy-five percent, so clean them as often as the windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: At least how often should a shop inspect your headlights to confirm proper aim?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Have the headlights inspected at least once a year to make sure they are aimed correctly.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: While daytime running lights turn on up front automatically, which two lighting sets stay completely off?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: Daytime running lights may switch on automatically to make a vehicle more visible, but taillights and parking lights do not come on automatically.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: During what hours, five weather types, and visibility distance must your full headlights stay switched on?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Headlights go on at sunset and stay on until sunrise, and also in rain, snow, hail, sleet or fog or whenever you cannot see the road at least five hundred feet ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: Besides headlamps and brake lamps, what rear tag lamp and directional bulbs must stay working?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: A white light must light the rear license plate so it can be seen at night, and every turn signal light on the vehicle must work.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: How do three hundred fifty feet and five hundred feet apply to different Minnesota headlight rules?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Two different distances apply to headlights: high beams must show objects at least three hundred fifty feet ahead, while headlights must be on any time you cannot see the road for at least five hundred feet.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: Why must you still twist your headlight switch on at sunset even when daytime running lights glow?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Daytime running lights can turn on by themselves, but taillights and parking lights never do, so at sunset you still switch on your headlights.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Which three categories of vehicles are the sole ones authorized to display blue lights in Minnesota?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Blue lights are limited to snowplows, road maintenance equipment and authorized emergency vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: Which six work, school, farm, or responder vehicle groups are permitted to run flashing lights?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: Flashing lights are limited to tow trucks, school buses, farm equipment, service vehicles, road maintenance equipment and authorized emergency vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: Which exact three vehicle types are authorized to run high-intensity strobe lamps?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Strobe lamps are limited to school buses, snow removal equipment and rural mail carrier vehicles.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: How do flashing-light rules and blue-light rules split between snowplows and tow trucks?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Blue lights belong only to snowplows, road maintenance equipment and emergency vehicles, while tow trucks, service vehicles and farm equipment may show flashing lights but not blue ones.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How do school buses and rural mail carrier vehicles compare across the flashing-light and strobe-lamp lists?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: School buses may use both flashing lights and strobe lamps, and rural mail carrier vehicles may use strobe lamps but are not on the flashing-light list.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: What noise rule makes a muffler mandatory, and what invisible deadly gas must you inspect exhaust pipes for?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Every motor vehicle needs a muffler to prevent sudden or prolonged loud noise such as popping or crackling, and the muffler should be checked regularly for carbon monoxide leaks.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: When must a vehicle add an extra side mirror beyond a standard inside rearview mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: Passenger vehicles need rearview mirrors, and a vehicle with no view through a rear window, such as a rental moving truck, or a pickup used for hauling needs an extra side mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Which two vehicle situations trigger Minnesota's requirement for an extra side mirror alongside the rearview mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Every passenger vehicle needs a rearview mirror, and a hauling pickup or a vehicle with no view through the rear window needs an extra side mirror as well.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: What does Minnesota require regarding seat belt presence, occupant use, and belt upkeep?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: Minnesota requires seat belts in all vehicles and requires everyone to wear them, and belts should be kept clean and in good condition for all occupants.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Why do airbags still need seat belts beside them, and why is cluttering your dashboard dangerous?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: Airbags work together with seat belts but do not keep occupants from being thrown out, and a cluttered dashboard can turn objects into hazards when airbags inflate.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: What six kinds of tire damage should you scan for often, and what trunk backup needs pressure checks too?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Look over your tires often for bulges, punctures, bald spots, cuts, cracks or uneven wear, and carry a good spare whose pressure you check often.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: How does tire traction on gravel or dirt roads compare with concrete or asphalt?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Tires grip gravel or dirt roads less well than concrete or asphalt.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: Where do you look up your car's recommended tire pressure—and what printed number should you ignore as a target?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: The recommended tire pressure is on a sticker inside the driver's door or in the owner's manual, not the number printed on the tire sidewall.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: At what two times is checking tire pressure accurate before adding or bleeding air?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: Check tire pressure before driving or at least three hours after driving, then add or release air until the gauge matches the recommended number.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Why is inflating to the number molded onto the rubber sidewall a classic maintenance mistake?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: The tire pressure to aim for is the one on the driver's door sticker or in the owner's manual, while the sidewall number is not the target.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: Why must you wait at least three hours after a trip rather than checking tire pressure right at a highway stop?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: Tire pressure is checked either before you drive or only once at least three hours have passed since driving, not right after a trip.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: Below what exact fraction of an inch does tire tread become illegal in Minnesota?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: A tire is illegal when its tread is less than one-sixteenth of an inch deep.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: How do you place a penny into your tire groove, and what sight proves legal tread remains?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: In the penny test you place Lincoln's head into the shallowest tread groove, and if the tread covers any part of his head the tire is legal and safe.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: How does Abraham Lincoln's head on a penny connect to Minnesota's one-sixteenth-inch tread floor?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: The legal tread limit is one-sixteenth of an inch, and the penny test passes only when tread covers part of Lincoln's head.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: What six glass conditions—plus hanging items—are illegal across your windshield and windows?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: The view through the windshield and windows must not be blocked by cracks, discoloration, steam, frost, ice or snow, and nothing may hang between the driver and the windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: Where may state stickers, toll tags, navigation screens, and driver-monitoring sensors legally sit?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: Stickers allowed by state law, such as park stickers, safety inspection stickers and toll devices, may go on the windshield, navigation units may mount near its bottom, and driver monitoring equipment may sit just behind, above or below the rearview mirror.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: How does Minnesota treat authorized toll tags and park stickers compared with items hanging from your mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: Toll devices and park or inspection stickers allowed by state law may go on the windshield, but objects may not hang between the driver and the windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: What two optical effects may never be added to a windshield by any film or treatment?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: A windshield may not be made of, covered with or treated with any material that makes it more reflective or lets less light through.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: What two ratings must appear on the label of side or rear window tint applied since August nineteen eighty-five?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: Side or rear window tint applied after Aug. one, nineteen eighty-five must be labeled with the percentage of light it transmits and reflects.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: Which specific windows and vehicle types are the sole ones allowed tint darker than fifty percent or shinier than twenty?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: Tint that transmits less than fifty percent or reflects more than twenty percent of light is allowed only on a pickup's rear window or on the rear and side windows of a van, limousine or funeral home vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: Even on vans, limos, or pickups allowed dark rear glass, is sub-fifty-percent tint ever legal on the windshield?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: Dark tint that lets through less than fifty percent of light or reflects more than twenty percent is limited to pickup rear windows and to the rear and side windows of vans, limousines and funeral home vehicles, never the windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: Which two clearing systems must keep a glass windshield and cabin windows free of rain, steam, and frost?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: A vehicle with a glass windshield must have working wipers, and defrosters are needed to keep the windshield and windows free of steam and frost.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: Why does Minnesota require fenders or wheel guards over passenger-vehicle tires?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: Passenger vehicles need fenders or other wheel guards so the tires do not throw water, dirt and debris into the air.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.front: What three maintenance habits keep your vehicle sipping less fuel?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.expected_back: Save fuel by keeping the engine tuned, the tires properly inflated and the recommended grade of motor oil in the engine.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.front: From trip planning and trunk weight to highway gears, what six behind-the-wheel habits stretch fuel farthest?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.expected_back: Drive efficiently by combining errands, avoiding speeding, hard acceleration and sudden braking, obeying the speed limit, removing heavy items you do not need, and using cruise control and overdrive on the highway.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.front: What five travel alternatives does the manual recommend whenever practical to cut fuel use?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.expected_back: Public transportation, carpools, ridesharing, biking or walking are recommended whenever possible to save fuel.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: What physical check outside the car and four-way scan inside come before shifting into reverse?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Before you back up, walk around the vehicle to be sure nothing is behind it, and look to the front, both sides and the rear.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: Where must your eyes stay locked the entire time you reverse, and into which lane do you back?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Keep watching through the rear window the whole time you back up rather than relying only on mirrors or a back-up camera, and back slowly into the closest lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: What is the maximum legal distance between your curbside tires and the curb when parallel parked?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: When parallel parked, the wheels nearest the edge of the road may be no more than twelve inches from the curb.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: After parallel parking, how should you leave your front wheels, gear selector, and brake set—and why?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: After parallel parking, point the front wheels toward the curb or shoulder, shift into park and set the parking brake, so a vehicle that starts rolling heads for the curb rather than a traffic lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: Which three pedestrian or corner zones are flatly off-limits for parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Parking is forbidden inside an intersection and on a crosswalk or sidewalk.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: Within how many feet of an intersection crosswalk is parking illegal in Minnesota?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: You may not park within twenty feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: Within how many feet of a roadside stop post, flashing beacon, or traffic signal is parking banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: You may not park within thirty feet of a flashing light, stop sign or traffic control signal standing beside a public road.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: Within how many feet of the nearest rail at a railroad crossing is parking illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: You may not park within fifty feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant is parking prohibited in Minnesota?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: You may not park within ten feet of a fire hydrant.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How do ten, twenty, thirty, and fifty feet match up across Minnesota's four no-parking curb buffers?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: The four no-parking distances on one list are ten feet from a fire hydrant, twenty feet from a crosswalk at an intersection, thirty feet from a roadside flashing light, stop sign or signal, and fifty feet from the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: Which three structural or access chokepoints also ban parking completely?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Parking is also banned on any bridge, inside a highway tunnel and across the street end of a driveway.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: What do we call stopping in the travel lane alongside a curb-parked car, and is it legal?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Stopping on the traffic side of a vehicle already parked at a curb or highway edge is called double parking and is not allowed.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: What four painted, posted, work-site, or postal curb spots also forbid parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: You also may not park beside a yellow-painted curb, where official No Parking signs stand, next to or opposite an excavation or obstacle if you would block traffic, or in front of mailboxes where local rules forbid it.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Before swinging open a roadside car door, whom must you scan for and how long may the door stay open?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: When stopped or parked at the roadside, check for approaching vehicles, motorcycles, bicyclists and pedestrians before opening any door, and keep a traffic-side door open only as long as loading or unloading needs.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: Which direction do you turn your front wheels whenever parking facing downhill?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: When a parked vehicle faces downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb or the road's shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking facing uphill beside a curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: When a parked vehicle faces uphill next to a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Which way do your front wheels turn when parked facing uphill along a road with no curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: When a parked vehicle faces uphill where there is no curb, turn the wheels toward the shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Across all downhill and uphill parking setups, which lone setup turns wheels away from the road edge?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: Downhill with or without a curb and uphill without a curb, the wheels turn toward the edge of the road; only uphill with a curb do they turn away from it.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: How do you align and space your car beside the lead parked vehicle to begin parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: To start parallel parking, stop beside the car ahead of the space, level with it and roughly one and a half feet away.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What three steering cuts guide you into the center of a parallel parking space?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: In the parallel parking steps you turn the wheel sharply right and back slowly, turn sharply left once clear of the car ahead while still backing, then turn sharply right and pull toward the curb in the middle of the space.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: What front and rear lamps—and minimum visibility footage—must mark a vehicle parked along a highway at night?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: A vehicle parked on a highway at night, or whenever lights are needed, must show at least one white or amber front light and one red taillight, each visible from at least five hundred feet.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: Where must you place a parked car on a state highway, and what if mechanical failure leaves it immovable?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: On a state highway or freeway, move a parked vehicle off the main part of the road, and if it cannot be moved, put out visible markers or signals so other drivers are not harmed.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: Which warning lights should a highway-parked car run, and what beam setting applies if headlights stay on?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: A vehicle parked on the highway should use parking lights or hazard warning lights to alert others, with any headlights set to low beam.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: Who bears responsibility for passenger safety, belt compliance, and age-matched child restraints inside your car?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: As the driver you are responsible for every passenger's safety, so insist that everyone buckles up and that children ride in a restraint suited to their age.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Which seats require belts in Minnesota, and can police pull you over solely for an unbuckled belt?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: Every person in the vehicle, front and back, must wear a properly adjusted and fastened seat belt, and an officer may stop a driver for a seat belt violation alone.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: Why does the manual call seat belts the single most important safety feature in your vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: The seat belt is called the most important safety equipment in the vehicle, and it keeps occupants from being thrown out, which usually brings death or serious injury.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: How many times more likely are you to be killed or injured when riding without a seat belt?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Riding without a seat belt makes you four times more likely to be killed or injured in a crash.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: At speeds as low as how many miles per hour can an unbelted rider die in a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: An unbelted occupant can die in a crash at speeds as low as twelve miles per hour

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: What reverse, seating-capacity, and medical exceptions exist inside Minnesota's seat-belt statute?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: The belt law does not apply to someone driving a passenger vehicle in reverse, to a rider whose seat belts are all taken by other passengers, or to a person holding a doctor's written certificate for medical reasons.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Under what strict speed ceiling are frequent-stop delivery or utility workers excused from buckling?
