sec12-card-sec12-F40.expected_back: Carbon monoxide poisoning is most common in winter, can build up in a garage even with the door fully open, and can knock a person unconscious within a few minutes.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.front: Where should you warm up your vehicle, and which two idling habits must you avoid?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.expected_back: To lower carbon monoxide risk, warm up the vehicle in the driveway rather than the garage, avoid sitting in an idling vehicle, and do not idle when stuck in snow or mud.

sec12-card-sec12-R33.front: Which window habits and exhaust-system check keep carbon monoxide out of your cabin on everyday drives?
sec12-card-sec12-R33.expected_back: Also avoid driving with every window shut, keep the exhaust system free of leaks and blockages, and lower the windows now and then for fresh air.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: What is Minnesota's baseline rule on driving while impaired by alcohol or any other substance?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: It is illegal to drive on Minnesota roads while impaired by alcohol or any other substance.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Which person dies most frequently in alcohol-related crashes, and which demographic drives impaired most often?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: In alcohol-related crashes the impaired driver is the one most often killed, and young men are more likely than others to drive impaired.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: How does alcohol involvement correlate with the severity of Minnesota traffic crashes?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Drinking and driving is a serious problem in Minnesota, and alcohol use is strongly linked to how severe traffic crashes are.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: Beyond illegal street drugs, which pharmacy and home items count under Minnesota's impaired-driving ban?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Minnesota law bans driving while impaired by controlled or intoxicating substances, which include illegal drugs, prescription and over-the-counter drugs such as cold medicines, and household products.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: How does drug impairment compare with alcohol danger, and what physical and legal fallout can follow?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Drug impairment is as dangerous as alcohol impairment, and drugs can cause drowsiness and slow your response to driving conditions, leading to crashes, arrest, fines and jail.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: Why can a harmless-feeling legal medication suddenly wreck your driving if combined with a drink?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: A legal drug that does not impair you alone can have a powerful intoxicating effect when mixed with alcohol, so the safest rule is not to mix drugs with driving at all.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: Under what medical guidance and label habits may you legally drive with a prescribed medication?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: You may possess and use a prescribed drug if your doctor tells you it will not affect your ability to drive safely, and you should follow warning labels and the doctor's orders.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Why should you never pop stimulants to mask road drowsiness, and what actually fixes fatigue?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: Never use a drug to hide fatigue; the only cure for being tired is rest.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: What drug class is alcohol, what term names its blood share, and how many drinks start impairment?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: Alcohol is a depressant, the amount in your blood is called the alcohol concentration, and your driving ability is impaired after just one drink.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: How does alcohol trick your self-assessment and erode four basic defensive driving habits?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: Alcohol makes you misjudge how impaired you are, so you may speed, misjudge stopping distances, skip your seat belt and stop driving defensively.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: What three changes does alcohol inflict on eye movement, side awareness, and clarity?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: Alcohol narrows the range of eye movement and reduces peripheral vision, and high alcohol concentrations can blur vision.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: How does alcohol degrade your reflexes, steering path, sensory intake, and body control?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: Alcohol slows reaction time, makes drivers over-steer and weave, dulls perception of sights and sounds, and weakens coordination, balance and attention.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: Which four common beverage servings hold roughly the same amount of pure alcohol?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.memory_hook: Twelve beer, five wine, nine-cooler, cocktail
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: About the same amount of alcohol is usually found in a twelve-ounce beer, a five-ounce glass of wine, a nine-ounce wine cooler and a typical mixed drink.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: Why can counting glasses mislead you on mixed cocktails and different beers?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: Mixed drinks may hold more than the standard one point five ounces of alcohol, and the alcohol content of beers can vary by as much as forty percent.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: How do you convert a bottle's proof number into its actual percentage of alcohol?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: A drink's proof is twice its alcohol percentage, so eighty-proof whiskey is forty percent alcohol.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: What happens in your bloodstream whenever you consume more than one standard drink per hour?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: Drinking more than one standard drink per hour raises your alcohol concentration.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: What is the sole way to bring alcohol concentration down, how fast does it clear, and do coffee or showers help?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: The only way to lower your alcohol concentration is to wait, since the body generally clears about one drink per hour and coffee, exercise or cold showers do not speed it up.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: How much alcohol does the liver oxidize, and how does the remaining five percent leave your body?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: The liver removes ninety-five percent of alcohol by oxidation, and the rest leaves through breathing, sweating and urination.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: If two people weigh the exact same, why does the one with higher body fat hit a higher alcohol concentration?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: Someone with a higher share of body fat than another person of the same weight reaches a higher alcohol concentration from the same amount of alcohol.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: Which seven biological or situational traits make alcohol hit people differently, even the same person on different days?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: Alcohol affects people very differently because of age, gender, body weight, mood, food intake, metabolism and genetics, and even the same person can react differently from one occasion to the next.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: How does muscle-versus-fat tissue explain one reason alcohol affects men and women differently?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.memory_hook: Muscle keeps more out of blood
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: Alcohol affects men and women differently, partly because men usually carry more muscle, and muscle takes alcohol into the bloodstream less readily than fat does.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: What simple rule separates drinking from driving, and when must you lock in your plan?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: The safest policy is simple: if you will drink, do not drive, and if you will drive, do not drink, and make your plan while you are still sober.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: What five practical options replace impaired driving for yourself or an impaired friend?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Alternatives to driving impaired include a designated driver who does not drink, a taxi or rideshare, a ride from a friend or relative, staying overnight, and taking the keys from an impaired friend.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: Why must your ride home from social drinking be settled before taking your very first drink?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: Social drinking frequently leads to impaired driving, and because alcohol impairs judgment you should decide how you will get home before you start drinking.

sec14-card-sec14-R20.front: At what minimum age may a person legally purchase and consume alcohol in Minnesota?
sec14-card-sec14-R20.expected_back: The legal age to buy and drink alcohol in Minnesota is twenty-one.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: Does a vehicle have to be moving for a DWI arrest, and what standard and commercial thresholds apply?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: A person in control of a moving or parked vehicle with an alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent or higher, or zero point zero four percent in a commercial vehicle, can be arrested for DWI.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: How low can a noncommercial driver's alcohol concentration be and still bring a DWI arrest?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Even at zero point zero four percent a driver can face DWI arrest when an officer can prove alcohol caused the driving errors.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: Compare Minnesota's DWI alcohol thresholds for general drivers, commercial rigs, and drivers committing alcohol-caused errors?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: Three different limits appear on this page: zero point zero eight percent for most drivers, zero point zero four percent for commercial drivers, and zero point zero four percent for any driver whose errors an officer proves were caused by alcohol.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: When an officer has probable cause to suspect impairment, which three tests fall under implied consent, and what is refusal?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Under the implied consent law, if an officer has probable cause to believe you are impaired while driving or in physical control of a vehicle, you must take a blood, breath or urine test, and refusing is a crime.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: Which three arrest, roadside-breath, or crash situations authorize an officer to request an alcohol test?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: An officer may ask for a test when you are under arrest for DWI, refuse or fail a preliminary breath test, or are in an alcohol-related crash causing injury, damage or death.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: Beyond highway cars and trucks, which recreational machines fall under Minnesota's DWI and implied-consent statutes?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: The DWI and implied consent laws also apply to off-road recreational vehicles and motorboats.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: How many years of license revocation follow refusing an implied-consent test, and what sets the duration?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: Refusing the implied consent test leads to a revocation lasting from one to six years, with the length set by how many offenses are already on your record.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: How does a roadside preliminary breath test differ in courtroom use from the post-arrest blood, breath, or urine test?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: A roadside preliminary breath test only indicates your alcohol level and has limited use as court evidence, while the blood, breath or urine test required after arrest can be used as evidence.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: Pair Minnesota's pre-arrest breath screen and post-arrest chemical test with each test's main job?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: The roadside preliminary breath test helps the officer judge your alcohol level before arrest, while the blood, breath or urine test after arrest is the one used as evidence.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: How can blowing zero on a roadside preliminary breath test protect a sober driver having a medical episode?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: A preliminary breath test can help a driver who seems intoxicated but is not, because some medical conditions look like intoxication, and officers get medical help for drivers who are ill.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.front: Which two separate penalty tracks hit every impaired-driving offense, and what shapes their severity?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.expected_back: Each impaired driving offense carries criminal penalties in addition to administrative sanctions, depending on the arrest situation, prior violations and criminal record.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: What dollar fee, application step, and possible starter device apply after an alcohol-related revocation?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: An alcohol-related revocation brings a six hundred eighty dollars reinstatement fee, a new license application and possibly enrollment in the Ignition Interlock Device Program.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: Which five record, concentration, passenger, age, or roadside factors trigger harsher Minnesota DWI penalties?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: Penalties are harsher with prior DWI arrests, an alcohol concentration of zero point one six percent or more, a child under sixteen in the vehicle, a driver under twenty-one, or a refused preliminary breath test.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: How many days does a temporary license last before revocation kicks in after failing at point-oh-eight or refusing?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: A driver found at zero point zero eight percent or more, or who refuses testing, may get a seven-day temporary license, after which the license is revoked.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: What revocation length, guilty-plea reduction, and jail or fine ceiling apply to a first DWI?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: A first offense brings at least a ninety-day revocation, or thirty days with a guilty plea to DWI, and a penalty listed as ninety days in jail, a one thousand dollars fine or both.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: How long must a first-time DWI offender wait for a work permit, and what alcohol reading blocks it completely?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: After a first offense no work permit is issued until fifteen days of revocation have passed and reinstatement requirements are met, and none at all if the alcohol concentration was zero point one six percent or more.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: What revocation floor, jail-or-fine maximum, and license-plate action hit a second DWI within ten years?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: A second offense within ten years of the first brings at least a one-year revocation, a penalty listed as one year in jail, a three thousand dollars fine or both, and impounded license plates.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.front: Step through Minnesota's minimum revocation floors for a first, second, and third DWI within ten years?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.expected_back: Revocation minimums climb by offense: at least ninety days for a first offense, at least one year for a second within ten years, and at least three years for a third within ten years.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: Which license, treatment, interlock, and vehicle-loss penalties hit a third DWI within ten years?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: A third offense within ten years brings at least three years without a license, cancellation, a chemical use assessment, required ignition interlock, and a forfeited vehicle with impounded plates.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.front: What custody or pre-trial release conditions can accompany a third DWI offense?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.expected_back: A third offense can also bring jail or maximum bail with electronic monitoring.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: Which three ten-year arrest counts or prior convictions elevate a Minnesota DWI to a felony charge?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: A fourth DWI arrest within ten years, a prior felony DWI conviction, or a criminal vehicular homicide conviction while impaired can lead to a felony DWI charge.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: What maximum prison term, conditional-release tail, and dollar fine can follow a Minnesota felony DWI?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: A felony DWI can be punished by as much as seven years in prison, followed by five years of conditional release, and a fourteen thousand dollars fine.

sec14-card-sec14-R19.front: How long can a fourth DWI strip your license, and what is required before it ever returns?
sec14-card-sec14-R19.expected_back: A fourth offense can mean four years without a license, and the license comes back only after rehabilitation and the other reinstatement steps are complete.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: At what breath alcohol concentration does an ignition interlock device block your engine's starter?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: An ignition interlock device on the vehicle's starter will not let the vehicle start if your breath shows an alcohol concentration of zero point zero two percent or more.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.front: Rank Minnesota's interlock lockout cutoff against the commercial and general DWI thresholds?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.expected_back: The interlock blocks starting at zero point zero two percent, which is lower than both the zero point zero four commercial limit and the zero point zero eight general limit.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.front: How does ignition interlock shift from optional to mandatory across first, second, and third DWIs?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.memory_hook: Optional first, possible second, required third
sec14-card-sec14-R15.expected_back: Ignition interlock is optional after a first offense, possibly required after a second, and required after a third.

sec14-card-sec14-R18.front: How can a first-time offender who blew zero-point-one-six or higher regain driving privileges when work permits are barred?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.expected_back: First-time offenders with an alcohol concentration of zero point one six or above may choose the Ignition Interlock Device Program to regain their driving privileges.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: For how many years must drivers canceled as inimical to public safety use ignition interlock to earn full privileges?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Drivers whose licenses are canceled and denied as inimical to public safety must use the ignition interlock for three to six years to regain full privileges.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: How much alcohol may a driver under twenty-one have in their system, and what suspensions hit first and second convictions?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: A driver under twenty-one may not drive with any detectable alcohol, and a conviction brings a thirty-day suspension, or one hundred eighty days for a second conviction.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.front: What happens to a commercial driver caught operating a commercial rig at point-oh-four, or with any detectable alcohol below it?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.expected_back: A commercial driver loses the commercial license for at least one year on a first offense such as driving a commercial vehicle at zero point zero four or more, and a detectable level below zero point zero four means twenty-four hours out of service.

sec14-card-sec14-R21.front: Which five first-offense violations, including in a personal car at point-oh-eight, strip a CDL for at least one year?
sec14-card-sec14-R21.expected_back: A commercial license holder loses that license for at least one year on a first offense such as driving any vehicle at zero point zero eight or more, refusing a blood, breath or urine test, driving under a controlled substance, leaving a crash scene, or using a vehicle for a felony.

sec14-card-sec14-R22.front: When does a CDL disqualification stretch to three years, and which offenses erase a CDL permanently?
sec14-card-sec14-R22.expected_back: If the offense happens in a placarded hazardous materials vehicle the commercial license is lost for at least three years, and a second offense or using a commercial vehicle for a controlled substance felony means permanent loss.

sec14-card-sec14-R23.front: If a CDL holder is arrested for DWI in their family car, can they get a limited work permit to drive a commercial rig?
sec14-card-sec14-R23.expected_back: A commercial license holder arrested for impaired driving in a passenger vehicle cannot get a work permit for a commercial vehicle during the withdrawal period.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.front: How does Minnesota treat driving while impaired by cannabis, low-potency hemp edibles, synthetic cannabinoids, or THC?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.expected_back: Driving under the influence of cannabis products, lower-potency hemp edibles, hemp-derived products, artificially derived cannabinoids or THC is illegal.

sec14-card-sec14-F37.front: May anyone smoke, vape, or consume cannabis flower or hemp-derived products inside a vehicle on a public road?
sec14-card-sec14-F37.expected_back: Using cannabis flower or any cannabis or hemp-derived product in a vehicle on a street or highway is illegal.

sec14-card-sec14-F38.front: Where must opened or partly used cannabis or hemp packages ride in a car, and which dash spot is banned?
sec14-card-sec14-F38.expected_back: Opened or partly emptied cannabis or hemp-derived products must ride in the trunk, or in an area not normally occupied if there is no trunk, never in the glove or utility compartment.

sec14-card-sec14-R24.front: Under what sole storage condition is an opened cannabis or hemp package legal inside a private vehicle on the road?
sec14-card-sec14-R24.expected_back: An opened or partly emptied package of cannabis or hemp-derived products is illegal in a private vehicle on a street or highway unless stored in the trunk or another unoccupied area.

sec14-card-sec14-R25.front: Does stepping away from or lending out your car excuse you as owner if unsealed cannabis sits in the cabin on a street?
sec14-card-sec14-R25.expected_back: When the owner is not in the vehicle, it is still illegal for the owner to keep or allow opened cannabis or hemp-derived packages in it on a street or highway.

sec14-card-sec14-F39.front: May either the driver or a passenger drink or hold an open alcoholic container in a vehicle on a public road?
sec14-card-sec14-F39.expected_back: You may not drink or have an open alcoholic beverage container inside a vehicle on a public street or highway, and you may not allow passengers to do so either.

sec14-card-sec14-F40.front: Which three actions involving controlled substances inside a motor vehicle does Minnesota prohibit?
sec14-card-sec14-F40.expected_back: Using, possessing or selling controlled substances in a motor vehicle is prohibited.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: What does Minnesota law allow motorcycles to do between adjacent lanes, and what must drivers avoid doing?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: In Minnesota a motorcycle may legally ride or pass in the space between your vehicle and a vehicle in the next lane, and you must not get in the way of its safe movement.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Where are you most likely to spot motorcycle lane sharing, and how else may riders pass slow traffic?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: You will most often see motorcycle lane sharing at a stoplight as riders move up to the front, but riders may also pass slow traffic on your left or right while using part of your lane.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: Since riding between lanes is legal for motorcyclists in Minnesota, how should a car driver respond?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: A motorcycle sharing your lane or riding between lanes is acting legally, so the driver's duty is to leave it room rather than block it.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: What active hazard do flashing red lights atop a school bus signal to nearby drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Flashing red lights on a school bus tell drivers that students are boarding or leaving the bus.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: What is the closest distance you may stop from a school bus displaying flashing red lights?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, you must stop your vehicle no closer than twenty feet from the bus.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: Do you still have to halt for a school bus with flashing red lights if its side stop arm stays folded in?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: You must stop for a school bus showing flashing red lights even when its stop arm has not swung out.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Under what single road-and-direction combination are you not required to stop for a bus's flashing red lights?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: The one exception to stopping for a school bus with flashing red lights is when you are on a divided highway and traveling in the opposite direction.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Which two financial and licensing penalties can hit if you blow past a school bus flashing red lights?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Failing to stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing can bring fines and a suspension of your driver's license.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: Pair Minnesota's school-bus stopping distance with the lone highway situation where oncoming traffic keeps rolling?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: Upon seeing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights, you must stop at least twenty feet away unless you are traveling in the opposite direction on a divided highway.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: Between the stop arm and the flashing red roof lights, which signal legally triggers your twenty-foot school-bus stop?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: The trigger for stopping at a school bus is the flashing red lights, not the stop arm, so a bus whose arm stays folded still requires you to stop at least twenty feet away.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: Which three traffic patterns require extra alertness in a work zone, and why are crews and machines so exposed?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: In a work zone, stay alert for distracted driving, zipper merges and changed lane patterns, because crews work very close to moving traffic and large construction vehicles can move unpredictably.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: Name the trio of hazards grouped together in Minnesota's work-zone safety reminder?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: The work-zone reminder names three hazards to watch for together: distracted driving, zipper merges and lanes that have been shifted or altered.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: How does Minnesota law treat interfering with or obstructing a Driver and Vehicle Services employee?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Interfering with or obstructing the work of a Driver and Vehicle Services employee is a crime under Minnesota Statute six hundred nine point five zero, Subdivision five.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Which five customer behaviors are banned inside a DVS office, and what two actions follow if someone crosses the line?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: Driver and Vehicle Services does not tolerate disruptive behavior or harassment, obscene or abusive language or gestures, interfering with services, refusing staff instructions, or violent conduct; a customer who does any of these is asked to leave and police are called.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Are interfering with DVS staff and obstructing them covered by separate laws or one shared criminal statute?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: Interfering with a DVS employee and obstructing a DVS employee are both described as crimes under the same statute, Minnesota Statute six hundred nine point five zero, Subdivision five.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: How does the Commissioner frame driving, and which three core road duties protect everyone around you?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: The Commissioner's message reminds drivers that driving is a privilege that carries a responsibility to everyone else on the road: buckle up, obey speed laws and never drive under the influence of alcohol.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: What two advantages does finishing the DVS online pre-application give you before stepping into an office?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: The pre-application in DVS online services lets you finish a large part of your license application before the visit and lists the documents each license type requires, which shortens your time at the counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Within how many days before your visit should you start the online pre-application, and what must you carry in?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Begin the online pre-application no more than thirty days before your office visit so you do not have to fill out a paper application, and bring the confirmation page together with every document it lists.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: Which four languages does drive.mn.gov's virtual assistant support, and what can you track inside a MyDVS account?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Driver and Vehicle Services offers a virtual assistant at drive.mn.gov in English, Spanish, Somali and Hmong, and a MyDVS account lets you follow your license and registration information online.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: What does the thirty-day DVS window actually control, and what licensing milestone should you never confuse it with?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: The thirty-day window governs when you start the online pre-application before an office visit, and the manual ties staying inside it to avoiding a paper application; it is not a permit holding period.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: What scheduling and online preparation steps belong on your Class D written-test checklist, and on what timeline?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: Before the Class D written test you need a scheduled test appointment, and the checklist says to finish the online pre-application at dps.mn.gov slash mydvs within the thirty days before that appointment, not earlier.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which three personal or payment items do you need ready alongside your appointment for the written test?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: For the written test, bring the required identification and money for the fees, and know your Social Security number if you are eligible to have one.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: What is the minimum age for an applicant under eighteen to sit for Minnesota's written knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: An applicant younger than eighteen must be at least fifteen years old to take the written test.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: Which two colored driver-education cards qualify an under-eighteen applicant for the written test, and what does each prove?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen brings either a Blue Card, showing classroom instruction is finished and behind-the-wheel training is scheduled, or a Pink Card, showing enrollment in a concurrent driver education course with the first fifteen classroom hours completed.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: Alongside age fifteen and a Blue or Pink Card, what optional certificate and adult signature rule apply to teen written testers?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: Written test applicants under eighteen must be at least fifteen, bring a Blue Card or Pink Card, bring the Supplemental Parental Curriculum completion certificate if completed, and have an approved adult sign the application with documentation when not a parent.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: Contrast the exact driver-ed milestone behind a Blue Card versus a Pink Card when heading to the written test?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: The Blue Card shows classroom instruction is complete and behind-the-wheel training is arranged, while the Pink Card shows enrollment in a concurrent course with the first fifteen classroom hours done; either one admits a teen to the written test.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: Why must you separate age fifteen on the written-test checklist from the road-test checklist age?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: A teen must be at least fifteen years old for the written test, a different age from the road test minimum on the next checklist page.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Besides your appointment and pre-application, who must accompany you to the road test or risk cancellation?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: For the road test you need an appointment, a completed online pre-application, and a licensed driver who comes with you; without that licensed driver the road test may be cancelled.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: Which driving credential do you hand directly to the examiner when checking in for your road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: At the road test you hand your valid instruction permit to the examiner.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: Which doors, restraints, lights, and registration rules must your road-test vehicle satisfy?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: The road test vehicle must be safe: doors open from inside and outside, seat belts work, and the headlights, taillights, brake lights and turn signals all function, with registration that is current or covered by a sixty-day permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: Which three forms of vehicle insurance proof are accepted at the Minnesota road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Proof of insurance for the road test vehicle can be the original card from the insurance company, the policy declaration page, or electronic proof from the insurer's website or shown on a device.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: Does Minnesota accept electronic proof of insurance displayed on a device when you check in for the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: Electronic proof of insurance from the insurer's website or on a device is accepted for the road test, alongside the original card or the policy declaration page.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What minimum age and driver-education completion card must an under-eighteen applicant bring on road-test day?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: A road test applicant under eighteen must be at least sixteen years old and bring the White Card showing driver education was completed.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: For how long must a teen hold a permit before the road test, and which convictions reset eligibility?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: A road test applicant under eighteen must have held an instruction permit for the past six months with no conviction for a moving violation or for an alcohol or controlled substance violation.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: What document proves road-test eligibility if part or all of a teen's six permit months happened in another state?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: If some or all of a teen's six months of permit driving took place in another state, the teen brings a certified driving record from that state to show eligibility for the provisional license.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: Which two parent-signed items must an under-eighteen applicant present at the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: A road test applicant under eighteen brings a Supervised Driving Log that is filled in and signed by a parent or guardian, plus the parental approval signature on the application.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: How long must an eighteen-year-old hold an instruction permit before the road test compared with someone nineteen or older?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: An eighteen-year-old road test applicant must have held the instruction permit for at least six months, while an applicant aged nineteen or older needs at least three months.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: Why won't a Blue Card or Pink Card get a sixteen-year-old into the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: A teen must be at least sixteen years old for the road test and brings the White Card, which certifies completed driver education, rather than the Blue or Pink enrollment card.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: Group all road-test applicants by whether they owe six months or three months on an instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: Permit holding time before the road test is six months for applicants under eighteen and for eighteen-year-olds, but only three months for applicants aged nineteen or older.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: What extra violation-free requirement attaches to a teen's six-month permit hold on the road-test checklist?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: For teens the six months of permit holding must also be free of convictions for moving violations and alcohol or controlled substance violations, a condition the adult checklist lines do not repeat.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: What two status requirements must your driver's license meet whenever you drive on Minnesota public streets or highways?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Driving on Minnesota public streets or highways requires a driver's license that is valid and not expired.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: Which four steps in order must someone complete if they have never been licensed anywhere?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Someone who has never held a license anywhere must pass a written test and a vision test, get an instruction permit and then pass a road test.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: Which tests are required before reapplying if your Minnesota license expired between one and five years ago?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: A Minnesota license that expired more than one year but less than five years ago means you must pass both the vision test and the written test, and only then apply for a new license.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: What does a new resident aged twenty-one or older holding a valid U.S., territory, or Canadian license need to get a Minnesota license?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: A new resident aged twenty-one or older from another state, certain U.S. territories or Canada who shows a valid, unexpired license gets a Minnesota license with only a vision test and an application, and no written or road test.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: How do required tests change for that adult new resident if their former license expired under one year ago versus over one year?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: For that new resident, a former license expired less than one year means passing the written test, and one expired more than one year means passing both the written and road tests.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Within how many days after becoming a Minnesota resident must a regular driver versus a commercial driver get licensed here?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: A new Minnesota resident has sixty days to get a Minnesota license or permit, while a commercial driver has thirty days.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: Which tests must a newcomer moving from outside the U.S. and Canada pass even with a valid home-country license?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: A newcomer from a country other than the U.S. or Canada must pass the written, vision and road tests even with a valid license from the former country.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: What must you do with all other driver's licenses and ID cards you hold before DVS issues your Minnesota license?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: You cannot obtain your Minnesota driver's license until you present every other driver's license and identification card you hold to DVS.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: At what minimum age may a nonresident visitor drive in Minnesota using a valid home-state or home-country license?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: A nonresident at least fifteen years old with a valid license from the home state or country may drive in Minnesota without a Minnesota license.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Under what age, vehicle-registration, and day-limit rules may someone from a country that does not license drivers drive here?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: A nonresident at least eighteen years old from a country that does not license drivers may drive a vehicle registered there for the current year in Minnesota for up to ninety days in a calendar year without a license or permit.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Contrast the testing rules for a valid-license newcomer from Canada against one from outside the U.S. and Canada?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: A newcomer from another state, certain U.S. territories or Canada can skip the written and road tests with a valid license, but a newcomer from any other country takes all three tests even with a valid foreign license.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: Compare the newcomer licensing deadline for a regular Class D driver against a commercial driver?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: The newcomer deadline is sixty days for a regular license but only thirty days for a commercial license after becoming a Minnesota resident.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How does the minimum age for a validly licensed visitor compare with the age and cap for a visitor from a non-licensing country?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: A visiting nonresident needs to be only fifteen with a valid home license, but the no-license exception for drivers from countries that do not license drivers requires age eighteen and is capped at ninety days per calendar year.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: Which three categories of farm, winter, or rail equipment can be operated without a Minnesota driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: No Minnesota license is needed to drive a farm tractor or farm implement temporarily on a public road, to operate a snowmobile, or to run a locomotive or other on-track rail equipment.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Which three identification, testing, or comprehension failures bar someone from receiving a Minnesota license?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: You cannot be licensed if you fail to show proper identification, fail any required test, or cannot read and understand official road signs or state traffic laws.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: Below what age will Minnesota refuse to issue any driver's license or instruction permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.memory_hook: Zero permits or licenses under fifteen
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: No license or instruction permit is issued to anyone under fifteen years of age.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: What must an applicant under eighteen prove to get licensed if they do not hold a valid out-of-state license?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen without a valid license from another state cannot be licensed unless they present proof of completing an approved driver education course.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: Below how many months of permit holding is a license refused to someone eighteen or younger versus nineteen or older?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: A license is refused to an applicant eighteen or younger who has held an instruction permit for under six months, and to one nineteen or older who has held it for under three months.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: How does an active suspension, revocation, or cancellation affect applying for a new license?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: A suspended or revoked license blocks a new license until every reinstatement requirement is met, and a canceled license also blocks issuance.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: For what disability, safety, or court-ordered reasons can a Minnesota license be refused?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: The Commissioner of Public Safety may refuse a license for a physical or mental disability that prevents safe driving or for good cause to believe your driving would harm public safety, and a court finding of mental incompetence can also block it.

sec02-card-sec02-R19.front: What happens if you falsify medical answers on an application, and what might DVS request for a real condition?
sec02-card-sec02-R19.expected_back: Giving false medical information on a permit or license application can cost you your driving privileges, and a medical condition may require a physician's statement on whether it affects safe driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.front: What must a permit or license holder submit—and within how many days—after a new diagnosis of epilepsy or blackouts?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.expected_back: A permit or license holder newly diagnosed with epilepsy or another condition that can cause loss of consciousness must send a physician's statement to DVS within thirty days of the diagnosis.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: What personal details must test ID verify, and what is required whenever names across documents do not match?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: For the written and road tests your identification must verify your first, middle and last name and your date of birth, and mismatched names require certified proof of each legal name change.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: What is DVS policy on laminated, altered, photocopied, or fraudulent identification documents?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: DVS may refuse laminated or altered documents, never accepts photocopies of identification, and may confiscate fraudulent documents.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: How long past expiration can a Minnesota photo card versus a non-photo card still verify identity for a standard card?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: For a standard license or ID you may show a Minnesota license, ID or permit that is current or expired no more than five years if it has a photo, or no more than one year if it has none.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: If you do not have a qualifying Minnesota card, what pair of documents must you bring and what must one display?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: Without such a card you present two documents, a primary and a secondary, and one of them must show your full name and date of birth.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: Compare the post-expiration ID window of a photo Minnesota card against one without a photo?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: A photo Minnesota card can serve as identification up to five years after expiry, but a card without a photo only up to one year after expiry.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.front: Which certified records prove a legal name change, and what applies if your name changed multiple times?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.expected_back: A legal name change through marriage, divorce or court order is proved with a certified marriage certificate, divorce decree or court order naming the change, and every change in a series must be documented.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.front: Which four statements must a translator certify when translating a non-English document for DVS?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.expected_back: A document not in English needs a qualified English translation whose translator certifies it is full and accurate, that they are competent in both languages, that they are not related to the subject by blood or marriage, and that a false translation carries a penalty.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: Under Minnesota's Driver's License for All law, how does immigration status affect getting a standard card?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: Under the Driver's License for All law, since Oct. one, two thousand twenty-three a standard license, learner's permit or state ID can be issued regardless of immigration status, without proof of legal presence.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Which documents and information must you bring in person to obtain a REAL ID compliant Minnesota card?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: A REAL ID compliant card needs one document proving identity, date of birth and legal presence, knowledge of your Social Security number, and two documents proving current Minnesota residency, all presented in person.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: What is the key proof difference between a Driver's License for All standard card and a REAL ID card?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: A standard card under the Driver's License for All law needs no proof of legal presence, while a REAL ID card requires a document proving legal presence and two residency documents.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Who is eligible for a Minnesota enhanced license or ID, what proofs are required, and what address prints on it?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: An enhanced license or ID is limited to U.S. citizens who prove identity, full legal name, Social Security number, photo identity and Minnesota residency, and the card must show the Minnesota residence address.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: What extra residency count, interview step, and surcharge apply when applying for an enhanced card?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: An enhanced card applicant gives two kinds of residency proof, completes an interview questionnaire, and pays a fifteen dollars fee on top of the regular license or ID fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: How is your Social Security number handled on a DVS application, on the card itself, and if an eligible person refuses it?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: You must give your Social Security number on the DVS application or check the box saying none was issued; the number is never printed on or embedded in the card, and an eligible applicant who withholds it cannot be processed.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.front: When can someone in a jail or correctional facility renew a Minnesota license or ID by mail?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.expected_back: A person serving more than six months in a jail or correctional facility without an existing DVS agreement can renew a license or ID by mail.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.front: How long does a temporary post-prison reintegration license last, and what cancels it early?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.expected_back: A reintegration license for someone released from a Minnesota prison is temporary, expires fifteen months after it is issued, and is canceled if the holder breaks traffic laws and loses driving privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: Where and how is the Class D written test administered, and what question styles and subjects appear?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: The Class D written test is given at DVS exam stations by appointment and uses multiple choice and true-or-false questions on Minnesota traffic laws and road signs, on paper or on a computer.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: Which language and audio accommodations are available at computer written-test stations?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: Computer test stations offer the written test in English, several other languages or American Sign Language, and headphones let you hear the questions while you read.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: How many written tests can you attempt in one day, and what percentage score is required to pass?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: You may take only one written test per day, and you need a score of eighty percent to pass.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: After how many consecutive written-test failures does a retest fee start, and how much does each extra try cost?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: Two consecutive failed written tests trigger a ten dollars fee for the third attempt and every attempt after it.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: How does the classroom driver-education rule for the written test differ at age eighteen versus under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.memory_hook: Adults skip class, teens show cards
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Classroom driver education is not required for written-test applicants who are eighteen or older, while those under eighteen show a Blue Card or Pink Card certificate of enrollment.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: State the exact trigger and dollar amount for Minnesota's written-test retest fee?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: Failing two consecutive written tests triggers a ten-dollar fee for the third written test and each subsequent attempt.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: What central acuity and peripheral side-vision minimums must you meet at DVS vision screening?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: The vision screening requires normal or corrected vision of at least twenty over forty and peripheral vision of at least one hundred five degrees.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: What process follows if you fail vision screening or score below one hundred five degrees of side vision?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: Failing the vision screening or having peripheral vision below one hundred five degrees sends you to an eye doctor, whose report to the DVS Driver Evaluation Unit decides whether you may drive or need correction or restrictions.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: If you read twenty over forty clearly, can narrow peripheral vision under one hundred five degrees still trigger a referral?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: Central vision must reach twenty over forty and side vision must reach one hundred five degrees; falling short of the side-vision number alone is enough to be referred to an eye doctor.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: Which three parts make up the Minnesota road test, and what promise applies to examiner instructions?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: The road test has three parts: showing the vehicle's safety equipment, showing vehicle control skills, and a driving test in normal traffic, and you will never be asked to do anything illegal.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Alongside your permit and insurance proof, what vehicle rules govern neighborhood electric cars and rentals at the road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: For the road test you bring a valid instruction permit and current proof of insurance and your own vehicle; a neighborhood electric vehicle is not allowed, and a rental vehicle must list you as a driver.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: How may you use a backup camera during the road test without losing points?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.memory_hook: Glance at camera, still look back
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: A backup camera may be used on the road test, but it must not be your only way of checking behind the vehicle while backing.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: Which four cabin habits, companions, or automated parking features are prohibited during the road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: During the road test there is no smoking, no phone or electronic device use, no passengers of any kind including pets, children or interpreters, and parking assist may not be used for parallel parking.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: Which cabin and exterior controls can the examiner inspect first, and what happens if your car fails that check?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: The safety equipment check can cover the seat, seat belts, parking brake, high and low beams, hazard flashers, horn, wipers, defroster and fan, mirrors and fuel gauge, and failing it ends your road test for that day.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.front: When must adaptive or restriction-required equipment work on your road-test car, and what is the lone exception?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.expected_back: Equipment required by your license or permit restrictions must work for the road test unless you are testing to remove those restrictions.

sec02-card-sec02-R17.front: If your test vehicle has automatic headlights, what must you still demonstrate during the pre-drive equipment check?
sec02-card-sec02-R17.expected_back: On a vehicle with fully automatic headlights, the driver must still switch the high and low beams on manually during the equipment check.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: Alongside traffic skills, hill parking, and parallel parking, what exact backing maneuver and stall width are graded?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: Road test scoring covers vehicle control, parallel parking, parking on a hill, turns and signals, lane use, response to signs and conditions, attention to pedestrians, and a ninety-degree backing maneuver into a space ten feet wide.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: Which five on-road mistakes or refusals cause immediate failure on the Minnesota road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: You fail the road test immediately for breaking a traffic law, driving dangerously or recklessly, needing the examiner's help to control the vehicle, an avoidable crash even when not legally at fault, or refusing the examiner's instructions.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: What retest fee kicks in after two failed road tests, and what training is required after four failures?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.memory_hook: Twenty after two, training after four
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: After two failed road tests each further attempt costs a twenty dollars retest fee, and after four failures you need a minimum of six hours of behind-the-wheel training from a licensed instructor before testing again.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.front: Before booking another shot after a failed road test, what requirement from your score sheet must you complete?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.expected_back: A failed road test comes with assigned practice time that must be finished before the next attempt.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: When does Minnesota's road-test retest fee start, and what is the exact dollar charge per attempt?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: Failing the road test twice triggers a twenty-dollar retest fee for every subsequent road test attempt.

sec02-card-sec02-R18.front: Once an applicant under eighteen passes the road test, which four adults are authorized to sign the license application?
sec02-card-sec02-R18.expected_back: After passing the road test, an applicant under eighteen needs the application signed by a parent, a legal guardian, a foster parent appointed by a county, or the director of the transitional living program where they live.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Which four categories of adults may approve a permit or license application for someone under eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen needs the permit or license application approved by a parent, a guardian appointed by a court, a foster parent appointed by a county, or the director of the transitional living program where the teen lives.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: When a teen's parents are divorced, who holds legal authority to approve the driving application?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: When the parents are divorced, the custodial parent or a stepparent married to the custodial parent may approve the teen's application.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: Who may sign for a teen who is married, emancipated, or has no living parent or guardian, and how old must they be?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: A teen with no living parent or guardian, or who is married or legally emancipated, may have a close family member, an employer or a spouse sign, and that signer must be at least eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: Once an adult approves a teen's driving application, is that signature permanent or reversible?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: The person who signed a teen's application may later withdraw that approval.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: When can a host sponsor sign for a foreign exchange student, and what two notarized forms are needed otherwise?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Host sponsors of a foreign exchange student may sign only with documented legal guardianship; otherwise the student brings two forms with the parents' notarized signatures, one for the permit and one for the provisional license.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Under Graduated Driver's Licensing, how long must a learner eighteen or younger hold an instruction permit before road testing?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Under the Graduated Driver's Licensing system, a driver aged eighteen or younger is required to keep an instruction permit a minimum of six months before the road test.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: How long is an instruction permit valid, where does your licensed supervisor sit, and must you carry the card?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: An instruction permit covers two years of practice with a licensed supervising driver in the front passenger seat, practicing without a valid permit is illegal, and the permit must be with you whenever you drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: At age fifteen, which two driver-ed classroom paths qualify for a permit, and when does driver ed stop being required?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: To get a permit you must be at least fifteen and either finish thirty hours of classroom instruction while enrolled in behind-the-wheel training, or be in a concurrent course with the first fifteen classroom hours done; at eighteen or older no driver education is needed.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Beyond age and classroom hours, which five counter steps complete getting your instruction permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: The permit also requires meeting the identification rules, passing the vision screening and the written test, completing an application and paying the permit fee.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: For a permit holder under eighteen, what supervisor age, occupant belt rule, and cell-phone rule apply?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: A permit holder under eighteen needs a supervising driver who is twenty-one or older, all occupants must wear a seat belt or ride in a child restraint, and the teen may not use or talk on a cell phone even hands-free.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: When the permit holder is eighteen or older, how old must the supervising driver be and who wears restraints?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: A permit holder aged eighteen or older may be supervised by a driver aged eighteen or older, and everyone in the vehicle must be belted or in a child restraint.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: How many months of practice driving precede the road test generally versus at age nineteen or older?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: The road test may be taken after six months of practice driving, or after three months for a permit holder aged nineteen or older.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: How do you replace a lost or expired instruction permit, and how long does the replacement run?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: A lost or expired permit is replaced by applying for a new one, which is valid for two years from the day you apply.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: Combine a teen permit holder's supervisor minimum age, cell-phone ban, and two classroom-hour paths?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: A teen permit holder needs a supervisor aged twenty-one or older and may not use a phone at all while driving, while the classroom rule for a permit is thirty hours finished or the first fifteen hours of a concurrent course.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: How do supervisor age at eighteen-plus and road-test wait time at nineteen-plus ease up for adult permit holders?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: An adult permit holder's supervisor needs to be only eighteen or older, and the adult may test after three months at age nineteen or older instead of six.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: Which GDL stage is the provisional license, how long is it valid, and what belt and phone rules carry over?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: The provisional license is the second stage of graduated licensing, is valid for two years from the application date, and requires every occupant to be belted while banning cell phone use, hands-free included.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: What minimum age, driver-education milestones, and clean permit stretch are required for a provisional license?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.memory_hook: Sixteen, both ed phases, six clean
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: A provisional license requires being at least sixteen, finishing both the classroom and behind-the-wheel phases of driver education, and holding a permit for six months with no moving, alcohol or controlled-substance convictions.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: How does a parent completing the optional parent class change the total and nighttime hours on your supervised log?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.memory_hook: Forty with parent class, fifty without
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: The supervised driving log must show at least forty hours including fifteen at night if a parent takes the class from an approved driver education program, or at least fifty hours including fifteen at night without that class.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: Along with age, education, and logged hours, what exam and approval complete provisional licensing?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: The provisional license also requires a passed road test and an application signed by an approved adult such as a parent or guardian.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: During the first six provisional months, which overnight hours are restricted and which exceptions allow driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: In the first six months a provisional driver may not drive between midnight and five a.m. unless with a licensed driver at least twenty-five years old, driving between home and work or a school event without school transportation, or driving for employment.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: During the first six months on a provisional license, how many passengers under twenty may ride without a parent or guardian?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: In the first six months a provisional driver may carry only one passenger under twenty unless a parent or guardian is in the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: During the second six months on a provisional license, how many passengers under twenty are allowed without a parent or guardian?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: In the second six months a provisional driver may carry no more than three passengers under twenty unless a parent or guardian is in the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: How do immediate family members under age twenty affect the provisional passenger caps?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Immediate family members under twenty do not count against the provisional passenger limits in either six-month period.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: How long do both the instruction permit and the provisional license last, and from what date does each run?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.memory_hook: Both run two years from application
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Both the instruction permit and the provisional license run for two years, but the permit counts from the day you apply for it and the provisional license from its application date.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: What overnight hours trigger the provisional curfew, and what minimum age lets a licensed companion lift it?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: The provisional night limit runs from midnight to five a.m., and a licensed companion only lifts it when that companion is at least twenty-five years old.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: Compare the under-twenty passenger limits across months one-to-six and seven-to-twelve, and who lifts both?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.memory_hook: One first, three second, parents lift
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: The provisional passenger cap is one passenger under twenty for the first six months and three for the second six months, and a parent or guardian riding along lifts either cap.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: Why was Vanessa's Law enacted, and which two teen violation categories trigger it?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: Vanessa's Law, passed a year after Vanessa Weiss died in May two thousand three as a passenger of an unlicensed fifteen-year-old, covers every teen who commits an impaired driving crime or a crash-related moving violation.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: Until what age is an unlicensed teen barred from any permit or license after a crash-related or alcohol-or-drug conviction?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.memory_hook: Zero permit or license until eighteen
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: An unlicensed teen convicted of a crash-related moving violation or an alcohol or drug offense such as DWI, Implied Consent, Open Bottle or the Not a Drop law cannot get any license or permit until age eighteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: Once that unlicensed teen turns eighteen under Vanessa's Law, what four steps stand before taking a road test?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: After turning eighteen that teen must meet the reinstatement requirements, pass the Class D written test, get a permit and hold it at least six months, or three months at nineteen or older, before the road test.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: When can a provisional driver revoked under Vanessa's Law regain a license?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.memory_hook: Eighteen or withdrawal end, whichever later
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: A provisional license holder revoked for such a violation cannot regain a license until age eighteen or the end of the withdrawal period, whichever comes later.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: Which five hurdles—including the exact fee and classroom rule—apply when reinstating that revoked provisional holder?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: Reinstatement for that provisional holder usually means serving the withdrawal period, passing the Class D written test, paying a six hundred eighty dollars reinstatement fee, finishing a thirty-hour classroom course that cannot be taken online, and applying for a permit.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: After reinstating into a permit under Vanessa's Law, how long do you hold it and what training happens inside?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.memory_hook: Hold ninety days, six instructor hours
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: After reinstatement the permit is held for ninety days, during which six hours of behind-the-wheel driver education are completed, and then the driver applies for a license.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Contrast the Vanessa's Law waiting period for an unlicensed teen against a revoked provisional holder?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Under Vanessa's Law an unlicensed teen waits until eighteen, while a revoked provisional holder waits until eighteen or the end of the withdrawal period, whichever is longer.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: Which two eligibility routes qualify a driver for an Under-Twenty-One Class D license?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.memory_hook: Turn eighteen or twelve clean months
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: An under-twenty-one Class D license requires being at least eighteen, or holding a provisional license for twelve consecutive months with no alcohol, controlled-substance or crash-related moving violation convictions.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: At most how many non-crash moving-violation convictions may an Under-Twenty-One Class D applicant have?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: An under-twenty-one license applicant is limited to at most one conviction for a non-crash moving violation.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: If upgrading to the Under-Twenty-One license before turning eighteen, what extra supervised hours must you certify?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen for that license certifies at least ten hours of driving supervised by a licensed driver aged twenty-one or older.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: How much fee credit do you earn when upgrading from a provisional license with a spotless record?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: Upgrading from a provisional license with a clean record earns a three dollars and fifty cents credit toward the license fee.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: How is a pre-twenty-one license labeled, when does it expire first, and how often does it renew afterward?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: A license issued before age twenty-one is marked Under twenty-one, expires on the twenty-first birthday, and afterward expires every four years on the birthday.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: Which three specialized licenses or permits can a fifteen-year-old earn after driver ed and a road test?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: At age fifteen a restricted farm work license, a special medical license or a moped permit may be available after driver education and a road test.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: When and how far may a fifteen-year-old drive solo on a restricted farm license, and when can the restriction come off?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.memory_hook: Daylight farm work within forty miles
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: A restricted farm work license lets a teen drive alone for farm work in daylight within forty miles of the farmhouse, and the restriction can be removed by application after six months with the license and reaching age sixteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.front: What waiting rule do farm-work and special-medical applicants bypass, and which three items must they still complete?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.expected_back: Farm work and special medical applicants skip the six-month wait before the road test but still need a permit, a behind-the-wheel completion certificate and a supervised driving log.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.front: What two household and medical facts justify a special medical license at fifteen, and what restriction code prints on it?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.expected_back: A special medical license may be issued at fifteen when no licensed driver lives in the household and the teen must drive for personal or a relative's medical needs; it carries the restriction code MEDLIM.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.front: Contrast the course and testing requirements for a moped permit at fifteen against riding an electric-assist bicycle?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.expected_back: A moped permit is available at fifteen after a motorized bicycle safety course and the written, vision and road tests, while an electric-assist bicycle needs no test or license but its rider must be at least fifteen.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: Which three weight, passenger-capacity, or cargo traits push a single-unit vehicle outside a standard Class D license?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: A Class D license allows all single-unit vehicles except those with a gross vehicle weight of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, those designed to carry more than fifteen people including the driver, and those carrying hazardous materials.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: Within what distance and by which three drivers may a farm truck haul farm goods on a Class D license?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: A Class D holder may drive a farm truck carrying farm products, machinery or supplies within one hundred fifty miles of the farm, but only as the farmer, an immediate family member or a farm employee.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: Which emergency, recreational, and small-vehicle types are covered by a Class D license, and which one needs an endorsement?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: A Class D license also covers authorized emergency vehicles of any weight, motor homes and camping trailers for personal use, mopeds, electric-assist bicycles, neighborhood electric vehicles, autocycles, and motorcycles once endorsed.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: When must you carry your license, what prints on its back, and how many license classes exist in Minnesota?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: You must carry your license whenever you drive, and its back lists your class, endorsements and restrictions; Minnesota has four license classes.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.front: What trailer weight may a Class D driver always tow, and when is towing a heavier trailer allowed?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.expected_back: A Class D driver may tow a trailer weighing ten thousand pounds or less, or a heavier one only when the vehicle and trailer together weigh twenty-six thousand pounds or less.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.front: Which six vehicle or cargo types require endorsements, and which three of them require an extra road test beyond written?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.memory_hook: Six endorsed; bus, school, motorcycle road-test
sec03-card-sec03-R12.expected_back: Endorsements are required for motorcycles, buses, school buses, double and triple trailers, tank vehicles and hazardous materials; each needs an extra written test, and the bus, school bus and motorcycle endorsements also need a special road test.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.front: What vehicles do commercial Classes A, B, and C include alongside their class rigs, and what happens under twenty-one?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.memory_hook: Include Class D, restricted under twenty-one
sec03-card-sec03-R13.expected_back: Classes A, B and C are commercial licenses that cover every Class D vehicle plus vehicles specific to each class, and a commercial license obtained before twenty-one carries restrictions.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.front: Which three workplace vehicle types can trigger commercial motor carrier rules and federal medical certificates?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.expected_back: Employers and employees may face commercial motor carrier rules for vehicles over ten thousand pounds, package delivery vehicles and vehicles carrying more than eight people including the driver, possibly including a federal medical examiner's certificate.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.front: Once you are twenty-one, when and how often does a Minnesota license renew, what check applies, and how are lost cards replaced?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.expected_back: A Minnesota license usually expires on your birthday and is renewed every four years once you are twenty-one, renewal requires a vision test, and a lost or damaged license is replaced with a duplicate.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.front: Within how many days must you get a duplicate after a name or address change, and how differs replacing a lost permit?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.expected_back: A name or address change before the license expires requires applying for a duplicate within thirty days, while a lost instruction permit is replaced by renewing the permit.

sec03-card-sec03-R17.front: When must an active-duty military member renew a Minnesota license, with what papers, and which family members qualify?
sec03-card-sec03-R17.expected_back: A Minnesota license holder in active military service need not renew until separation or discharge and must then renew within one year with the license and DD-two hundred fourteen papers; the rule extends to a spouse, domestic partner or dependents under twenty-six living outside Minnesota.

sec03-card-sec03-R18.front: Which vehicle taxes and DVS fees are waived for a veteran rated one hundred percent total and service-connected disabled?
sec03-card-sec03-R18.expected_back: A veteran whose disability is rated one hundred percent total and service-connected pays no sales, registration or wheelage taxes on up to two vehicles and no title, license or ID card fees.

sec03-card-sec03-R19.front: What service length and discharge types qualify for the optional veteran license indicator, and does it alter VA benefits?
sec03-card-sec03-R19.expected_back: A veteran indicator requires separation from service, at least one hundred eighty-one days of active service with an Honorable or General discharge, and is optional with no effect on VA benefits.

sec03-card-sec03-R20.front: How does license renewal timing work for Peace Corps volunteers and federal foreign service employees holding valid Minnesota licenses?
sec03-card-sec03-R20.expected_back: Peace Corps volunteers and federal foreign service employees with a valid Minnesota license need not renew until their service ends, then must renew within one year.

sec03-card-sec03-R21.front: How does applying for a Minnesota license or ID handle Selective Service for ages eighteen-to-twenty-six and under eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-R21.expected_back: Applying for any Minnesota license or ID registers a citizen or resident aged eighteen to twenty-six with Selective Service, and for applicants under eighteen registration is held until the eighteenth birthday.

sec03-card-sec03-R22.front: Can you hold a Minnesota state ID card alongside a valid license or permit, and what statement changes that?
sec03-card-sec03-R22.expected_back: You may hold only one type of Minnesota card, so DVS will not issue an ID card to someone with a valid license or permit unless they sign a downgrade statement giving up driving privileges.

sec03-card-sec03-R23.front: What does twenty-dollar fast track service speed up, and for which three card transactions is it unavailable?
sec03-card-sec03-R23.memory_hook: Three-day processing, barred first, enhanced, upgrades
