sec03-card-sec03-R23.expected_back: Fast track service costs an extra twenty dollars, processes the card within three business days with UPS delivery within ten business days and an adult signature, and is not available for a first license, an enhanced card or an upgrade.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: Which set of standards do Minnesota's road signs, traffic lights, and pavement lines follow?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Minnesota's signs, signals and pavement markings follow national standards.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Why are road sign shapes and background colors standardized into distinct categories?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Sign shapes and colors are coded so that you can grasp a sign's general meaning before you are close enough to read it.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: Which seven common road sign shapes does the Minnesota driver's manual identify?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Besides colors, the manual names seven common sign shapes: octagon, triangle, diamond, rectangle, pentagon, crossbuck and circle.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: What two visual elements do road signs combine to communicate instructions clearly?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Road signs combine uniform symbols and pictures with written instructions.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: On regulatory signs, what distinct roles do red and white play?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: On regulatory signs, red prohibits and commands, while white regulates.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: How do yellow, yellow-green, and orange divide up warning duties along the road?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.memory_hook: Yellow general, green-yellow crossings, orange work
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: On warning signs, yellow warns, yellow-green warns and controls at pedestrian and bicycle crossings and school areas, and orange warns and controls in construction zones.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What type of traveler information does each color carry on green, blue, and brown signs?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.memory_hook: Green guides, blue services, brown parks
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: On informational signs, green guides and informs, blue describes motorist services, and brown marks historic, cultural or recreational sites.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Which exact zones reserve yellow-green warning signs versus orange warning signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Yellow and yellow-green both warn, but yellow-green is limited to pedestrian and bicycle crossings and school areas, while orange is the color of construction zones.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: While most warning signs use standard yellow, which three crossing or zone signs may appear in fluorescent yellow-green?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: Most warning signs are yellow, but pedestrian crossing, bicycle crossing and school zone signs may be yellow or fluorescent yellow-green.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: What legal duty do regulatory signs carry, and what happens if you disobey one?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Regulatory signs require you to follow traffic laws, and ignoring one can bring a traffic citation and a fine.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: What complete sequence must you follow at a Stop sign before proceeding?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: At a Stop sign, come to a full stop and wait until every pedestrian and vehicle that has the right-of-way is out of the intersection, then go on with caution.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: How must you adjust your driving and priority when approaching a Yield sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: At a Yield sign, slow down or stop if necessary and give the right-of-way to all other vehicles and pedestrians until it is safe to go.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: What does a Do Not Enter sign facing your windshield forbid you from doing?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: A Do Not Enter sign facing you means you may not enter that lane or road.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: What urgent mistake has already happened if you spot a Wrong Way sign ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: A Wrong Way sign means you have entered a lane of oncoming traffic and are traveling in the wrong direction.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How does the meaning of a Do Not Enter sign differ from a Wrong Way sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: A Do Not Enter sign facing you forbids going into that lane or road, while a Wrong Way sign means you are already in a lane of oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: What universal message does a red circle with a diagonal red slash over a black symbol send?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: A red circle with a red slash across a symbol, as on No Left Turn, No Right Turn, No U Turn and No Parking signs, means the action shown is not allowed.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: What do speed limit signs and interstate minimum speed signs require, and when may you drop below a minimum?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: A speed limit sign shows the maximum speed for the road, and controlled-access interstate freeways may also post minimum limits that you must not go below unless bad weather or poor road conditions require it.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: What roadway boundary does a white regulatory Do Not Pass sign mark?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: The regulatory Do Not Pass sign marks where a no-passing zone begins.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: Which side of a two-way highway carries the No Passing Zone warning sign, and what does it mark?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Located on the left side of a two-way highway, the No Passing Zone warning sign alerts drivers to the start of a no-passing zone.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: What traffic rule does a black-and-white One Way sign enforce?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: A One Way sign means traffic in that lane moves only in the direction of the arrow.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: Where does a Keep Right regulatory sign direct you to steer?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: A Keep Right sign tells you to stay to the right of a traffic island, median or obstruction ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: How should you use lane-choice signs posted ahead of a multilane roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Before a multilane roundabout, signs show which lane to use for each turn, so move into the correct lane well in advance, for example the right lane only to turn right and the left lane only to turn left.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: In the manual's multilane roundabout sign example, which lanes may continue straight through?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: In the multilane roundabout sign example, going straight is allowed from either lane even though turning right and turning left are each limited to one lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: What does a lane-use control sign require when you are in its marked lane?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: A lane-use control sign means you must turn if you are in the lane it marks, though a sign may also show that one lane can go straight or turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What must you do at an intersection posted with a No Turn on Red sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: A No Turn on Red sign means you wait for a green signal before turning.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Who may use a center lane marked with a left-turn-only sign, and for what single maneuver?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: A center lane left-turn only sign means traffic from both directions shares the center lane and may use it only to make left turns.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: What action should you start taking as soon as you spot a Reduced Speed Ahead sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: A Reduced Speed Ahead sign means a lower speed limit is coming, so begin slowing down.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: What does a white diamond symbol painted or posted on a lane indicate?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: A diamond symbol marks a lane reserved for certain uses or vehicles, such as cars with two or more passengers, buses, commercial vehicles or bicycles.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: Which vehicles are legally allowed to park in spaces marked by blue disability parking signs?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: Only vehicles carrying disability license plates or a disability parking permit may use spaces marked with blue disability parking signs.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: How may a driver with valid disability plates or a permit park if every designated disability space is full?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: If the designated disability spaces are full or unavailable, a driver with a valid disability permit or plates may park at an angle across two standard spaces.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: Which three white pavement markings appear on the road surface ahead of a railroad crossing?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Pavement markings in front of a railroad crossing include a stop line, an X and the letters RR.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: What does a white X-shaped crossbuck sign mark, and what extra sign appears when multiple tracks cross?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: An X-shaped crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing, and when there is more than one track, a sign below it shows how many.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: How does an Exempt sign at a railroad crossing change the rule for bus and truck drivers?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: An exempt sign at a railroad crossing lets bus and truck drivers who normally must stop go on without stopping, though they must still look both ways for trains.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: What three actions should you take when you pass a circular Railroad Crossing Ahead sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: Railroad crossing ahead signs mean slow down, look carefully both ways and be ready to stop, because trains cannot stop quickly.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: What shape and colors identify a school zone sign, and what does it warn is ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: Pentagon-shaped school zone signs, yellow or fluorescent yellow-green, warn that a school or an approved school crosswalk is ahead, so watch for children and be ready to stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: How must you drive when reaching a posted school crossing sign?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: At a school crossing sign, watch for children and be ready to stop, since drivers must yield to every pedestrian in a crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: What three responses does a pedestrian crossing warning sign call for?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: A pedestrian crossing sign means slow down, be ready to stop, and yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections and crosswalks.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: What companion sign sits directly underneath standard school crossing and pedestrian crossing signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: The school crossing and pedestrian crossing signs each come with an arrow sign below them, which the manual calls the standard marking.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: Which vehicles must display the slow-moving vehicle emblem, and how should you react when spotting one?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: The slow-moving vehicle emblem must be shown on every vehicle traveling thirty miles per hour or less on a public road, such as farm implements or animal-drawn vehicles, so adjust your speed or get ready to change lanes when you see it.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: How should you overtake animal-drawn vehicles, and what nighttime lighting must they carry?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: Slow down and pass animal-drawn vehicles slowly; from sunset to sunrise or in poor visibility they must carry a light or lamp visible within five hundred feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: What does a yellow T-intersection ahead sign tell you about your lane and priority?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: A T-intersection ahead sign means your road ends soon, so get ready to turn right or left and yield to cross traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: What upcoming road feature and action does a yellow crossroad sign warn about?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: A crossroad sign means an intersection is ahead and you should prepare to yield.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: What specific traffic movement does a side road warning sign alert you to watch for?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: A side road sign means traffic is coming from your right, so watch for vehicles entering the road.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: What two things should you prepare for when approaching a Y-intersection warning sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: A Y-intersection sign means the road splits in two directions, so expect crossing traffic and get ready to bear one way or the other.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: How should you adjust your speed when a curve warning sign includes an advisory speed plaque?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: If a curve sign shows a speed, slow to that speed for the curve.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: What two steps should you take when you see a yellow roundabout warning sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: A roundabout warning sign means slow to the advisory speed as you approach and be ready to stop.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: How does a winding road warning sign differ from a road turns ahead sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: A winding road sign means the road bends back and forth ahead, while a road turns ahead sign means it changes direction sharply; slow down for both.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: What roadway transition does a Two-Way Traffic Ahead sign announce, and where must you position your car?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: A two-way traffic ahead sign means you are leaving a one-way road for a two-way road, so stay to the right.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: How do the Divided Highway Begins and Divided Highway Ends warning signs differ?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: A divided highway begins sign tells you to stay right as the road divides, while a divided highway ends sign warns that two-way traffic will no longer be separated by a center island.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: What does a yellow diamond showing red, yellow, and green circles warn is coming up?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: A traffic signal ahead sign warns that the next intersection has a traffic light.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: What three categories of road crossers do general yellow crossing signs warn you to watch for?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: Crossing signs warn you to watch for animals, people or vehicles crossing the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: What road condition does a Slippery Road sign warn of, and where is it commonly placed?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: A slippery road sign warns that the surface is slippery when wet and is often placed near bridges and overpasses.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.front: What does a Steep Hill sign warn is ahead, and what vehicle check should you make before descending?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.expected_back: A steep hill sign means the road drops sharply ahead, so be sure your brakes work before you go on.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.front: When a Lane Ends sign shows the right lane tapering away, which drivers must yield and merge?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.expected_back: A lane ends sign means two lanes are becoming one, and in the example shown the right-lane vehicles must yield and merge into the left lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.front: How do your duties differ at a Lane Ends sign, a Merging Traffic sign, and an Added Lane sign?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.memory_hook: Ending yields, merge shares, added free
sec09-card-sec09-R18.expected_back: With a lane ends sign the ending lane must yield and merge, with a merging traffic sign you make room for vehicles joining your road, and with an added lane sign the new traffic does not need to merge at all.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.front: What must you do at a Low Clearance sign if your vehicle or rooftop load exceeds the posted height?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.expected_back: A low clearance sign means you must not go on if your vehicle is taller than the height shown, or it may become stuck.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.front: What change in roadway width does a Narrow Bridge warning sign announce?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.expected_back: A narrow bridge sign means the bridge ahead is narrower than the road leading to it.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.front: What hazards do orange signs with black lettering warn of, and how should you respond?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.expected_back: Orange signs with black letters mark construction and work zones, warning of restricted lanes, detours and other road work hazards, and you should slow down when you see one.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.front: What job do orange drums, cones, arrows, and striped barriers do, and whom must you always obey?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.expected_back: Drums, cones, tubes, flashing arrows and orange-and-white striped barriers keep traffic out of dangerous work areas, and you must always follow people directing traffic with orange signs, flags or stop signs.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.front: What does an orange warning sign showing a person holding a flag tell you?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.expected_back: A flagger sign means a person with a flag is ahead, so drive cautiously.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.front: How should you adjust speed and lane placement when an orange Road Work sign shows workers?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.expected_back: A road work sign showing workers means maintenance is under way, so slow down and shift your lane position to keep away from them.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.front: What speed-limit change is commonly posted through active construction and maintenance zones?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.expected_back: Reduced speed limits are often posted in work zones.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.front: What fine hits drivers who exceed a posted work-zone speed limit while workers are present?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.expected_back: Drivers who break the posted work zone speed limit while workers are present are fined three hundred dollars.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.front: Which destinations do brown roadside guide signs point drivers toward?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.expected_back: Brown signs point out historic sites, parks and other points of interest.

sec09-card-sec09-R24.front: Which six kinds of roadside stops do blue motorist-service signs help you find?
sec09-card-sec09-R24.expected_back: Blue signs lead you to motorist services such as telephones, gas, food, motels, hospitals and rest areas.

sec09-card-sec09-R25.front: What five pieces of directional info appear on green highway and street signs?
sec09-card-sec09-R25.expected_back: Green signs show exits, distances to cities, interstate interchanges, street or route names and bicycle routes.

sec09-card-sec09-R26.front: Which four levels of roadways get their own distinct route-marker sign shapes in Minnesota?
sec09-card-sec09-R26.expected_back: Route signs identify the type of road, with separate markers for interstate freeways, U.S. highways, Minnesota highways and county roads.

sec09-card-sec09-R27.front: What two main goals do traffic-control signals serve at busy intersections?
sec09-card-sec09-R27.expected_back: Traffic-control signals are placed at busy intersections to promote safety and orderly traffic flow.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.front: How must you treat an intersection when its traffic signal is dark or completely out of order?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.expected_back: When a traffic signal is not working, treat the intersection as an uncontrolled intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.front: Even on a green light, what must be true on the far side before you enter a signalized intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.expected_back: Do not enter an intersection with a traffic signal unless you can move through it immediately, continuously and completely without blocking cross traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F44.front: In which three situations does Minnesota's intersection gridlock rule not apply?
sec09-card-sec09-F44.expected_back: The gridlock rule does not apply when a traffic-control agent or peace officer directs you, when you are moving aside for an emergency vehicle with lights on, or when your turn lets you leave the intersection safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Where exact spot must your car halt when you approach a stop sign?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: At a stop sign you must stop completely, before the stop line if one is marked, or before the crosswalk if there is one.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: What must you do after halting at a stop sign, especially if parked cars or bushes block your view?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: After stopping at a stop sign, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and traffic before you go, and if your view of the intersection is blocked, be ready to stop again.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: Where must you come to a complete halt when pulling onto a street from an alley, driveway, or parking ramp?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Stop completely before pulling onto a road from an alley, a private driveway, a parking lot or a parking ramp, and always stop before driving across a sidewalk or crosswalk.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: When may you pull forward after stopping at a steady red traffic light?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: At a red traffic signal, stop and wait until the light is green and your path is clear before going.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: What is the key difference between a steady red signal and a flashing red signal?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: A steady red signal means stop and wait for green, while a flashing red light means stop and then go when clear, just as at a stop sign.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Which everyday intersection sign works the exact same way as a flashing red traffic light?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Treat a flashing red traffic light exactly like a stop sign.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: How long must you stay stopped when a pedestrian or cyclist is crossing in a marked or unmarked crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Stop at any crosswalk, marked or unmarked, where a pedestrian or bicyclist is crossing, and stay stopped until they have passed your lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: Name four other roadside situations besides stop signs and intersection lights that demand a full stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Full stops are also required for a red freeway ramp meter, for a railroad crossing posted with a stop sign, when a flag person or traffic device signals you to halt, and at a bridge raised for boats.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: In a speed zone of 35 mph or slower, how far before stopping does a school bus start flashing yellow lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: In a speed zone of thirty-five miles per hour or less, a school bus driver turns on the flashing yellow lights at least one hundred feet before the bus stops.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: When the speed limit is over 35 mph, how far in advance does a school bus activate its flashing yellow lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: In a speed zone above thirty-five miles per hour, a school bus driver turns on the flashing yellow lights at least three hundred feet before the bus stops.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: How do the two minimum yellow-light warning distances on a stopping school bus compare across speed zones?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.memory_hook: One hundred slow, three hundred fast
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: School buses flash yellow and red lights alternately when stopping for students, activating flashing yellow lights at least one hundred feet ahead in speed zones of thirty-five miles per hour or less and at least three hundred feet ahead in faster zones.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Is it ever legal to pass on the right side of a school bus flashing yellow or red lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Passing a school bus on its right side while it shows flashing red or yellow lights is against the law.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: How far away must you stop when a school bus halts with its red lights flashing?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: When a stopped school bus has its red lights flashing, you must stop at least twenty feet away from it.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: Whether approaching from ahead or behind, when may you move again after stopping for a school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: Whether you are facing the front or the back of the bus, you stay stopped until its red lights stop flashing.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: What offense class, minimum fine, and license consequence hit a driver convicted of failing to stop for a school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Failing to stop for a school bus is a misdemeanor, and a conviction brings a fine of at least five hundred dollars and the loss of your driving privileges.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: When are oncoming drivers exempt from stopping for a school bus displaying flashing red lights?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: On a divided roadway you do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights that is on the other side of the divider.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: On a road with no median divider, which directions of traffic must stop for a school bus flashing red?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Without a divider, the duty to stop for a bus with flashing red lights covers traffic from both directions, behind the bus and facing it; only a divided roadway frees drivers on the far side.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: Within how many hours of an illegal school bus pass can an officer with probable cause arrest the driver?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: An officer with probable cause to believe you illegally passed a stopped school bus may arrest you within four hours of the violation.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: What happens to a vehicle's owner or lessee if someone uses their car to illegally pass a stopped school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: The owner or lessee of a vehicle used to break the school bus stopping law is guilty of a petty misdemeanor unless they can prove someone else was driving, in which case the driver is charged.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: How does the charge against the actual driver compare with the charge against the vehicle's owner in a school bus violation?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: A driver who passes a stopped school bus faces a misdemeanor, while the vehicle's owner or lessee faces a petty misdemeanor unless they show someone else was driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: What specific promise about school buses do you certify when signing a Minnesota license application?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: When you sign a driver's license application, you certify that you understand the duty to stop for a school bus and know the penalties for breaking that law.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: What action must you take for a student safety patrol or an adult crossing guard holding a stop sign or flag?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: Come to a complete stop for a student safety patrol helping classmates cross, and for an adult crossing guard holding a stop sign or flag.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: What happens legally if you drive through a line of children crossing the road even when no patrol is present?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Driving through a line of children crossing the road is illegal even with no safety patrol present; it is a misdemeanor, and a second violation within a year is a gross misdemeanor.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: When a school bus flagger holds traffic so buses can exit school grounds, when may you drive forward?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Stop for a school bus flagger who is holding traffic so buses can leave school property, and do not move on until the flagger or a police officer tells you to.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: What two everyday principles back right-of-way laws, and what is breaking them a top cause of?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: Right-of-way and yielding laws rest on courtesy and common sense, and breaking them is a leading cause of traffic crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection, all-way stop, or flashing red at the same time, who yields?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: At an intersection without signals, and at an all-way stop or flashing red light, when two drivers arrive together the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: Which oncoming traffic must you yield to whenever you make a left turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: When turning left, yield to oncoming vehicles that are in the intersection or near enough to cause a crash.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: Even when a green left-turn arrow lights up, whom must you still yield to before completing your turn?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: A green left-turn arrow still requires you to yield to vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection before you continue in the arrow's direction.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: Who must yield at an uncontrolled T-intersection where one street dead-ends into a through road?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: At an uncontrolled T intersection, the driver who is turning yields to all cross traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: When driving in the right lane, which buses signaling to pull back into traffic must you yield to?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: A driver in the right-hand lane yields to transit and metro mobility buses merging out of a bus stop or off the shoulder, and to a school bus re-entering the lane after loading, which shows its left turn signal.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: How do vehicles in a funeral procession mark themselves, and what must other drivers do?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: Yield to every vehicle in a funeral procession once it marks itself with headlights or hazard warning lights.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: What two yielding duties apply when leaving a private driveway and whenever pedestrians cross at intersections?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: Coming out of a private road or driveway onto a public road, you stop and yield to pedestrians and traffic, and at intersections and crosswalks, marked or unmarked, you always yield to crossing pedestrians.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: How must you clear the way for an approaching emergency vehicle on two-way roads, one-way streets, and inside intersections?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: When an emergency vehicle with flashing red lights and a siren or bell comes toward you on a two-way road, move right and stop; on a one-way road move to the closer side; finish crossing an intersection first if you are in one; and stay stopped until every emergency vehicle has gone by.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: When are you allowed to keep driving instead of stopping for an approaching emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: You need not stop for an emergency vehicle that is separated from your lane by a physical barrier such as a fence, wall or median strip.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: How long after failing to yield to an emergency vehicle can an officer with probable cause arrest you?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: An officer with probable cause to believe you failed to yield to an emergency vehicle may arrest you within four hours of the violation.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: On a road with at least two lanes your way, what must you do for a stopped flashing emergency vehicle or tow truck?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Under the Move Over Law, when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on or beside a road with two lanes in your direction, move to the lane farthest from it if it is safe; tow trucks count as emergency vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: Beyond police, fire, ambulances, and tow trucks, which other stopped vehicles does Minnesota's Move Over rule protect?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: The Move Over rule also applies to stalled or disabled vehicles and to stopped service patrol, road maintenance, utility, construction, postal, and solid waste or recycling vehicles with warning lights on.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: What must you do for a stopped flashing roadside vehicle if heavy traffic or a single lane keeps you from moving over?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: If you cannot move over a lane, or the road has only one lane in your direction, slow down and pass the stopped vehicle with caution.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: How far back must ordinary drivers stay behind a firefighting vehicle on an emergency run?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: Only vehicles on official emergency business may follow within five hundred feet of a firefighting vehicle on an emergency run.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: When, if ever, may you drive across an unprotected fire hose stretched over the street?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: Never drive over an unprotected fire hose unless a law enforcement officer or fire department official tells you to.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.front: How should you set and adjust your following distance behind the vehicle ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.expected_back: Keep enough distance behind the vehicle ahead to stop or turn away from a collision, adjust it for weather, traffic and road conditions, and use the three-second rule taught later in the manual.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: How does Minnesota law distinguish careless driving from reckless driving, and where does racing fit?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: Careless driving endangers people or property, while reckless driving means knowingly ignoring a substantial and unjustifiable risk to others, which includes racing whether or not the speed limit is exceeded.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.front: How are both careless driving and reckless driving charges classified when tried in court?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.expected_back: A charge of either careless or reckless driving is tried in court as a misdemeanor.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: Where and how should you pull over when patrol lights flash behind your car?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: When emergency lights appear behind you, stay calm, slow down, signal and pull onto the right shoulder as soon as it is safe, avoiding bridges, curves and the traffic lane.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.front: Under what condition may you pull onto the left shoulder instead of the right during a multi-lane police stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.expected_back: On a multi-lane road, if you are nearer the left shoulder and it has room for a full lane, you may pull over onto the left shoulder instead of the right.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: Which four actions keep a nighttime traffic stop calm and safe once you park on the shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: During a stop after dark, switch on the interior light, keep the doors shut, stay inside unless the officer says otherwise, and keep your hands visible on the steering wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-R15.front: What should you do during a stop if your license or insurance card is tucked out of reach, or you want to step out?
sec07-card-sec07-R15.expected_back: If your license or insurance proof is out of reach, tell the officer where it is before reaching, and do not get out of the vehicle or approach the officer unless you ask and are given permission.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: What exact steps should you follow during a traffic stop if there is a firearm inside your vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: With a firearm in the vehicle, leave both hands visible on the wheel, tell the officer about the firearm and its location as soon as they approach, and never reach for it.

sec07-card-sec07-R16.front: Where should you challenge a ticket you disagree with, and when should you ask clarifying questions?
sec07-card-sec07-R16.expected_back: If you disagree with a citation, do not argue at the roadside; explain your view in court, and ask any questions before the officer finishes the stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R17.front: What can happen if you refuse an officer's lawful order, and how must you act if placed under arrest?
sec07-card-sec07-R17.expected_back: Not obeying a lawful order or direction from an officer is illegal and can lead to arrest, and you should not resist if taken into custody.

sec07-card-sec07-R18.front: What is the main safety goal behind traffic enforcement warnings and citations?
sec07-card-sec07-R18.expected_back: Traffic enforcement aims to change unsafe behavior, reduce crashes and injuries and save lives, and a warning or citation is meant to deter future unsafe driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R19.front: What five steps will a law enforcement officer normally take when approaching your window during a stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R19.expected_back: During a stop the officer will usually greet you, say they are a law enforcement officer, ask for your license and insurance proof, explain the reason for the stop and check that your license is valid.

sec07-card-sec07-R20.front: Which types of driver credentials or identification are accepted during a Minnesota traffic stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R20.expected_back: Identification accepted at a traffic stop includes a Minnesota or out-of-state driver's license, a temporary license, a learner's permit, a military ID, and a consulate or international driver's license.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: Does taking or signing a traffic citation mean you are admitting guilt to the violation?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: Accepting a citation is not an admission of guilt; it only acknowledges that you received it and promises that you will appear in court if required.

sec07-card-sec07-R21.front: Where are citations sent for a hearing, and what alternative might the court offer instead of a conviction?
sec07-card-sec07-R21.expected_back: Citations go to a local jurisdiction for a hearing, and the court may offer a diversion program such as driver education training.

sec07-card-sec07-R22.front: How and where should you report concerns about an officer's conduct after a traffic stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R22.expected_back: Concerns about an officer's conduct go to the officer's agency or supervisor, using the officer information printed on the citation.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: What crime class, maximum prison sentence, and fine apply to fleeing a police officer in a motor vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: Fleeing a police officer in a motor vehicle is a felony punishable by up to three years and one day in prison, a fine of up to five thousand dollars, or both.

sec07-card-sec07-R23.front: How high do prison time and fines climb when fleeing police causes substantial harm, great bodily harm, or death?
sec07-card-sec07-R23.expected_back: If someone dies because a driver fled police, the penalty reaches up to ten years in prison and a twenty thousand dollars fine; great bodily harm brings up to seven years and fourteen thousand dollars; substantial bodily harm brings up to five years and ten thousand dollars.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: What does the law say about passing another vehicle that has stopped at a crosswalk for a pedestrian?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: Passing a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian is illegal, so when another vehicle stops, look for someone in the crosswalk and be ready to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.front: How must you drive around a blind pedestrian using a white or metallic cane or guide dog?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.expected_back: Watch for blind pedestrians carrying a white or metallic cane or using a guide dog, and do not honk or rev the engine near them.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.front: How does an unmarked crosswalk differ visually from a marked one, and where does it exist?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.expected_back: A marked crosswalk has solid white lines and may have signs or flashing lights, while an unmarked crosswalk is where a sidewalk meets the road with no lines painted.

sec07-card-sec07-R24.front: How is a pedestrian right-of-way violation penalized the first time versus a second time within one year?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.expected_back: Breaking pedestrian right-of-way laws is a misdemeanor, and a second violation within a year becomes a gross misdemeanor.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.front: In which three settings should you scan extra hard for pedestrians, and where must your car never stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.expected_back: Watch extra carefully for pedestrians on streets lined with parked cars, in poor visibility and wherever children are around, and never stop with your vehicle blocking a crosswalk.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.front: What four safety habits should pedestrians practice before and during a signalized intersection crossing?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.expected_back: Pedestrians should obey signals, wait a few feet back from the road for the WALK signal, still yield to vehicles already in the intersection, and make eye contact so drivers yield before they cross.

sec07-card-sec07-R27.front: Who yields when someone crosses away from a crosswalk, and which side must walkers use along a road without sidewalks?
sec07-card-sec07-R27.expected_back: Where there is no crosswalk a pedestrian yields to all vehicles, and if walking on the road is necessary, walks on the left side facing oncoming traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-R28.front: How can pedestrians stay visible in darkness, and what daytime hazard can still blind drivers to them?
sec07-card-sec07-R28.expected_back: At night or in poor visibility, pedestrians should wear light-colored clothing with reflective material or carry a flashlight, and expect that sun glare may keep drivers from seeing them.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.front: How does Minnesota traffic law classify bicycles riding on public roadways?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.expected_back: Bicycles are legal vehicles on Minnesota roads with the same rights and responsibilities as other vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.front: In which three limited situations may a motor vehicle enter a bicycle lane, and who goes first?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.expected_back: Driving in a bicycle lane is illegal except to park where allowed, to enter or leave the road, or to prepare for a turn, and you must yield to approaching bicyclists before moving into it.

sec07-card-sec07-R29.front: What exact sequence must you follow before turning right across a marked bicycle lane?
sec07-card-sec07-R29.expected_back: Before turning across a bicycle lane, make sure it is clear, signal, and move into the bicycle lane before you make the turn.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.front: What is the minimum side-to-side clearance required when overtaking a bicyclist in Minnesota?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.expected_back: When passing a bicyclist, leave at least three feet between the side of your car and the rider.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.front: When may you cross the center line to overtake a bicyclist even inside a no-passing zone?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.expected_back: When it is safe, you may cross the center of the road to pass a bicyclist even in a no passing zone, after making sure the rider is not signaling or turning left.

sec07-card-sec07-R30.front: How do Minnesota road rules treat electric-assist bicycles compared with gas-powered mopeds?
sec07-card-sec07-R30.expected_back: Electric-assist bicycles follow the same road rules as bicycles, while mopeds, which have a gas engine, follow different rules.

sec07-card-sec07-F43.front: Which direction must bicyclists ride, and what rules apply to their turns and traffic signals?
sec07-card-sec07-F43.expected_back: Bicyclists must obey all traffic laws, ride with the flow of traffic, signal every turn and obey traffic control signs, signals and devices.

sec07-card-sec07-F44.front: How may a bicyclist legally handle a stop sign when no vehicles are nearby?
sec07-card-sec07-F44.expected_back: At a stop sign a bicyclist must slow enough to be able to stop before the intersection or crosswalk, and may continue without stopping when no vehicle is nearby.

sec07-card-sec07-R31.front: Where in the lane do cyclists normally ride, and when may they move toward the center?
sec07-card-sec07-R31.expected_back: Bicyclists ride just to the right of faster traffic but may move toward the center of the lane for hazards, when passing or when turning left.

sec07-card-sec07-R32.front: Which arm positions let a bicyclist signal a right turn versus slowing or stopping?
sec07-card-sec07-R32.expected_back: A bicyclist signals a right turn with the left arm bent upward or the right arm held straight out, and signals stopping with the left arm bent down toward the ground.

sec07-card-sec07-R33.front: Under what two conditions may two bicyclists ride side by side on a Minnesota road?
sec07-card-sec07-R33.expected_back: Two bicyclists may ride side by side if they stay within one lane and do not impede traffic, and riders should wear helmets for safety.

sec07-card-sec07-R34.front: What lighting and winter tire equipment are legal on a bicycle riding at night in Minnesota?
sec07-card-sec07-R34.expected_back: At night a bicycle needs legal lights and reflectors and may use a white flashing front lamp, a red flashing rear lamp or both, and tires with spikes are allowed for traction.

sec07-card-sec07-R35.front: What duties apply when riding a bicycle on a sidewalk, and where is sidewalk riding banned by default?
sec07-card-sec07-R35.expected_back: On sidewalks and crosswalks a bicyclist yields to pedestrians, gives an audible signal before passing them, has a pedestrian's rights and duties, and may not ride on business district sidewalks unless local authorities allow it.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: Whom do Minnesota's traffic statutes govern, and across which roadways?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Out-of-state visitors, bicyclists on pavement, and brand-new permit holders all answer to the exact same public-road code.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: Under what five road, lane, or safety conditions may you leave the right side of a wide roadway?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Outside those five statutory reasons, drifting left of center invites head-on conflicts and keep-right stops.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: What two boundaries does Minnesota's basic speed law set using current conditions and posted signs?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Driving fifty-five during a whiteout blizzard still earns a speeding ticket because fifty-five was unreasonable for ice.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: How does the law treat creeping below a posted minimum speed limit when roads and weather are normal?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Slow rolling roadblocks on dry freeways trigger sudden braking waves and dangerous swerves from behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: With no sign posted and ideal conditions, what is Minnesota's statutory speed limit inside an alley?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Blind garage doors, trash bins, and stepping pedestrians leave zero room above a ten-mile-per-hour crawl.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Unless signs say otherwise, what is the ideal-condition speed limit on urban or town roads in Minnesota?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Don't guess twenty-five from other states—Minnesota's statewide unposted urban and town default is thirty.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: Where no sign stands outside alleys and urban streets, what default speed limit covers everywhere else?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Open rural two-lanes and county highways default cleanly to fifty-five unless higher or lower signs appear.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: How must you adjust your driving inside school zones when kids are out and inside work zones?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Unpredictable footsteps near schools and narrow cone tapers leave zero margin for normal cruising pace.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: What three numbers summarize Minnesota's unposted default speed ladder, and what overrides them?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Locking in ten, thirty, and fifty-five solves every unposted speed question on the Minnesota permit test.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: Under what exact road-type, posted-limit, and maneuver rules does Minnesota allow ten over the limit?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: This ten-mile-per-hour passing allowance applies strictly on two-lane highways posted fifty-five or higher—never on multi-lane freeways.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: What three things worsen simultaneously as your driving speed climbs?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Every extra ten miles per hour steals reaction time while multiplying crash impact energy.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: What legal privilege does a driver lose by barreling into an intersection above the speed limit?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Minnesota statute strips normal right-of-way from speeders—a favorite legal twist on knowledge exams.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: At how many miles per hour above the posted limit do extra Minnesota speeding fines kick in?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Crossing twenty-plus over the sign doubles down on fine surcharges and flags reckless speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: What license penalty hits anyone caught driving faster than one hundred miles per hour in Minnesota?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Exceeding one hundred triggers an automatic six-month-minimum license revocation—even on a clean first record.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: What must you do near a stopped flashing emergency vehicle, and what minimum surcharge hits violators?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Adding at least twenty-five dollars onto the speeding ticket underscores how seriously Minnesota guards roadside responders.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How does the penalty at twenty-plus over the limit escalate if you push past one hundred miles per hour?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: One hits your bank account with extra surcharges while triple digits takes your license for half a year.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Besides raising crash odds, how does high speed change what your eyes take in?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Peripheral awareness blurs at high speed, hiding cross-street cars and ditches until you actively scan wider.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: Around what five people or warning markers in the roadway—plus weather and rough pavement—must you drop speed?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Flares or reflectors on asphalt warn of fresh wrecks or stalled rigs ahead before headlights catch the metal.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: Which five road widths, alignments, or crossings require easing off your speed in advance?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Slowing before a hill crest or curve—never midway through—keeps weight balanced if a train or stalled car sits beyond.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: What two traction changes demand slower speeds whenever pavement turns to gravel or dirt?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Entering a loose gravel bend at asphalt speed washes the front or rear end sideways into the ditch.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: What two custom restrictions often appear on bridge approaches that drivers must watch for?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Narrow bridge decks lack shoulders and freeze faster than earth-backed roads, making passing or speeding hazardous.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: At least how far ahead of a turn must your blinker start, and how long does it stay flashing?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Canceling your signal mid-maneuver leaves cross-street drivers guessing whether you aborted the turn.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: When may hand and arm gestures be used in Minnesota, and in what two situations are they invalid?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Unlit arms vanish after dark and behind wide box-truck bodies, where electric lamps must carry the signal.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: Why must you rely strictly on electric turn signals at night or in wide-body vehicles?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Permit questions love asking whether hand signals rescue a broken blinker at midnight—in Minnesota, daylight is required.
sec05-card-sec05-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Nighttime and wide bodies hide arms

visual_sync.text_span: Nighttime and wide bodies hide arms

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Do traffic lanes still exist on unmarked or snow-covered asphalt, and how must you hold your path?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Fresh snow hides paint half the Minnesota winter, yet drivers must still hold neat single-file paths without weaving.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: What three-way space check and physical head move must come before switching lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Physically turning your head catches motorcycles and sedans tucked outside mirror coverage.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: What structural car parts create permanent blind spots, and what two glass issues create temporary ones?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Leaning slightly forward at corners peeks around thick front roof pillars while clean glass cuts low-sun glare.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: Whose blind spots must you avoid pacing inside—especially on multi-lane highways?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Semi-trailers carry massive front, rear, and dual-side blind zones where a lane-changing rig will never see your sedan.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: Because improper turns cause so many crashes, when should you move into your turn lane?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Setting up in your lane well upstream avoids last-second diagonal cuts across straight-moving traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: What wrong-lane mistake must you never make, and what scan and finish rule govern every turn?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: If you miss your turn bay, drive straight to the next block rather than swerving across neighbors.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: How should you hold your wheels and right foot while waiting for a gap to turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Brake pressure plus straight tires keeps a rear bumper impact from shoving you diagonally into oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: Waiting to turn left on green in Minnesota, how far into the intersection do you pull, and when might your gap come?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Lining your torso even with the cross-street curb sets a clean ninety-degree left turn once oncoming cars stop on yellow.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: How should you respond right away when the car directly ahead flicks on a left turn signal?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Left turners often halt abruptly in live lanes waiting out a long stream of oncoming traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Where do you start a left turn on marked or unmarked roads, and in which lane do you finish?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Finishing directly inside the lane just right of the center stripe leaves outer lanes clear for opposing right turners.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: How do you set up, scan, and finish a textbook right-hand turn?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Staying tight to the right curb start-to-finish prevents swinging wide into middle lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.question_text: How do left-turn and right-turn finish lanes contrast, and what steering technique applies to both?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.teaching_text: Smooth hand-over-hand steering hits your exact target lane on road tests without palming or crossing wrists.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: What lane rule governs intersections marked with two or more parallel turning lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Switching lanes halfway around a dual turn sideswipes the vehicle arcing inches beside you.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: What lane, stop, sign, and scanning steps are required before turning right on a red light?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Checking every direction catches both fast cross-traffic from the left and walkers stepping off your right curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: Under what sole street layout—and after what two checks—is turning left on red legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Turning left on red involving any two-way street crosses opposing lanes and draws an immediate ticket.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: What requirement do right-on-red and left-on-red share, and how do their street rules differ?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Pairing mandatory complete stops with the one-way-pair restriction solves every red-turn multiple-choice question.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: While edging up for a right turn on red, what unexpected oncoming movement must you watch out for?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Opposing left-turn bays often get a protected green arrow into the exact lane you want to enter.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.question_text: Whom must every red-light turner yield to, and what overrides turning on red altogether?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.teaching_text: Even an empty midnight intersection stays locked until green wherever a No Turn on Red board hangs.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.question_text: What two advantages lead engineers to build roundabouts in place of four-way stops?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.teaching_text: Smooth curved one-way circulation eliminates high-speed right-angle broadside and head-on left-turn crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: What speed, lane-choice, yielding, and sign checks belong on your approach to a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Choosing your lane before crossing the yield line avoids illegal mid-circle lane swaps.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: Whom must you yield to—and from which direction does circulating traffic come—before entering a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Because roundabouts spin counterclockwise, every vehicle already inside the ring approaches from your left.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Which direction do you circulate inside a roundabout, and what three maneuvers are banned inside it?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Halting inside the ring to wave someone in triggers immediate rear-end chain reactions behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: What must you do if an ambulance or fire rig approaches while you are circulating inside a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Stopping on the narrow curved apron blocks wide fire engines from threading the center island.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: Which long, wide, or hitched vehicles are legally allowed to straddle lanes through a roundabout?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Long trailers track tightly inward across lane paint, so passenger cars should never crowd beside them.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.question_text: When two large trucks enter a multi-lane roundabout side by side, which truck must yield?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.teaching_text: This unique Minnesota rule gives the inner-lane big rig swing room by having the outer right-hand rig hold back.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: What deadly crash type are J-turn intersections engineered to slash on four-lane divided highways?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Crossing two directions of sixty-five-mile-per-hour traffic straight across from a side stop causes severe T-bone fatalities.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: How does a side-street driver cross straight or go left at a Minnesota J-turn intersection?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Breaking a two-direction crossing into one right merge plus one downstream U-turn lets you judge one traffic stream at a time.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.question_text: When turning right into a J-turn with clear highway lanes, may you sweep straight across into the left-turn bay?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.teaching_text: Crossing directly into the median turn bay when safe minimizes your exposure in fast through lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: What priority rule governs the final U-turn phase of a J-turn before re-entering highway lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Protected inside the median bay, you wait calmly until opposing highway lanes open a generous acceleration gap.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.question_text: How may you cross a standard rural divided highway when its center median is wide enough to hold your car?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.teaching_text: Staying to the right side of a wide median opening keeps two opposing crossers from nose-blocking each other.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.question_text: Beyond two-stage crossing steps, what extra gap cushion must you allow when turning left onto a divided highway?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.teaching_text: Pulling out so close that sixty-five-mile-per-hour traffic must brake behind your accelerating car invites a rear-end hit.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.question_text: What motion defines a U-turn, and what traffic condition and sign rule govern whether it is legal?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.teaching_text: Forcing oncoming or trailing cars to slam brakes makes even an unposted turnaround unlawful.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: On which highways—and inside what hilltop or curve sight distance—are U-turns banned in Minnesota?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: One thousand feet gives fifty-five-mile-per-hour traffic roughly twelve seconds to spot your car swinging sideways.

sec05-card-sec05-R22.question_text: On a road with two or more lanes going your way, how wide may you swing to complete a tight U-turn?
sec05-card-sec05-R22.teaching_text: Minnesota lets wide-turning vehicles use the outer lane and brief shoulder edge rather than stopping sideways.

sec05-card-sec05-R23.question_text: Where must you position your vehicle on a single-lane direction road if moving slowly enough to create a hazard?
sec05-card-sec05-R23.teaching_text: Tucking right opens sightlines behind you and reduces rear-end closure surprises on two-lane country roads.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: On highways with multiple lanes in your direction, how should you use the right-hand and left-most lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Clearing the left-most lane lets faster vehicles overtake cleanly instead of weaving across right lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R24.question_text: What five situations make driving outside the right-hand highway lane completely legal?
sec05-card-sec05-R24.teaching_text: Preparing for a left turn, left freeway split, or work-zone lane shift justifies leaving the right lane.

sec05-card-sec05-R27.question_text: When does passing demand extra caution, and what front-and-rear checks come before pulling left?
sec05-card-sec05-R27.teaching_text: Pulling left without checking behind sideswipes a car that already moved into the passing lane behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-R28.question_text: How do you signal both ends of a pass, and what mirror sight tells you to pull back right?
sec05-card-sec05-R28.teaching_text: Signaling right and waiting until the entire passed vehicle shows in your rearview mirror prevents clipping their bumper.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.question_text: In Minnesota, before closing within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle must you be back in your right lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.teaching_text: Closing speeds double on two-lane highways, turning one hundred feet into less than a single heartbeat.

sec05-card-sec05-R25.question_text: Which two separate Minnesota passing laws both rely on the exact one-hundred-foot measurement?
sec05-card-sec05-R25.teaching_text: Linking oncoming clearance with intersections, tunnels, underpasses, and rail crossings locks in both hundred-foot rules together.
sec05-card-sec05-R25.must_match_memory_hook: Oncoming return and four no-pass spots

visual_sync.text_span: Oncoming return and four no-pass spots

sec05-card-sec05-F39.question_text: How do No Passing signs, a solid yellow stripe on your side, and double solid yellow lines restrict overtaking?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.teaching_text: Whether a single solid stripe hugs your side or twin yellows split center, crossing to pass is illegal.

sec05-card-sec05-R26.question_text: How does a single solid yellow stripe on your side differ in reach from double solid yellow lines?
sec05-card-sec05-R26.teaching_text: With mixed stripes oncoming cars might have a broken stripe, whereas double solid locks down both directions.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.question_text: At least how many feet of clear road ahead must you see before passing on any hill or curve?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.teaching_text: Seven hundred feet is a signature Minnesota passing-sightline number that trips up students guessing five hundred.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.question_text: Within one hundred feet of which four roadway structures or crossings is passing strictly illegal?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.teaching_text: Cross traffic, dark tunnel walls, pier columns, and trains eliminate side escape room at all four spots.

sec05-card-sec05-R29.question_text: When must you abort starting a pass, and what must you do while someone overtakes you?
sec05-card-sec05-R29.teaching_text: Racing a passing driver traps them head-on in the opposing lane and violates Minnesota traffic law.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.question_text: In what three road or left-turn situations is passing on the right legal when safe?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.teaching_text: Even when one of those three conditions applies, never leave main pavement to squeeze past.

sec05-card-sec05-R30.question_text: May you dip into a bike lane, paved shoulder, or gravel edge to pass a left-turning car on the right?
sec05-card-sec05-R30.teaching_text: Unlike Wisconsin's paved-shoulder rule, Minnesota forbids leaving the main travel roadway onto shoulders or bike lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.question_text: Who is the sole exception allowed to reverse on a freeway, and what criminal charges can street backing bring?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.teaching_text: Backing up after missing a freeway ramp draws careless or reckless driving charges and risks deadly high-speed crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-R31.question_text: Into which lane should you reverse when backing out of a driveway, and what crossing move is off-limits?
sec05-card-sec05-R31.teaching_text: Backing across multiple lanes exposes your blind rear end to both directions of traffic simultaneously.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Where must you come to a halt at a steady red light, and when may you proceed?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Halting behind the stop line or crosswalk keeps pedestrian paths and cross traffic open until the signal changes.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Under what conditions may you turn right on a red light, and what posted sign blocks it?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Rolling through a right-on-red without stopping first or missing a No Turn on Red notice earns an intersection ticket.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: Under what exact street-direction and yielding rules may a Minnesota driver turn left on red?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Turning left on red works strictly from a one-way street onto a matching one-way cross street after stopping and yielding.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: What starting step do right-on-red and left-on-red share, and what extra road restriction applies only to left-on-red?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Right-on-red works from two-way streets when clear, whereas left-on-red demands connecting two one-way streets after stopping.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: What must you do at a red arrow, and when may you move in the arrow's direction?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red light, a red arrow forbids turning in its direction until a green indication replaces it.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: How does a steady red arrow match a steady red ball, and how is its reach narrower?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Both demand a complete stop behind the line, yet a red arrow regulates only traffic moving in its pointed direction.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: What three steps—stopping, yielding, and proceeding—govern a flashing red traffic light?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Treat flashing red intersections with full stop-sign discipline, yielding to earlier cars and pedestrians before rolling clear.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: Contrast when you may enter the intersection after stopping for a steady red light versus a flashing red light?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Steady red pins you behind the stop bar until green, while flashing red lets you proceed once clear after stopping.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: What does a steady yellow light or arrow warn, and how do you decide between stopping and continuing?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Steady yellow clears the intersection ahead of red, so brake smoothly whenever safe rather than racing the change.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: If you are already waiting inside an intersection to turn when yellow changes to red, what must you do?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Backing toward the crosswalk invites hitting stopped traffic behind you, so clear the turn promptly once oncoming cars stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: How should you drive through a flashing yellow light or flashing yellow arrow?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Ease speed and yield to pedestrians or vehicles already occupying the crossing before moving through on flashing yellow.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: To whom must a driver yield when turning left or making a U-turn on a flashing yellow signal?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Misjudging fast oncoming traffic on a permissive flashing yellow causes severe broadside left-turn and U-turn collisions.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Contrast what a steady yellow signal announces against what a flashing yellow signal instructs?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Steady yellow signals an imminent red phase, whereas flashing yellow stays permissive provided you proceed cautiously and yield.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: Even with a circular green light, to which three groups must you still yield before going or turning?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Green grants permission only after clearing stragglers in the box, oncoming traffic on left turns, and crossing pedestrians.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What turning right and conflict protection does a illuminated green arrow provide?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: A green arrow holds conflicting oncoming and cross movements on red so your turn lane flows protected.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: When turning left, how does your oncoming-traffic duty change between a circular green light and a green arrow?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Circular green leaves left-turners yielding to opposing lanes, while a green arrow gives protected clearance.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: What safety check should pedestrians still make when the Walk signal lights up, and what if it changes mid-crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Looking for turning cars before stepping off the curb prevents crosswalk strikes even during a legal Walk phase.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: How does a flashing raised hand or Don't Walk signal treat pedestrians on the curb versus those mid-crosswalk?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Flashing orange clears the street before cross traffic gets green, barring new step-offs while letting crossers finish.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: What must pedestrians on the sidewalk and anyone caught mid-street do when Don't Walk turns steady?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: A steady raised hand means conflicting lanes have or are getting green, so anyone still crossing must clear fast.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: Compare pedestrian rules across Walk, flashing Don't Walk, and steady Don't Walk?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Start after checking on Walk, finish without starting on flashing hand, and clear quickly on steady hand.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: What traffic management purpose do overhead lane-use control signals serve, and do standard signs still apply?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Overhead lane signals flip directional capacity for rush-hour peaks while leaving every other sign and signal active.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: What does a steady downward-pointing green arrow suspended above a travel lane tell you?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: A downward green arrow confirms that reversible or managed lane is open to traffic moving your way.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: Contrast a steady downward green arrow above a lane against a steady red X?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Downward green welcomes you into that lane, whereas a steady red X warns oncoming traffic or closure owns it.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: What is happening when a steady yellow X lights up above your lane, and how should you respond?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Moving safely out of the lane during steady yellow X beats getting stranded head-on when steady red X appears.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: On a freeway, what does a steady downward-pointing yellow arrow over your lane announce?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Spotting an overhead downward yellow arrow early lets you signal and merge smoothly before barrels or crashes block ahead.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: What shared lane action do an overhead steady yellow X and downward-pointing steady yellow arrow call for, and why?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Both tell you to exit the lane promptly, whether reversible direction control is flipping or a freeway lane is closing.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: Which single maneuver does a flashing yellow X over a lane allow, and why is caution essential?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Drivers approaching from the opposite direction can enter that same center lane simultaneously to make their own left turns.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: What does a flashing downward yellow arrow above a freeway lane permit?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Unlike a steady downward yellow arrow closing the lane, a flashing downward yellow arrow keeps the lane open cautiously.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: Contrast how you may use a lane under a flashing yellow X versus a flashing downward yellow arrow?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Flashing yellow X restricts the lane strictly to cautious left turns, while flashing downward yellow permits cautious freeway travel.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: What rule applies whenever a steady red X illuminates over a lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Entering a steady red X lane puts you into closed work space or head-on reversible rush-hour traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: What are freeway ramp meters, and how do they manage merging traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Red-yellow-green ramp signals break up platoons of entering cars so freeway mainlines stay flowing smoothly.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: At an active freeway ramp meter, how many vehicles are allowed to go on each green light?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Piggybacking through a ramp meter behind the car ahead defeats spacing and earns a red-light ticket.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.question_text: In pavement markings, what traffic-direction rule distinguishes white lines from yellow lines?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.teaching_text: Reading line color instantly tells you whether adjacent lanes move with you or carry oncoming headlights.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: Which relative flow of traffic do white pavement lines separate?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Seeing white paint on both sides of your car confirms neighboring lanes travel the same way you do.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: What do regular white dashed lines allow, and what do shorter, thicker white dashes warn?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Spotting stubby, wide white dashes gives you early warning to merge before an exit-only or merge lane runs out.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.question_text: How does the shape of white dashed lines shift when your travel lane is about to end?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.teaching_text: Unlike long standard dashes marking normal multi-lane dividers, short fat white blocks signal an ending lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: What lane-change guidance does a single solid white line give, and what four other features does solid white mark?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Stay in your lane across single solid white, which also outlines crosswalks, stop bars, parking stalls, and road edges.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: What strict rule applies where double solid white lines separate same-direction lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Crossing double solid white lines into or out of managed lanes, tunnels, or bridges is strictly prohibited.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.question_text: How does the strength of the rule escalate from a single solid white line to double solid white lines?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.teaching_text: Single solid white discourages lane weaving whereas parallel double solid white makes crossing illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: Which two rider types may use a lane marked by a solid white line and bicycle symbol, and heading which way?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Dedicated bike lanes serve standard and electric-assist bicycles moving strictly in the same direction as adjacent cars.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: What relationship between traffic streams do yellow pavement markings indicate?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Yellow paint on your left warns that lanes beyond that line carry oncoming traffic heading straight toward you.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: How do a solid yellow centerline and a broken dashed yellow centerline differ for overtaking?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Broken yellow dashes open legal passing when clear ahead, whereas solid yellow locks you into your lane.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.question_text: Is overtaking allowed inside a no-passing zone, and which yellow line marks that restriction?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.teaching_text: Crossing a solid yellow no-passing stripe gambles head-on where hills, curves, or junctions block sightlines.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: When a centerline pairs a solid yellow stripe alongside yellow dashes, which stripe governs you?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Check the stripe bordering your own lane—dashes on your side allow passing while solid on your side bars it.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: Who is allowed to pass across a double solid yellow centerline?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Twin solid yellow stripes ban overtaking for traffic traveling in both directions alike.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.question_text: Compare passing rights on a two-lane road marked with single yellow dashes versus dashes paired with one solid line?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.teaching_text: Single broken yellow opens passing both ways, whereas adding a solid stripe blocks whichever lane touches the solid side.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: On an undivided highway with two lanes each way separated by double solid yellow lines, may you cross yellow to pass?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Use the two lanes on your own side of the road and never cross double yellow into opposing fast lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.question_text: When a two-lane two-way road carries no-passing markings for both directions, which drivers may overtake?
