sec10-card-sec10-R16.teaching_text: Sightline limits in both directions lock every driver behind lead vehicles until dashed markings return.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.question_text: When a physical solid divider separates a two-way multilane highway, what road feature is missing along the inner edges?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.teaching_text: Raised or concrete center dividers sit flush against fast left lanes without inner breakdown shoulders.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: What do white lane arrows near intersections require, and how do multi-arrow lanes differ?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Single turn arrows—often paired with ONLY—commit you to turning, while combined straight-and-turn arrows offer both.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: Why are dedicated intersection turn lanes bordered by a solid white stripe next to through lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Diving out of or into a turn pocket right at the stop bar sideswipes rolling through-lane cars.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: How is a shared center left-turn-only lane painted, and which directions may enter it to turn left?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: Parallel outside solid and inside dashed yellow stripes let drivers from either direction pull in strictly to turn left.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.question_text: On a two-way three-lane street, what single purpose belongs to the middle lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.teaching_text: Never use the middle lane of a three-lane street for overtaking or cruising; it holds left-turning cars only.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.question_text: What yellow lines border a reversible lane, and when may you cross into it?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.teaching_text: Wait for an overhead green arrow or posted time permission before crossing dashed double yellow stripes.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.question_text: Distinguish the yellow stripes of a shared center left-turn lane from those of a reversible lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.teaching_text: Solid outside with dashed inside marks shared left turns, whereas twin dashed yellows on both sides mark reversible lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.question_text: How many occupants qualify a car for a carpool lane, how is it marked, and where does it usually sit?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.teaching_text: Diamond pavement symbols and Carpool Only notices reserve that far-left freeway lane for vehicles carrying two or more people.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.question_text: Which paint colors may separate a freeway carpool lane from general-purpose lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.teaching_text: Watch specific white or yellow separation stripes along carpool corridors to see where entering and exiting are allowed.

sec10-card-sec10-R21.question_text: What role do large words painted directly on the roadway—like School Zone Ahead—play?
sec10-card-sec10-R21.teaching_text: Stenciled lane lettering reinforces roadside signs right in your forward gaze before you reach school zones or hazards.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.question_text: When a traffic officer directs an intersection, how do their hand signals rank against lights, signs, and paint?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.teaching_text: Live traffic officers see crashes, emergencies, or gridlock the light timer cannot, so obey their hand commands even through red.

sec10-card-sec10-R23.question_text: Who may direct traffic on occasion alongside police, and whose commands take top priority when an officer is present?
sec10-card-sec10-R23.teaching_text: Authorized flaggers or staff sometimes direct flow, and whenever law enforcement steps in, hand commands supersede fixed controls.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.question_text: Which hand gesture and whistle blast do most traffic officers pair together to command a stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.teaching_text: One raised open palm facing your windshield paired with one long whistle blast unmistakably commands a full stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.question_text: How do traffic officers signal you to start or keep moving, and what tool helps after dark?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.teaching_text: A waving arm motion with quick short whistle blasts—guided by a flashlight beam in low light—keeps traffic rolling.

sec10-card-sec10-R22.question_text: Contrast a traffic officer's whistle and hand cues between stop and go?
sec10-card-sec10-R22.teaching_text: Pair one long whistle and flat palm with stopping, and rapid short blasts plus a wave with moving.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: How does Minnesota treat holding a driver's license, and what can take it away?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Viewing driving as a conditional privilege explains why breaking traffic statutes or missing state requirements ends it.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: Which violations land on your Minnesota DVS record, and what restrictions can serious or repeat offenses trigger?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Out-of-state tickets follow you home onto your DVS file and can restrict where, when, or what you drive.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: Where can a Minnesota driver request a personal copy of their driving record?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Pulling your own record online lets you verify clean status or check past entries anytime.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: What are Minnesota's three ways of withdrawing a license, and how do you learn the steps back?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Keeping your mailing address current matters because DPS mails your withdrawal notice with exact reinstatement instructions.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: Which official publication details how commercial driver's license holders lose CDL privileges?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Commercial operators face stricter disqualification triggers spelled out separately inside Minnesota's CDL handbook.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: Which pattern of traffic tickets, or single crash-linked conviction, can suspend your Minnesota license?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Contributing to a crash with death, injury, or major property damage risks suspension even without prior tickets.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: When does a traffic violation committed outside Minnesota trigger a license suspension back home?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Crossing state borders offers zero shield when the same conduct would suspend a driver inside Minnesota.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Which court fitness ruling or unreported health issue can suspend your driving privileges?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Hiding a disqualifying medical change from the state risks suspension alongside court findings of unfitness.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: Within what lookback window does a second conviction for passing a red-flashing school bus bring suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Blowing past extended bus lights a second time inside five years puts your license straight into suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: How do missed court appearances, unpaid vehicle fines, or traffic misdemeanors affect your license?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Ignoring a ticket's court date or fine deadline turns a routine citation into a suspended license.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: Does Minnesota require multiple misdemeanor traffic convictions before suspension becomes possible, or can one suffice?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Unlike minor petty citations that stack over time, a single misdemeanor traffic conviction is a standalone suspension ground.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: What license action can follow when a court finds someone under twenty-one drove after consuming alcohol?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Zero-tolerance rules expose drivers under twenty-one to suspension after any court-found drinking and driving.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: What happens to your driving privileges if you are convicted of stealing gasoline?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Minnesota ties pump drive-offs directly to your driver's license, making fuel theft a statutory suspension ground.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: May you ever let a friend borrow your license or permit, and what penalty covers unlawful license lending?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Handing your card to someone else, or misusing your own for an unlawful act, puts your driving privilege on ice.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Which three credential or exam-room frauds carry a Minnesota license suspension?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Altering an ID, filing a phony application, or sitting for someone else's exam triggers license suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: If someone else takes part of your license exam for you, who faces suspension under Minnesota rules?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Sending a ringer into the written or road exam suspends the applicant right alongside the test-taker.
sec13-card-sec13-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Both applicant and stand-in risk suspension

visual_sync.text_span: Both applicant and stand-in risk suspension

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: What can happen to your driver's license if you give a false identity to a police officer?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Giving an officer a fake name or someone else's details adds license suspension on top of criminal trouble.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: Using or lending your ID to buy tobacco or alcohol for which underage groups can suspend your license?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Loaning an ID for underage purchases links directly to suspension under Minnesota's handbook rules.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: How can falling behind on court-ordered child support affect your Minnesota driver's license?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Even with a spotless driving record, nonpayment of court-ordered child support can suspend driving privileges.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: What happens if a check written for a state or license-agent fee bounces, and when does the suspension lift?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Clearing both the original dishonored check amount and every added fee restores privileges immediately.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: Which stronger withdrawal hits a driver who fails or refuses an alcohol or controlled-substance test?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Saying no to chemical testing escalates straight past a temporary suspension into full license revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: What license withdrawal follows a conviction for impaired driving, vehicular manslaughter, or another crime behind the wheel?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Convictions for impaired operation or criminal acts while driving strip your license via revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: What happens to your driving privileges after any felony conviction in which a motor vehicle was used?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Even if the felony was not a traffic statute, using a car in its commission triggers revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: Exceeding what exact speed threshold on conviction can revoke your Minnesota driver's license?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Crossing one hundred miles per hour jumps past ordinary speeding fines into license-revocation territory.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: What license withdrawal can follow a conviction for fleeing a police officer?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Trying to outrun flashing squad lights carries criminal consequences plus full license revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: Failing to perform which three post-crash duties, especially after injury or death, can revoke your license?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Leaving a crash scene without stopping, sharing identity, and helping injured people triggers revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: Which false statements about vehicle ownership or operation can trigger license revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Perjury under oath, falsified vehicle legal papers, or lying to DPS carries revocation consequences.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: How many jailable traffic pleas or bail forfeitures within one year can revoke your Minnesota license?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Stacking three serious jail-eligible traffic violations inside twelve months crosses Minnesota's revocation threshold.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: How can driving or lending a vehicle lacking Minnesota no-fault insurance cost you your license?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Both knowingly operating someone else's uninsured car and letting others drive yours uninsured risk revocation.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: If you borrow a friend's car while knowing the owner carries zero no-fault insurance, what withdrawal threatens you?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Not owning the car offers no excuse once a misdemeanor conviction shows you knew coverage was missing.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: Which severity of school-bus red-light conviction escalates penalty status to license revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Aggravated school-bus violations charged as gross misdemeanors trigger revocation rather than simple suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: What license penalty can follow a conviction for possessing or selling controlled substances while operating a vehicle?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Even without proven driving impairment, drug possession or sales behind the wheel can revoke your license.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: When does an out-of-state driving offense count toward revoking your Minnesota license?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Minnesota applies its own revocation yardstick to serious convictions reported from any other state.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: What must you complete after a suspension period ends, and when is a brand-new license application required?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: Satisfying every listed condition and fee restores your card unless expiry or a name-or-address change requires reapplying.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: Once a revocation term finishes, what notice items, testing step, and application are mandatory?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Revocation wipes out your prior credential, requiring ID-verified exams and a fresh license application.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: Contrast getting your privileges back after a suspension versus returning from a revocation?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Suspension usually restores your existing valid card after fees, whereas revocation demands exams and reapplying.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: Who may qualify for a Minnesota limited license, and what timing hurdle often applies first?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Not every suspended or revoked driver qualifies immediately because mandatory waiting periods must pass first.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: Which four essential destinations or family errands may a Minnesota limited license cover?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Social outings stay strictly illegal when your limited card covers only work, counseling, post-secondary classes, and dependent care.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: Can someone apply for a Minnesota limited license as an everyday starter card or use it for casual errands?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Limited licenses exist solely as restricted relief during suspension or revocation for approved essential trips.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: Under what overarching rule does DPS cancel a license, and what disability or testing examples trigger it?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Cancellation steps in when physical or mental conditions bar safe driving or a driver fails a DPS-requested exam.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: How long does cancellation last if you put false or misleading facts on a Minnesota license application?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: Because the longer period governs, fixing bad data on day ten still leaves fifty days of cancellation.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.question_text: Beyond disabilities, failed DPS retests, and false applications, what two legal grounds bring license cancellation?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.teaching_text: Minnesota cancels credentials both when someone never legally qualified and when a criminal statute orders cancellation.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: What central question decides most license cancellations, alongside specific criminal punishments?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Unlike suspension for conduct, cancellation primarily asks whether you legally qualify to hold that card at all.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: What book should you read and what four basic parts should you check regularly before driving on public roads?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Spotting a dead bulb, bald tread, torn wiper, or silent horn in your driveway beats discovering it mid-storm.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: What three setup and seating habits must happen right when you climb in before rolling?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Dialing in mirrors and belting every rider before shifting out of park eliminates dangerous one-handed adjustments in traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: At least how many independent brake systems must every car and truck carry, and what are they?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: If hydraulic pressure fails on the foot pedal, a separate mechanical parking or emergency brake can still halt your wheels.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: How do front-and-rear bumper requirements differ between private passenger cars and pickups or vans?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Work pickups and cargo vans often haul trailers or step platforms, so Minnesota allows rear reflectors in place of a rear bumper.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: Under what condition may a pickup truck or van legally skip having a rear bumper?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Exam distractors claim every vehicle needs two bumpers or let passenger sedans swap in reflectors—neither is true.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: Which audible warning device must every standard vehicle carry, and which three sound makers are off-limits?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Reserving bells, sirens, and whistles strictly for emergency rigs ensures drivers never mistake a prankster for an ambulance.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: For what sole safety reason should you sound your horn, and what two casual uses are banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Driveway arrival honks and angry blasts desensitize neighbors and startle walkers without preventing a collision.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: From glass and exhaust to rear lamps and belts, what core items must a street-legal Minnesota car carry?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Missing a single required item—even a tiny white license-plate bulb or cracked safety glass—justifies a patrol stop.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: Aside from motorcycles, what front headlamp and rear brake-lamp setup must every motor vehicle have?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Driving one-eyed with a burned-out headlamp makes oncoming night drivers mistake your wide car for a narrow motorcycle.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: At least how many feet ahead must your high-beam headlights illuminate objects on the roadway?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Three hundred fifty feet gives rural night drivers just enough runway to spot deer or dark pedestrians at highway pace.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: Why must you replace a cracked headlight housing even if the bulb inside still glows?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Water droplets and road dust inside a fractured lens starve your own sightline while blinding oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: Up to what share of light output can grimy headlights lose, and how often should you wipe them?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Minnesota winter road salt coats plastic lenses fast, slashing three-quarters of your night vision unless wiped with your windshield.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: At least how often should a shop inspect your headlights to confirm proper aim?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Potholes and frost heaves knock headlamps upward into oncoming eyes or downward short of highway hazards.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: While daytime running lights turn on up front automatically, which two lighting sets stay completely off?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Cruising into dusk or blizzard spray on daytime lights leaves the entire back of your car invisible from behind.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: During what hours, five weather types, and visibility distance must your full headlights stay switched on?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Minnesota mandates full headlights the moment rain, snow, hail, sleet, or fog hits—even at high noon.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: Besides headlamps and brake lamps, what rear tag lamp and directional bulbs must stay working?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: A burned-out white rear tag bulb is one of the easiest night equipment citations an officer can spot.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: How do three hundred fifty feet and five hundred feet apply to different Minnesota headlight rules?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Keep equipment reach at three-fifty separate from weather visibility at five hundred so test choices never blur together.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: Why must you still twist your headlight switch on at sunset even when daytime running lights glow?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Dashboard gauges glow brightly in modern cabins, tricking dusk drivers into forgetting their dark rear bumper.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: Which three categories of vehicles are the sole ones authorized to display blue lights in Minnesota?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Mounting decorative blue bulbs on a personal car or pickup violates restricted emergency-lighting statutes.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: Which six work, school, farm, or responder vehicle groups are permitted to run flashing lights?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Flashing beacons warn fast traffic of slow, wide, or roadside-stopped working vehicles ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: Which exact three vehicle types are authorized to run high-intensity strobe lamps?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Bright rooftop strobes punch through rural blowing snow and fog where school buses, plows, and mail carriers stop.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: How do flashing-light rules and blue-light rules split between snowplows and tow trucks?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Permit questions love slipping tow trucks or farm tractors onto the blue-light list—remember blue stays plow, maintenance, and emergency.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: How do school buses and rural mail carrier vehicles compare across the flashing-light and strobe-lamp lists?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Spotting rural mail carriers as strobe-authorized yet absent from the general flashing list nails a subtle equipment distinction.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: What noise rule makes a muffler mandatory, and what invisible deadly gas must you inspect exhaust pipes for?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Odorless carbon monoxide seeping from a rusted muffler into a closed winter cabin causes fatal drowsiness in minutes.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: When must a vehicle add an extra side mirror beyond a standard inside rearview mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Box vans and loaded pickups lose center-mirror sightlines completely, making external side glass mandatory.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: Which two vehicle situations trigger Minnesota's requirement for an extra side mirror alongside the rearview mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Renting a moving truck or stacking cargo above the tailgate shifts all rearward tracking onto outside mirrors.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: What does Minnesota require regarding seat belt presence, occupant use, and belt upkeep?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Twisted, frayed, or jammed webbing cannot lock cleanly under crash loads when every rider needs protection.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: Why do airbags still need seat belts beside them, and why is cluttering your dashboard dangerous?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Airbags deploy at explosive speed—hurling phones or cups on the dash into faces while offering zero rollover ejection hold.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: What six kinds of tire damage should you scan for often, and what trunk backup needs pressure checks too?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: A flat spare tire leaves you stranded on a dark shoulder right after a sidewall bulge blows out.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: How does tire traction on gravel or dirt roads compare with concrete or asphalt?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Rolling pebbles act like tiny ball bearings underfoot, stretching braking distance and sliding corners wide.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: Where do you look up your car's recommended tire pressure—and what printed number should you ignore as a target?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: Inflating to the tire sidewall's maximum rating over-stiffens ride grip instead of matching your car's weight balance.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: At what two times is checking tire pressure accurate before adding or bleeding air?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Highway rolling heats air inside rubber and spikes gauge readings artificially above true cold inflation.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: Why is inflating to the number molded onto the rubber sidewall a classic maintenance mistake?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Permit exams love testing door-sticker-and-manual target pressure against the molded sidewall decoy number.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: Why must you wait at least three hours after a trip rather than checking tire pressure right at a highway stop?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Bleeding air from hot highway tires leaves them dangerously underinflated once they cool overnight.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: Below what exact fraction of an inch does tire tread become illegal in Minnesota?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: Worn-out grooves cannot channel rain or slush away, floating your car into a hydroplane skid.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: How do you place a penny into your tire groove, and what sight proves legal tread remains?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Testing the shallowest groove ensures uneven alignment wear is not hiding an illegal bald strip inside.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: How does Abraham Lincoln's head on a penny connect to Minnesota's one-sixteenth-inch tread floor?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: From the coin rim to the top of Lincoln's hair measures one-sixteenth of an inch—an instant pocket gauge.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.question_text: What six glass conditions—plus hanging items—are illegal across your windshield and windows?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.teaching_text: Peephole winter scraping or swinging mirror charms hide whole pedestrians and cars inside blind angles.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.question_text: Where may state stickers, toll tags, navigation screens, and driver-monitoring sensors legally sit?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.teaching_text: Tucking navigation low and sensors tight around the mirror preserves clean eye-height sightlines across intersections.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.question_text: How does Minnesota treat authorized toll tags and park stickers compared with items hanging from your mirror?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.teaching_text: Swinging air fresheners, beads, or parking tags between your eyes and the glass draw avoidable traffic stops.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.question_text: What two optical effects may never be added to a windshield by any film or treatment?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.teaching_text: Darkened front glass starves night vision while mirrored film bounces blinding sun glare at oncoming traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.question_text: What two ratings must appear on the label of side or rear window tint applied since August nineteen eighty-five?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.teaching_text: Compliance labels let officers verify legal light percentages without guessing by eye.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.question_text: Which specific windows and vehicle types are the sole ones allowed tint darker than fifty percent or shinier than twenty?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.teaching_text: Standard passenger sedans must keep side and rear glass at fifty percent light or brighter so drivers and officers see clearly.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: Even on vans, limos, or pickups allowed dark rear glass, is sub-fifty-percent tint ever legal on the windshield?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Every single vehicle class needs full forward light transmission to spot dark pedestrians at night.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.question_text: Which two clearing systems must keep a glass windshield and cabin windows free of rain, steam, and frost?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.teaching_text: Driving with fogged-over interior glass in January blinds you just as badly as broken exterior wipers.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.question_text: Why does Minnesota require fenders or wheel guards over passenger-vehicle tires?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.teaching_text: Uncovered spinning tires launch rocks, slush, and blinding rooster-tail spray straight into windshields behind you.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.question_text: What three maintenance habits keep your vehicle sipping less fuel?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.teaching_text: Soft tires and wrong-viscosity oil add rolling and internal drag on every single mile you drive.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.question_text: From trip planning and trunk weight to highway gears, what six behind-the-wheel habits stretch fuel farthest?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.teaching_text: Jackrabbit starts, speeding, and hauling dead trunk weight burn extra gas without getting you across town noticeably sooner.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.question_text: What five travel alternatives does the manual recommend whenever practical to cut fuel use?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.teaching_text: Sharing rides or walking short errands saves fuel, wear, and cold-start emissions simultaneously.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: What physical check outside the car and four-way scan inside come before shifting into reverse?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Toddlers, bikes, and low pets sit completely below rear glass and bumper height until a quick walk-around spots them.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: Where must your eyes stay locked the entire time you reverse, and into which lane do you back?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Staring down at a dashboard backup screen blinds you to cross-sidewalk joggers and approaching street cars.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: What is the maximum legal distance between your curbside tires and the curb when parallel parked?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Parking wider than one foot narrows the active street lane and invites clipped side mirrors.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: After parallel parking, how should you leave your front wheels, gear selector, and brake set—and why?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Aiming tires toward the curb ensures any accidental roll catches the concrete edge instead of drifting into traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: Which three pedestrian or corner zones are flatly off-limits for parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Blocking sidewalks or crosswalks forces wheelchair users and kids out into blind intersection traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: Within how many feet of an intersection crosswalk is parking illegal in Minnesota?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Twenty open feet lets approaching drivers spot short children stepping off the curb before reaching the stripes.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Within how many feet of a roadside stop post, flashing beacon, or traffic signal is parking banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Tall vans or trucks parked right up to a stop post hide the octagon completely from trailing drivers.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: Within how many feet of the nearest rail at a railroad crossing is parking illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Fifty feet keeps parked cars clear of crossing gates, overhang clearance, and train-spotting sightlines.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: Within how many feet of a fire hydrant is parking prohibited in Minnesota?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Note Minnesota's ten-foot hydrant buffer—shorter than fifteen-foot states, making ten a classic state exam check.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How do ten, twenty, thirty, and fifty feet match up across Minnesota's four no-parking curb buffers?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Climbing ten-twenty-thirty-fifty from hydrant to crosswalk to signal to rail locks in four exam questions at once.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: Which three structural or access chokepoints also ban parking completely?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Bridges and tunnels have zero breakdown room, and blocking driveway aprons traps residents inside their property.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: What do we call stopping in the travel lane alongside a curb-parked car, and is it legal?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Even flicking on hazard flashers for a thirty-second pickup still blocks live lanes and draws a double-parking ticket.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: What four painted, posted, work-site, or postal curb spots also forbid parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Parking opposite a narrow street excavation pinches the remaining gap shut for fire trucks and buses.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Before swinging open a roadside car door, whom must you scan for and how long may the door stay open?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Flinging a traffic-side door into a cyclist's path causes severe dooring crashes before riders can swerve.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: Which direction do you turn your front wheels whenever parking facing downhill?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Whether a concrete curb or gravel shoulder borders the road, turning right directs a downhill roll out of traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Which way must you turn your front wheels when parking facing uphill beside a curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Turning left away from the curb lets the back of your right front tire wedge safely against the concrete.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Which way do your front wheels turn when parked facing uphill along a road with no curb?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: With no raised concrete to catch a left-turned wheel, turning right rolls a runaway vehicle away from live lanes.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Across all downhill and uphill parking setups, which lone setup turns wheels away from the road edge?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Every other hill scenario turns toward the edge—remembering that single uphill-curb outlier makes hill questions effortless.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: How do you align and space your car beside the lead parked vehicle to begin parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Roughly eighteen inches side clearance gives clean swing room without crowding the adjacent travel lane.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What three steering cuts guide you into the center of a parallel parking space?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Reversing sharp right angles you in, sharp left tucks the nose clear, and right centers you beside the curb.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: What front and rear lamps—and minimum visibility footage—must mark a vehicle parked along a highway at night?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Unlit dark metal on a sixty-mile-per-hour shoulder gets struck fast without five-hundred-foot front and rear warning.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: Where must you place a parked car on a state highway, and what if mechanical failure leaves it immovable?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Setting out reflective markers or signals gives fast-closing drivers advance warning around an immobile breakdown.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: Which warning lights should a highway-parked car run, and what beam setting applies if headlights stay on?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Leaving high beams blazing on a shoulder blinds oncoming drivers and hides walkers standing around your car.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: Who bears responsibility for passenger safety, belt compliance, and age-matched child restraints inside your car?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Keep your car in park until every friend and child is properly buckled or harnessed.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: Which seats require belts in Minnesota, and can police pull you over solely for an unbuckled belt?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Minnesota enforces primary seat-belt law—an officer needs zero other moving violation to write a belt ticket.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: Why does the manual call seat belts the single most important safety feature in your vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Staying anchored inside the steel safety cage multiplies survival odds compared with being thrown onto asphalt.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: How many times more likely are you to be killed or injured when riding without a seat belt?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Skipping a three-second click quadruples your odds of death or trauma in the exact same collision.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: At speeds as low as how many miles per hour can an unbelted rider die in a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Thinking you can skip belts on a quick twelve-mile-per-hour neighborhood run ignores deadly unrestrained head impacts.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: What reverse, seating-capacity, and medical exceptions exist inside Minnesota's seat-belt statute?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Written medical waivers must come from a physician and ride with you to count.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: Under what strict speed ceiling are frequent-stop delivery or utility workers excused from buckling?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: The instant that delivery van accelerates above twenty-five miles per hour, the belt must click back in.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: Which postal, agricultural, and pre-nineteen-sixty-five vehicles also hold Minnesota seat-belt exemptions?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Vehicles built before January first, nineteen sixty-five came off assembly lines before federal safety-belt mandates existed.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: How quickly do the frequent-stop worker exemption and passenger-car backing exemption vanish?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Shifting into drive or passing twenty-five miles per hour immediately restores mandatory belt enforcement.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: Across which strong bones—never soft tissue—must your lap and shoulder belts sit?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Wearing a lap strap high over your soft abdomen causes severe internal injuries, and tucking shoulder straps behind you fails.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: Under what age must children ride in the back seat whenever a rear seat is available?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Front airbags inflate at adult chest height—striking smaller under-thirteen riders around the head and neck.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: What approval standard and installation guide govern every child car seat and booster?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Even a top-rated seat fails in a crash if anchored loosely instead of following the maker's manual.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: How long must a child under two—or a two-year-old still inside seat limits—ride rear-facing?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Turning two is a floor, not a flip switch—keep toddlers rear-facing until height or weight maxes out.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: Who transitions into a forward-facing harnessed seat, and what typical weight range caps that stage?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Five-point harnesses spread crash forces across shoulders and hips up to forty-to-sixty-pound manufacturer limits.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: Which age range must use a belt-positioning booster seat once they outgrow a harnessed car seat?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Boosters lift smaller frames so adult lap and shoulder straps hit hipbones and collarbones instead of necks.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: What age milestone or size limit moves a child from a booster seat to a standard safety belt?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Remember children ages nine through twelve still belong buckled in the back seat until turning thirteen.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: How do the age and growth triggers contrast between Minnesota's rear-facing stage and booster stage?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Keeping under-two rear-facing, forward harness in between, and four-to-nine booster straight nails child-restraint questions.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: When do child safety seats expire, and how must you treat a seat after a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Plastic shells turn brittle with heat cycles and suffer hidden micro-fractures in a single collision.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: How do you calculate expiration on a child restraint that carries no stamped expiration date?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Check the molded manufacture-date dial on the base and add six years.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: What three seating or cargo placements for infants and children must never happen?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: An active passenger airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing infant shell inches from the dashboard with lethal force.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: What four severe dangers forbid leaving children or vulnerable adults alone inside a parked vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Closed cabins trap oven-like summer heat or subzero Minnesota cold far faster than a quick store run.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.question_text: What four simple steps protect your unattended vehicle from car theft?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.teaching_text: Winter puffing—leaving a running car unlocked to warm up—drives huge spikes in stolen Minnesota vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.question_text: Why should dogs and other pets never be left waiting inside a parked vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.teaching_text: Cracked windows barely slow down deadly heatstroke on sunny days or freezing hypothermia in winter.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: What does calling an airbag a supplemental restraint mean about what it can and cannot do?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Front bags deflate milliseconds after impact, leaving unbuckled riders unrestrained during secondary hits or rollovers.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.question_text: Because of front-airbag force, what age-based seating rule is stressed a second time?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.teaching_text: Repeating an age cutoff twice across the handbook practically guarantees you will see thirteen on exam day.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: At least how many inches of space should separate your breastbone from the steering wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Ten inches gives the steering-hub airbag room to inflate fully before cushioning your torso.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: Which two clock-face hand grips—and thumb position—replace old ten-and-two steering?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: High ten-and-two grips with wrapped thumbs get slammed back into your face or broken if an airbag fires.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.question_text: How should front-seat passengers position their seat and prepare for airbag-equipped cabins?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.teaching_text: Maximizing distance from the dashboard softens airbag contact and protects legs and knees.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.question_text: From cigarette butts and snow chunks to glass or cans, what may be tossed from a vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.teaching_text: Flicked butts spark grassfires while roof ice chunks, glass, and nails puncture tires and shatter windshields.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: What three immediate steps come first right after a collision?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Clearing driveable cars onto the shoulder prevents secondary pileups while killing the ignition cuts fuel-spark fire risk.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: What three lighting tools warn approaching drivers of a crash scene?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Making a dark wreck visible early prevents secondary highway collisions that often hurt more people than the first.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: When does Minnesota law require an immediate call to police or nine-one-one after a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Every minute saved dialing nine-one-one brings trauma care and scene protection faster.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: What reasonable help does Minnesota law require you to give injured crash victims?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Never move spinal-injured victims carelessly if untrained—keep them warm and safe until paramedics arrive.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: What four personal and vehicle details—plus card—must you share with other involved drivers and officers?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Leaving a crash scene without exchanging full identification turns an accident into a hit-and-run crime.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: What insurance details must you share if asked at a crash, and how long do you get if missing?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Seventy-two hours is a classic Minnesota post-crash deadline that appears regularly on written tests.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: Does a property-damage-only crash require calling police in Minnesota, and what two duties still apply?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Clearing disabled metal fast and notifying owners of struck fences, signs, or parked cars satisfies the law.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.question_text: How does police-reporting law split between crashes with injuries or deaths and property-only crashes?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.teaching_text: Unlike states with dollar thresholds for police calls, Minnesota draws the line cleanly at human injury or death.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.question_text: Which two types of insurance must cover every Minnesota public-road vehicle, and where must proof stay?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.teaching_text: No-fault covers medical bills promptly regardless of fault while liability covers damage and injuries caused to others.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.question_text: What two revocations can hit you if you fail to produce proof of insurance during a stop?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.teaching_text: Keep current paper or digital insurance proof ready even if your policy is paid up at home.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.question_text: What four requirements—including exact fee—restore driving privileges after an insurance revocation?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.teaching_text: Skipping proof costs far more hassle than carrying a card—requiring retesting, thirty dollars, reapplying, and insurer filing.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.question_text: Up to what fine, jail term, and license revocation can a conviction for driving uninsured bring?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.teaching_text: Driving uninsured is a misdemeanor crime carrying jail exposure—not a minor civil parking ticket.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.question_text: How do mandatory and optional coverages differ for motorcycles compared with four-wheel cars?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.teaching_text: Motorcyclists must insure injuries and property damage to others, while no-fault and uninsured add-ons remain optional.

sec06-card-sec06-R25.question_text: Beyond court fines or jail, what happens to the vehicle itself when operated without insurance?
sec06-card-sec06-R25.teaching_text: Administrative plate and registration revocation grounds the car until valid coverage is filed.

sec06-card-sec06-R27.question_text: How do thirty dollars, two hundred seventy-five dollars, and one thousand dollars match Minnesota's insurance and phone penalties?
sec06-card-sec06-R27.teaching_text: Stacking thirty, two-seventy-five, and one thousand side by side keeps dollar distractors crystal clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.question_text: How many days does a new Minnesota resident get to register public-road vehicles with Driver and Vehicle Services?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.teaching_text: Letting out-of-state plates ride past sixty days after moving in violates Minnesota registration deadlines.

sec06-card-sec06-R26.question_text: Which two documents do you carry into a deputy registrar's office to register your vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-R26.teaching_text: Bringing both ownership proof and valid identification avoids a wasted second trip to the registrar.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.question_text: What messaging and browsing actions on a wireless device are illegal behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.teaching_text: Taking eyes off traffic for five seconds at highway speed drives blind across an entire football field.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.question_text: Which three emergency or operating modes stay legal under Minnesota's wireless messaging ban?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.teaching_text: Single-touch voice commands and nine-one-one calls let you communicate without typing or holding a screen.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.question_text: What extra dollar penalty hits a driver convicted two or more times of messaging while driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.teaching_text: That mandatory two-hundred-seventy-five-dollar add-on stacks right on top of the base court fine.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: When may a bicyclist legally proceed through a red traffic light that fails to detect their bike?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Lightweight bike frames often fail to trip pavement sensors, so riders may cross only after stopping, waiting, and checking hazards.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: Which specific legal charge does Minnesota's undetected-bicycle red-light defense cover?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Pulling into an oncoming car still leaves the cyclist open to civil lawsuits or other criminal charges beyond the red-light ticket.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Which three conditions must all hold at the exact same time before an undetected bicyclist crosses on red?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Skipping any one of the three steps voids the legal defense and risks a broadside collision with fast cross traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Where should drivers actively scan for bicyclists, and when do riders require extra caution?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Narrow bike profiles blend into cluttered backgrounds around driveways and dark corners where drivers only expect wide headlights.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: What top speed defines a motorized bicycle or moped in Minnesota, and which general road rules apply?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: If a two-wheeler can exceed thirty miles per hour on flat pavement, Minnesota classifies it above a moped.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Which three types of paths or roadways are completely off-limits to mopeds?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Mopeds are too fast for walkers and cyclists on trails yet far too slow to survive high-speed freeway traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: Although mopeds generally follow bicycle riding rules, where are mopeds banned that regular bicycles can use?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: A gas motor bars mopeds from pedestrian sidewalks and dedicated bike lanes or trails even when bicycle traffic laws otherwise apply.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Why do drivers frequently misjudge an approaching motorcycle's speed and distance?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: A narrow single headlight makes a fast-closing bike look much farther away and slower than a wide sedan.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: How much following distance must you keep behind a motorcycle, and why?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Potholes, gravel, or gusts can make a rider weave or wobble unexpectedly within their lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: How much space should you leave behind your bumper when pulling into a lane ahead of a motorcycle?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Cutting in tight forces hard braking on two wheels, which can lock a tire and dump the rider.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: How should you handle your speed and lane position while a motorcyclist is overtaking you?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Drifting or accelerating mid-pass traps an exposed rider alongside your quarter panel in turbulent air.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: May a car ever drive side by side with a motorcycle inside the same traffic lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Every motorcyclist needs the full width of a lane to swerve around road debris, potholes, and wind blasts.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: What must drivers avoid doing when a motorcyclist legally shares a lane to pass in slow or stopped traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Swinging your nose over or cracking a door to pinch off a passing rider is illegal and causes serious injury.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: Under what road setup and two exact speed limits is motorcycle lane splitting legal in Minnesota?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Once moving multi-lane traffic climbs past twenty-five miles per hour, riding between lanes becomes illegal.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: What road setup and speed limit apply when a motorcycle filters between stopped vehicles at a red light or jam?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Filtering lets riders roll gently past stopped bumpers at fifteen miles per hour or less instead of sitting exposed to rear-enders.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: How does motorcycle lane splitting differ from lane filtering in traffic flow and speed caps?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Splitting happens in moving traffic under both twenty-five and fifteen-over caps, whereas filtering happens in stopped traffic at fifteen-over.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Where and how do the most common crashes between cars and motorcycles happen?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Drivers scanning past a narrow headlight routinely turn left directly across an oncoming rider's right-of-way.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: Do standard right-of-way laws protect motorcyclists, and may solo riders use HOV lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Motorcycles hold full right-of-way protection and can legally cruise high-occupancy lanes even with one rider.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: How does a motorcycle compare with a passenger car in protecting its rider during a collision?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Without crumple zones or steel doors around the rider, even a low-speed fender-bender for a car can maim a motorcyclist.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: Which five groups of unprotected travelers count as vulnerable road users in Minnesota?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Anyone traveling on foot, horseback, mobility gear, scooters, or two- and three-wheelers lacks a protective vehicle body.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Why do vulnerable road users face higher crash injury risk, and must they obey traffic laws?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Lacking seat belts and airbags makes crashes severe, yet vulnerable travelers must still follow every traffic rule.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: Across which four types of travel corridors must you share space safely with vulnerable users and their passengers?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Driveway aprons and trail crossings intersect roads constantly, requiring alert sharing beyond main highway lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: What wheel count, top-speed range, and paperwork define a neighborhood electric vehicle in Minnesota?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Unlike golf carts on private turf, street-legal NEVs need full Driver and Vehicle Services title and registration.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: Which license drives an NEV, what street speed limit caps its routes, and can you take a road test in one?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Standard Class D drivers can operate NEVs on thirty-five-mile-per-hour streets, never for licensing skills exams.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: How does a neighborhood electric vehicle's own top speed compare with the posted speed limit of streets it may use?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Permit questions love swapping the vehicle's twenty-to-twenty-five speed capability with the thirty-five street limit.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Which three categories of vehicles count as commercial vehicles under Minnesota's road-sharing rules?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Even a small van carrying hazardous-materials placards or any size school or transit bus qualifies alongside heavy rigs.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: Which three zones around your car must have safe clearance before you start passing a commercial vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Getting boxed in mid-pass alongside a long trailer traps you right inside the truck driver's side blind spot.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: How many extra seconds does passing a truck on a flat highway take, and what oncoming clearance rule still applies?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Long trailers stretch passing distance, yet you still must merge back with at least one hundred feet before oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: What should you do instead of passing a commercial vehicle when your exit or turnoff is coming up soon?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Sprinting past a semi only to dive across its front bumper toward an exit ramp causes catastrophic underride crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: How do uphill grades and downhill grades change passing a commercial vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Gravity drags heavy rigs down on climbs, then accelerates their momentum rapidly on descents so passes take much longer.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: What mirror cue tells you it is safe to pull back into the lane after passing a truck, and what should your speed do?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Waiting until the entire front grille fills your rearview mirror keeps you out of the front no-zone, and easing off invites tailgating.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: How should you adjust lane position and speed while a truck or bus is passing your vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Giving extra lateral space and lifting slightly off the throttle shortens the time you spend beside eighteen spinning tires.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: Where should you position your car when meeting a truck head-on, and which way does wind turbulence push?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Drivers expect suction, yet the bow wave between passing vehicles actually shoves them apart toward the shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: How does a large truck's size distort your perception of its speed at intersections?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Optical scale makes big rigs look leisurely even at highway pace, luring drivers into deadly pulls across their path.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.question_text: Why might trucks and buses travel below your preferred pace, and why should you avoid honking or weaving?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.teaching_text: Electronic speed limiters and operating rules cap heavy rigs, and aggressive horn blasts or lane darts only distract professional drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: What two dangers make cutting in closely ahead of a bus or truck especially hazardous?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Disappearing below a high hood leaves the driver blind while forty tons of freight cannot shed speed quickly.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: At 55 mph, how does an average car's stopping distance compare with a fully loaded tractor-trailer's?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: A loaded semi needs roughly triple a sedan's pavement to halt, turning tight merges ahead of rigs into instant collisions.
sec08-card-sec08-F28.must_match_memory_hook: One forty car, four hundred truck

visual_sync.text_span: One forty car, four hundred truck

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: What visual test tells you whether you are following far enough behind a commercial truck?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Tailgating a trailer blinds you to traffic ahead and hides your car completely from the trucker's side mirrors.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: Beyond visibility, what crucial safety benefit does keeping extra distance behind a commercial vehicle give you?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: When you cannot see past a tall trailer box, extra following seconds keep you from slamming into its rear bumper.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: Why must you always switch to low-beam headlights when following a commercial vehicle after dark?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Oversized West Coast truck mirrors bounce high-beam glare straight into the cab and blind the driver.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: How should you respond when a commercial vehicle is accelerating onto the roadway to merge?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Heavy rigs build highway momentum slowly, so adjusting early avoids pinching forty tons onto a disappearing ramp.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: Where and how far back should you stop behind a commercial vehicle on an uphill grade?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Manual-shift rigs can roll backward slightly as the clutch engages, and sitting left puts your car in the side mirror.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: Why must you never try to pass on the right side of a commercial vehicle that could be turning right?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Sneaking between a turning trailer and the curb traps your car as the trailer's rear axles sweep inward.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: How do a turning vehicle's rear wheels track compared with its front wheels, and what makes that gap wider?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Longer wheelbases pull trailer axles much closer to the corner curb, forcing wide setups before the turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: Why might a truck leave tempting open pavement on its right just before an intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Drivers mistake that right-side gap for an open curb lane unless they check the trailer's flashing right blinker.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: Where are a truck's four blind-spot no-zones located, including the exact front and rear distances?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Lingering inside twenty feet ahead, beside either flank, or within two hundred feet behind makes your car invisible.
sec08-card-sec08-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Twenty front, sides, two hundred rear

visual_sync.text_span: Twenty front, sides, two hundred rear

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: How many times longer is a truck's rear blind-spot no-zone than its front blind-spot no-zone?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Comparing two hundred feet behind the trailer with twenty feet ahead shows why tailgating hides you ten times farther.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: Why do most collisions between motor vehicles and trains end in driver fatalities?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Thousands of tons of steel cannot swerve or brake quickly, overwhelming passenger car crumple zones in seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.question_text: How do road markings and trackside signs warn you about an upcoming railroad crossing and extra tracks?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.teaching_text: Checking the number plaque beneath the crossbuck warns you to scan for a second hidden train before rolling.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: What minimum distance from the nearest rail or gate must you stop when crossing lights, bells, or gates activate?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Locomotives overhang wider than the steel rails, so stopping at least ten feet back keeps your bumper clear.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: How much clear space beyond the tracks must exist in traffic ahead before you start driving across?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: Starting across behind bumper-to-bumper traffic traps your trunk inside the train's overhang zone if cars ahead halt.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.question_text: What are the two matching ten-foot buffer rules at a Minnesota railroad crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.teaching_text: Ten feet before the near rail keeps you safe while waiting, and ten feet past the far rail prevents stranding.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.question_text: Which vehicles must stop at every railroad track, and within what distance of a crossing is passing illegal?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.teaching_text: Expect passenger vans, buses, and heavy trucks to halt at clear tracks, and never overtake within one hundred feet.

sec08-card-sec08-F39.question_text: Why must you wait and check both directions after the last car of a passing train clears the crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-F39.teaching_text: Drivers accelerating the instant a caboose clears get broadsided by an opposite-direction train hidden on parallel rails.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.question_text: Where must you wait when traffic is backed up across both sides of a railroad crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.teaching_text: Holding short of the crossing costs nothing if gates drop, whereas gambling on traffic creeping forward can be fatal.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.question_text: Why should you always stop and let a visible train pass if you hesitate for even a moment?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.teaching_text: Single train headlights especially at night disguise fast approach speeds, and locomotives need long distances to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F40.question_text: When driving a manual transmission vehicle across railroad tracks, how must you handle shifting gears?
sec08-card-sec08-F40.teaching_text: Missing a shift mid-crossing can stall your engine directly across live rails with no momentum to coast off.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.question_text: Why shouldn't motorcyclists swerve sharply right before railroad tracks to get a better crossing angle?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.teaching_text: Whipping wide for a ninety-degree rail angle can throw a bike directly into the oncoming lane or adjacent cars.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.question_text: How must you treat a flag person stationed at a railroad crossing?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.teaching_text: Rail crews post human flaggers during gate maintenance or switching moves, carrying full warning-device authority.

sec08-card-sec08-F41.question_text: What does the blue Emergency Notification System sign posted at every highway-rail crossing provide?
sec08-card-sec08-F41.teaching_text: If a car stalls on the rails, calling that posted blue plaque first alerts railroad dispatch before a train arrives.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.question_text: Why is reading the crossing ID number off the blue ENS sign crucial when calling dispatchers?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.teaching_text: Exact crossing codes let railroad dispatchers radio approaching engineers immediately to halt or slow before impact.

sec08-card-sec08-F42.question_text: What happens if you ignore a flag person's instructions or disobey a posted speed limit inside a work zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F42.teaching_text: Work zone signs and flaggers carry full legal force to shield crews standing feet from moving bumpers.

sec08-card-sec08-F43.question_text: How much extra money is added on top of a regular speeding ticket when you speed in a work zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F43.teaching_text: Minnesota tacks three hundred dollars onto the base speeding fine to deter drivers from rushing past road crews.

sec08-card-sec08-F44.question_text: Which speed limit governs a work zone when no reduced work-zone speed sign is posted?
sec08-card-sec08-F44.teaching_text: Absence of an orange speed plaque never means unlimited speed; the road's standard limit stays fully enforced.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.question_text: Why must you expect equipment, delays, and temporary lane markings in work zones at any hour?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.teaching_text: Heavy machinery parks or maneuvers overnight too, so patience and following temporary orange markings prevent crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.question_text: How should you adjust your attention and lane position when passing workers and equipment in a work zone?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.teaching_text: Shifted lanes leave zero room for phone glances, and edging away from cones gives workers vital breathing space.

sec08-card-sec08-F45.question_text: How do you properly execute a zipper merge when a lane-closed sign appears and traffic slows down?
sec08-card-sec08-F45.teaching_text: Using both open lanes all the way to the taper and taking polite one-for-one turns keeps traffic flowing smoothly.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.question_text: What three traffic problems happen when drivers abandon a closing lane way too early?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.teaching_text: Leaving half the highway empty stretches congestion backward past ramps and sparks sudden lane-change collisions.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.question_text: In heavy, slow-moving traffic approaching a lane closure, what is the safest lane choice until the merge taper?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.teaching_text: Holding your lane at matching slow speed eliminates sudden brake-slamming weaves into packed adjacent traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.question_text: By up to what percentage can a proper zipper merge shorten traffic backups?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.teaching_text: Packing two full lanes instead of one cuts the physical length of a construction queue by nearly half.

sec08-card-sec08-R26.question_text: Beyond shorter lines, what safety and traffic benefits does zipper merging create around lane closures?
sec08-card-sec08-R26.teaching_text: Equal lane speeds stop dangerous fly-bys near workers, clear nearby freeway ramps, and make turn-taking feel fair.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: What five defensive-driving steps make up the SIPDE strategy in order?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Cycling continuously through those five mental steps catches developing road hazards long before emergency braking starts.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: Where do your eyes search during the Scan step, and around which busy zones should you spot escape routes?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Scanning ahead, beside, and behind while spotting escape outs protects you around intersections, schools, shops, and commercial strips.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Which four categories of traffic and road hazards should you actively look for while scanning?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Watching oncoming left-turners, side-entering bikes and walkers, fast followers, and rough pavement covers every collision angle.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: Which three motion factors do you weigh in the Predict step, and which vehicles deserve top priority?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Prioritize vehicles converging toward your travel path over stationary cars or traffic heading away.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: What mental planning happens continuously during the Decide step of SIPDE?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Choosing your evasive move beforehand saves precious split-seconds if traffic ahead changes abruptly.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Which communication tools and vehicle adjustments carry out the Execute step?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Alerting others with headlamps or horn while smoothly adjusting speed, lane position, or direction puts your plan into action.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: Why does the Minnesota manual warn that your own eyes are the only ones you can truly count on?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Even bright daytime headlights and turn signals cannot force a distracted driver to notice your car.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: How do you apply Minnesota's three-second rule to check whether you are following too closely?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Passing that roadside object before finishing one-thousand-one through three proves your following cushion is too tight.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Which four roadside objects make solid three-second markers, and how should you fix a tight gap?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Pick a stationary pole, signpost, tree, or bridge shadow, and ease off throttle gently whenever you arrive early.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: What ideal baseline does three seconds assume, and when should you expand your count to four or five seconds?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Standard cars on dry pavement fit three seconds, whereas slick weather or longer vehicles need four or five.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What is the safest response when another driver rides closely on your rear bumper?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Tapering your speed slightly encourages an impatient follower to overtake cleanly instead of riding your bumper.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Roughly how long does moving from spotting danger to pressing the brake take, and what else shapes stopping distance?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Your car rolls forward during that three-quarter-second reaction before weather, tread depth, and brake health ever bite.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: What visual-and-mental delay adds distance to your stop even before brake reaction time begins?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Every split-second spent noticing and interpreting a hazard rolls extra feet onto total stopping distance before your foot moves.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: Despite lighter traffic volumes after dark, what share of fatal Minnesota crashes occur at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Reduced sightlines, glare, fatigue, and impairment pack almost half of Minnesota's fatal wrecks into nighttime hours.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: Which three preparation checks should you complete before setting out on a night drive?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Knowing your turns beforehand while verifying working bulbs and defect-free clean glass cuts nighttime visual workload.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: During which hours, precipitation types, and visibility threshold must your headlights stay on in Minnesota?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Flip headlights on overnight, during rain, snow, hail, sleet, or fog, and whenever clear sightlines drop below five hundred feet.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: At what oncoming distance and what following distance must Minnesota drivers switch to low beams?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Minnesota requires dimming brights a full thousand feet from approaching cars and within two hundred feet behind traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: Compare Minnesota's required low-beam distance when meeting oncoming traffic versus trailing behind a vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Direct windshield glare blinds approaching drivers five times farther out than mirror glare hits a driver ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: What rule links your night speed to your headlight beam, and how far do most high beams reach?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Outrunning that three-hundred-fifty-foot high-beam pool means obstacles appear too close to stop in time.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: How do you counter blinding oncoming headlights ahead and bright beams shining from behind?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Tracking the right white edge line protects forward vision while switching your rearview mirror tames rear glare.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: Which access and intersection features define a freeway and allow nonstop long-distance travel?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Separating directions and replacing cross-traffic intersections with ramps keeps high-speed freeway lanes flowing nonstop.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: What purpose does the acceleration lane at the end of a freeway entrance ramp serve?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Pressing up to mainline speed before merging prevents high-speed freeway drivers from slamming brakes behind you.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Who holds right-of-way at a freeway merge, and what three steps move you smoothly onto the mainline?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Through-lane freeway traffic holds priority, so signal early, yield, and slip smoothly into an open gap.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: Should you stop on a freeway entrance ramp or acceleration lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: Halting unexpectedly in an acceleration lane destroys your merge speed and surprises drivers checking mirrors behind you.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: How must you merge at an older entrance ramp posted with a Yield sign and no acceleration lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Without a run-up lane, obey the Yield sign—stopping when gaps are tight—rather than forcing mainline cars aside.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: Where along an entrance ramp do ramp meters sit, when do they usually run, and what if red shows?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Positioned halfway down the ramp during rush hours, red ramp lights carry full legal force against running them.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: Why do metro freeways use ramp meters, and how many vehicles advance per green cycle?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Spacing entries one vehicle per green light smooths metro merges and trims mainline bottlenecks and rear-end crashes.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: How should you set your freeway speed relative to traffic and the limit, and where belong slower drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Cruising near surrounding flow without exceeding posted limits—while keeping right if slower—prevents dangerous lane weaving.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: Which two steps must precede every freeway lane change for passing or exiting?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: High freeway speeds close gaps fast, so signal intentions and confirm an open path before moving over.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: Under what three speed conditions may transit and metro mobility buses ride a freeway shoulder?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Shoulder bus travel opens only below thirty-five mainline pace, capped fifteen faster than traffic and thirty-five overall.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.question_text: To which vehicles must a transit bus driving on the freeway shoulder yield right-of-way?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.teaching_text: Shoulder-running buses must give way to every ramp merger, exiting driver, and stalled vehicle occupying the shoulder.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: What freeway hazards do electronic message signs announce, and how do they assist during an AMBER Alert?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Overhead digital boards warn of wrecks or stalls ahead and broadcast AMBER Alert vehicle details so motorists report sightings.
