sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: Which three vehicle or occupancy categories are allowed inside high-occupancy vehicle lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Solo passenger-car commuters must stay out of HOV lanes reserved for buses, motorcycles, and two-plus carpools.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.question_text: How does a highway interchange connect intersecting roads without stopping traffic, and name a classic ramp layout?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.teaching_text: Grade-separated ramps—like classic cloverleaf loops—let drivers transfer between highways without traffic lights or cross-traffic stops.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: How does traffic move across a diverging diamond interchange bridge to make freeway ramp lefts easier?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Crossing traffic briefly to the left side of the bridge lets drivers veer onto ramps without cutting opposing lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: How much can a diverging diamond cut traffic delays, and how does it help conflict points and walkers?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Eliminating left-turn phases trims overall delays up to sixty percent while spreading out fewer conflicts and shortening crosswalks.

sec11-card-sec11-R14.question_text: Which two visibility and ramp-entry safety advantages come built into diverging diamond interchanges?
sec11-card-sec11-R14.teaching_text: Angled crossovers open longer turn sightlines and channelize lanes so wrong-way ramp entry becomes extremely difficult.

sec11-card-sec11-R15.question_text: Where do pedestrians walk across the bridge of a diverging diamond interchange?
sec11-card-sec11-R15.teaching_text: Walkers cross to a barrier-protected median walkway running safely down the center between traffic lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: When is stopping on an interstate allowed, and how does Minnesota law treat running out of gas there?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Running your fuel tank dry is preventable rather than an emergency, so coasting stopped on an interstate risks a ticket.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: Where should you park during a freeway breakdown, and which visual signals ask for help?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Pulling deep onto the shoulder with hazard flashers and a raised hood, open trunk, or white cloth alerts patrols.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: Along what road edge and distance range behind a disabled vehicle should flares or reflectors sit?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Spacing warning reflectors one hundred to five hundred feet back along the right roadway edge cues fast drivers early.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: Why should you stay with your disabled vehicle on a freeway instead of walking down the highway?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Stepping onto active high-speed freeway pavement on foot is both unlawful and life-threatening.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: Which vehicles are the sole legal exception to Minnesota's ban on backing up or turning around on a freeway?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Only on-duty emergency responders and highway maintenance crews may ever reverse or turn across freeway medians.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: How should you clear the way on a freeway when an emergency vehicle approaches from behind with lights and siren?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Signaling calmly to the nearest edge without slamming brakes—and checking for trailing units before re-entering—prevents secondary wrecks.

sec11-card-sec11-R16.question_text: Contrast your freeway response to a flashing emergency vehicle parked on the shoulder versus one approaching behind with sirens?
sec11-card-sec11-R16.teaching_text: Vacate the adjacent lane—or slow—past parked shoulder lights, whereas approaching sirens behind require pulling aside and stopping.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: What minimum following distance must you maintain behind any firefighting vehicle?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Fire engines stop abruptly at hydrants or scenes and carry heavy gear, requiring a five-hundred-foot buffer.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: What is the single safe and legal move if you drive past your intended freeway exit?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Reversing on a shoulder or cutting a median U-turn turns a five-minute detour into a fatal freeway collision.

sec11-card-sec11-R17.question_text: Where should your braking happen when exiting a freeway so mainline traffic stays unblocked?
sec11-card-sec11-R17.teaching_text: Knowing your exit ahead, signaling early, and waiting until the deceleration ramp to shed speed keeps through-lanes safe.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: Why might a driver add caretaker information onto their Minnesota Driver and Vehicle Services record?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: If a serious crash incapacitates you, officers checking your record immediately learn a dependent needs care at home.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: Contrast where your car stays after an injury crash versus a property-damage-only collision?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Keep injury scenes untouched while calling nine-one-one, whereas minor damage-only cars should move somewhere safe before stepping out.

sec11-card-sec11-R18.question_text: Which four driver and vehicle details should you exchange or record after a collision?
sec11-card-sec11-R18.teaching_text: Swapping license and policy details, jotting down license plate numbers, and adding VINs streamlines claims accurately.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: At least what percentage of all Minnesota traffic crashes each year involve driver distraction?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: One out of every four Minnesota wrecks traces back to distracted attention behind the wheel.

sec11-card-sec11-R19.question_text: Which two performance losses hit distracted drivers and shrink their margin of safety?
sec11-card-sec11-R19.teaching_text: Spotting brake lights late and reacting sluggishly erases the time cushion needed to avoid impact.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: Name the three categories of driving distraction and what each pulls away?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Visual pulls gaze off pavement, mechanical or physical lifts hands off steering, and cognitive wanders your mind.

sec11-card-sec11-R20.question_text: Besides phones and GPS, what everyday cabin tasks, outside sights, or mental states distract drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-R20.teaching_text: Grabbing dropped items, eating, tuning radios, chatting, reading, rubbernecking wrecks, and daydreaming all fracture driving focus.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: Which wireless actions are illegal while driving in Minnesota, and does stopping at a red light excuse them?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: Waiting at a stoplight or in bumper-to-bumper traffic still counts legally as operating on the roadway.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.question_text: What cell-phone restriction applies to under-eighteen teens driving on a learner's permit or provisional license?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.teaching_text: Bluetooth and speakerphone do not exempt teen permit or provisional drivers; only emergency nine-one-one calls are legal.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.question_text: When does wearing headphones or earphones behind the wheel break Minnesota law?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.teaching_text: Plugging both ears with music or audio cuts off sirens, horns, and train bells outside your cabin.

sec11-card-sec11-R21.question_text: What speed habit and four risky behaviors typically characterize an aggressive driver?
sec11-card-sec11-R21.teaching_text: Outpacing surrounding cars fuels tailgating, abrupt unsignaled weaves, illegal shoulder passes, and hostile glares or threats.

sec11-card-sec11-R22.question_text: Where do an aggressive driver's anger and frustration usually originate?
sec11-card-sec11-R22.teaching_text: Recognizing that hostile drivers bring personal anger from outside traffic helps you avoid taking their behavior personally.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.question_text: Which three de-escalation steps keep you safe around an aggressive driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.teaching_text: Giving wide room, skipping eye contact, and refusing to retaliate lets an angry motorist move away harmlessly.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.question_text: When does carrying cargo or seating four-plus people across the front bench break Minnesota law?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.teaching_text: Packing cargo high or squeezing four people up front breaks the law whenever sightlines or steering-and-pedal freedom suffer.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.question_text: What is the maximum distance a load may stick out ahead of your front wheels or bumper?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.teaching_text: Ladders or lumber jutting beyond three feet ahead swing wide into cross traffic and pedestrian crosswalks.

sec11-card-sec11-F43.question_text: When cargo extends four feet or more past the rear, what daytime flag and nighttime light are mandatory?
sec11-card-sec11-F43.teaching_text: Tie a sixteen-inch-square red, yellow, or orange flag by day and hang a five-hundred-foot red lamp after dark.

sec11-card-sec11-F44.question_text: How far may cargo stick out beyond the left fender line versus the right fender line of a passenger car?
sec11-card-sec11-F44.teaching_text: Zero left overhang prevents clipping oncoming traffic, while the right side caps strictly at six inches.

sec11-card-sec11-R26.question_text: Compare Minnesota's cargo overhang rules across front, rear, left fender, and right fender?
sec11-card-sec11-R26.teaching_text: Keep three feet max up front, warn at four feet behind, allow zero left, and cap six inches right.

sec11-card-sec11-F45.question_text: At least how many feet of following space must you leave behind other vehicles when pulling a camper or trailer?
sec11-card-sec11-F45.teaching_text: Heavy towed weight stretches highway braking distances dramatically, demanding at least a five-hundred-foot cushion.

sec11-card-sec11-R23.question_text: What share of a loaded trailer's weight belongs on the hitch, and how should its floor sit?
sec11-card-sec11-R23.teaching_text: Too little tongue weight causes violent highway fish-tailing, so load ten to fifteen percent forward with a level floor.

sec11-card-sec11-R24.question_text: When during a towing trip should you pull over to inspect your hitch, tires, lights, and cargo?
sec11-card-sec11-R24.teaching_text: Catching a loosening hitch pin or settling strap after the first few miles—and each rest stop—prevents highway breakaways.

sec11-card-sec11-R25.question_text: Which two mechanical limits—wheel bearings and car brakes—explain why you must drive slower when towing?
sec11-card-sec11-R25.teaching_text: Small trailer wheels spin hot at speed while passenger brakes struggle with heavy trailers, risking jackknife rollovers.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: How should pulling a trailer change how you accelerate, follow traffic, and judge passes?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Added trailer weight slows pickup and stretches braking, requiring lower-gear launches, generous spacing, and extra passing room.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: How should wet pavement or crosswinds adjust your speed when pulling a camper or trailer?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Broad camper sides catch crosswind gusts easily while rain cuts tire bite under heavy towed weight.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: Why must you swing wider on turns with a long trailer, and which engine gauge needs watching on hot climbs?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Trailer wheels cut closer to curbs on turns while hot weather, highway pace, and climbs strain cooling systems.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: What are Minnesota's maximum legal length, width, and height limits for a trailer?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Keep forty-five feet length paired with eight feet six inches width and thirteen feet six inches height.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Which rear lamps and reflectors must every trailer carry, and when does it need its own brake and turn signals?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Pair two red taillights, two red reflectors, and a white plate lamp with dedicated signals at night or when blocked.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: What registration display applies to recreational trailers, and what backup connection must every trailer carry?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Every trailer needs a permanently mounted safety chain hooked to the tow vehicle in case the coupler pops.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: How wide may a trailer be relative to the outside rearview mirrors on the vehicle pulling it?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Towing anything wider than your outside mirrors blinds you completely to cars approaching behind the trailer.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: At what gross vehicle weight must a trailer be equipped with its own brakes?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Once loaded trailer weight reaches three thousand pounds, tow-vehicle brakes alone cannot stop safely.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: What minimum driver age and truck towing-capacity rule govern operating a recreational vehicle combination?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Drivers must be eighteen or older behind a pickup or truck-tractor rated for the entire towed load.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: What length cap and Twin Cities weekday rush-hour bans apply to a recreational vehicle combination?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: RV combinations cap at seventy feet and stay off Twin Cities metro roads weekdays six-to-nine morning and four-to-seven evening.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: Compare Minnesota's length ceilings across standard single-unit vehicles, motor homes or trailers, and RV combinations?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Standard single-unit vehicles cap at forty feet, Type A-B-C motor homes match trailers at forty-five, and RV combos reach seventy.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: What exterior hardware is excluded from the one-hundred-two-inch width limit on self-propelled recreational vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Rolled awnings or trim on a motor home skip the one-hundred-two-inch count provided they stay inside exterior mirror width.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: Which six recreational items are listed as examples a recreational vehicle combination's trailer may haul?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: That rear trailer can carry watercraft, motorcycles, snowmobiles, ATVs, golf carts, or equestrian gear.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: Which exterior surfaces must you clear before driving in winter, and what washer fluid belongs in the reservoir?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Brushing snow off hood, windows, and lamps prevents blow-back blindness while antifreeze washer fluid resists freezing solid.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: How can you safely gauge winter road slickness early, and what speed-control feature must stay off?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Gently checking brake bite at low speed reveals hidden glare ice early, while disabling cruise prevents wheelspin.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: How should you position your front wheels and work the pedals to rock a vehicle free from snow?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Pointing front tires straight cuts snow resistance while alternating gently forward and backward builds momentum without polishing ice.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: While rocking a stuck car, what should you do the instant your tires start spinning or sliding?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Spinning tires melt snow into slick ice pockets, so catch slips with the brake and switch directions.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: Which three flashing colors identify Minnesota snowplows, and what spacing and visibility rules govern passing one?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Hang well clear of flying sand and ice behind white-yellow-blue beacons, overtaking only with the entire plow visible.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: Which three operating traits—visibility, speed, and neighborhood maneuvers—require giving snowplows wide room?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Plows kick up blinding whiteout plumes, travel slowly, and frequently reverse to turn around on residential streets.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: What municipal declaration often follows heavy snowfall, and why must drivers follow its special parking rules?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Moving parked cars off snow-emergency routes lets plows clear curb-to-curb and saves you expensive impound fees.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: Which warmth, traction, signaling, and emergency supplies belong inside a Minnesota winter survival kit?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Packing a shovel, sand, warm gear, blanket, antenna cloth, snacks, water, chains, flares, cables, candles, and first-aid saves lives.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: Why must you stay inside your vehicle rather than setting out on foot when stranded in severe cold?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Most winter breakdown fatalities happen when drivers abandon shelter, lose orientation in blowing snow, and freeze outdoors.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: When stranded in winter, how long per hour do you run the heater, and which two carbon-monoxide precautions are vital?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Running ten minutes each hour conserves fuel while clearing tailpipe snow and cracking a window prevents deadly exhaust buildup.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: Which four visibility and supply actions help rescuers find you and keep gear handy while stranded?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Run flashers, tie red cloth onto your antenna or handle, set flares outside, and pull trunk supplies into the cabin.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: When multiple people are stranded inside a cold-weather vehicle, what alertness rule applies?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Having at least one occupant stay awake continuously spots approaching rescuers and watches against carbon monoxide drowsiness.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: On a long road trip, at what distance or time interval should you stop to stretch and refresh?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Walking, stretching, and grabbing water or a snack every hundred miles or two hours keeps highway hypnosis away.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: Why shouldn't tired drivers trust loud music, open windows, or stay-awake pills—and what works instead?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Singing, fresh air, and stimulants wear off fast, so trade drivers or park well off traffic with locked doors.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.question_text: Contrast the stranded-engine runtime schedule against Minnesota's long-trip fatigue break rule?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.teaching_text: Keep ten minutes per hour tied to stranded cabin heat and two hours—or one hundred miles—tied to rest stops.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: How should you react if your tires begin skidding, and what prevents skids beforehand?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Panicked wheel jerks or brake slams worsen slides, whereas calm inputs—backed by lower speeds and wider gaps—preserve control.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: How do you apply anti-lock brakes during an emergency stop or slide?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Pumping defeats computer anti-lock pulsing, so hold steady firm pedal pressure while steering cleanly around trouble.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: Which four adjustments—speed, spacing, beams, and stopping—apply in heavy thunderstorms or fog?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Ease speed, stretch your following cushion, run low beams against glare, and pull completely off when sightlines vanish.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: What lifts tires off wet pavement during hydroplaning, and at what speed can standard cars start hydroplaning in heavy rain?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Trapped water builds hydrodynamic lift beneath rolling rubber starting as low as thirty-five miles per hour in downpours.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.question_text: Compare how tires interact with wet pavement at thirty-five miles per hour or below versus faster speeds?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.teaching_text: Tread grooves channel water clear at thirty-five and under, whereas higher speeds trap water wedges beneath rubber.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: Which three controls vanish once tires hydroplane, and what immediate foot action should you take?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Water-floating tires cannot brake, accelerate, or turn, so ease your foot off the accelerator until rubber settles.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: When can hydroplaning strike at any speed—even slow city speeds?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Once standing water exceeds your tire groove depth, tread channels flood completely regardless of how slowly you roll.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.question_text: How do healthy tires with deep tread grooves fight hydroplaning at highway speeds?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.teaching_text: Open tread channels evacuate surface water sideways so rubber blocks stay planted firmly against wet asphalt.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: Walk through the five steps to control and park your car safely during a tire blowout?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Stomping brakes on a blown tire yanks the car violently sideways, so coast straight under firm grip first.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.question_text: Which sound and steering-wheel sensation warn that a tire blowout may be starting?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.teaching_text: Catching rhythmic tire thumps or sudden sideways wheel pull early lets you slow smoothly before tread separates.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: How should you slow down if your steering stops responding, and why avoid abrupt pedal or gear moves?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Hard braking or abrupt downshifts shift weight unevenly and spin an unsteerable car, so ease off throttle gently.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.question_text: As you ease off speed during a steering failure, how may the vehicle track on its own?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.teaching_text: Caster alignment built into front suspension often keeps a slowing vehicle rolling straight ahead when undisturbed.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: If your brake pedal sinks to the floor, what two steps do you try—and which wheels does the parking brake grab?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Rapid pumping can rebuild hydraulic pressure, and if not, ease the parking brake slowly so rear wheels don't lock.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.question_text: Which pedal feel and dashboard cue warn that your braking system may be failing?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.teaching_text: A spongy pedal creeping downward under steady foot pressure—or an illuminated brake warning lamp—demands immediate service.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.question_text: When open pavement lets you coast with failed brakes, how can your transmission help bring you down safely?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.teaching_text: Stepping progressively down through lower gears uses engine compression to bleed speed smoothly toward the shoulder.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: If your right wheels drop onto the roadside shoulder, how should you return to the pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Jerking back across a pavement lip at highway speed slingshots cars across oncoming lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.question_text: Why must you never coast down steep hills in neutral, and what gauge should you monitor?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.teaching_text: Disengaging engine braking lets gravity accelerate your car rapidly even with your foot completely off the gas.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: During which hours are deer most active, and which five precautions help prevent a strike?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Scan ditches from dusk to dawn for shining eyes, slow down, honk, prepare to stop, and expect trailing deer.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.question_text: Are deer crossings confined strictly to rural country highways and nighttime hours?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.teaching_text: While most common along rural corridors, deer wander into city neighborhoods and cross roads anytime.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: Which direction must you steer—and what signals should you trigger—if an oncoming vehicle enters your lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Heading right—even off the shoulder—clears the lane while horn blasts and headlight flashes wake up the drifted driver.

sec12-card-sec12-R23.question_text: Why must you never swerve into the left lane to dodge an oncoming car in your lane?
sec12-card-sec12-R23.teaching_text: The moment that wrong-way driver looks up and corrects right, both cars collide head-on in the left lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: On a two-lane road, how do you adjust speed to help a passing car nearly past you versus one dropping back?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Easing off opens space ahead when a passer is almost clear, whereas speeding up opens tuck-in room behind.

sec12-card-sec12-R24.question_text: When a failed pass makes a crash look imminent and a wide right shoulder exists, what should you do?
sec12-card-sec12-R24.teaching_text: Escaping promptly onto a wide right shoulder hands your travel lane to the trapped passer and prevents a head-on.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.question_text: On narrow roads where curves, brush, or trees block sightlines, how may you alert unseen road users?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.teaching_text: A brief warning tap on the horn alerts hidden oncoming drivers, cyclists, or walkers before rounding tight brushy bends.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: If your car stalls on railroad tracks with a train approaching, how and in what direction must you evacuate?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Walking briskly at a forty-five-degree angle toward the oncoming locomotive keeps flying wreckage moving away behind you.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: What must you do when your route meets a flooded roadway, and what if no alternate road exists?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Never gamble driving across floodwater; reroute immediately or park safely on high ground if every road is blocked.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: What damage can just six inches of water cause, and what does two feet of moving water sweep away?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Half a foot wets passenger-car underbodies into stalling, while two feet of current carries off pickups and SUVs.

sec12-card-sec12-R25.question_text: How fast can flash floods rise, what road damage does murky water hide, and when is danger highest?
sec12-card-sec12-R25.teaching_text: Shallow-looking floodwater can conceal missing roadbeds within minutes of downpours, making nighttime crossings especially treacherous.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: Roughly how long do most cars float in deep water, and how should you escape right away?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Use that brief thirty-to-sixty-second floating window immediately to lower side glass and climb out before water rises.

sec12-card-sec12-R26.question_text: Why won't submerged car doors open right away, which end sinks first, and where might air linger?
sec12-card-sec12-R26.teaching_text: Outside water pins doors shut until cabin pressure equalizes, while heavy engines tilt fronts down leaving rear air.

sec12-card-sec12-R27.question_text: What should you do when other passengers are inside a submerged vehicle with you?
sec12-card-sec12-R27.teaching_text: Checking on every occupant and coordinating one shared exit keeps panicked riders from getting left inside.

sec12-card-sec12-R29.question_text: Which backup lights should you try if headlights die, and how do you handle a dark empty road?
sec12-card-sec12-R29.teaching_text: Test parking, hazard, or turn lamps first, staying slowed on paved lanes until you spot a safe shoulder.

sec12-card-sec12-R30.question_text: Which four steps handle sudden windshield wiper failure during heavy rain or snow?
sec12-card-sec12-R30.teaching_text: Ease speed, flip hazard flashers on, skip abrupt braking with cars trailing you, and exit lanes promptly.

sec12-card-sec12-R31.question_text: Where can you look to steer safely off the road if your hood pops open at speed?
sec12-card-sec12-R31.teaching_text: Peer beneath the raised hood gap or lean out your driver window with hazards flashing while easing roadside.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: What immediate steps apply when smoke rises from under your hood, and why never pour water on it?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Park roadside, kill ignition, and move clear immediately because throwing water onto burning fuel or oil spreads flames.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: How can cabin climate controls help an overheating engine, and when must you pull over and shut down?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Shutting off AC cuts load while blasting cabin heat pulls warmth off coolant—until rising gauges or steam demand stopping.

sec12-card-sec12-R28.question_text: Which three driving demands commonly push engine temperatures higher than normal?
sec12-card-sec12-R28.teaching_text: Summer gridlock starves radiator airflow just like steep grades and heavy trailers work cooling systems hard.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: What quick foot move do you try first for a stuck accelerator, and what three-step sequence backs it up?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: If hooking the pedal upward with your shoe tip fails, brake steadily, pop into neutral, and steer roadside.

sec12-card-sec12-R32.question_text: If handling a stuck accelerator puts you onto an unpaved gravel or dirt shoulder, how do you steer?
sec12-card-sec12-R32.teaching_text: Keep hazard lights blinking and hold straight wheel alignment on loose gravel until speed bleeds off safely.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: What must you do after striking a utility pole, power line, or transformer box—and what is the lone exception?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Stepping out bridges lethal voltage between car metal and dirt, so stay inside awaiting crews unless fire forces evacuation.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: If fire forces you out of a vehicle touching power equipment, how must your feet leave and move away?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: Leaping clear without touching car and ground simultaneously—then shuffling feet together—avoids deadly ground-current step voltage.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.question_text: What sensory traits make carbon monoxide impossible to detect directly, and what is the only treatment?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.teaching_text: Because carbon monoxide has zero smell or color, getting victims immediately into abundant fresh air is the sole cure.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.question_text: Which four physical symptoms give early warning of carbon monoxide poisoning, and what three actions follow?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.teaching_text: Sudden sleepiness, throbbing head, dizziness, or nausea means roll windows down, shut off ignition, and exit immediately.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.question_text: When does carbon monoxide poisoning peak, does an open garage door make idling safe, and how fast does it act?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.teaching_text: Fumes pool inside garages even with the door wide open, knocking someone unconscious within just a few minutes.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.question_text: Where should you warm up your vehicle, and which two idling habits must you avoid?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.teaching_text: Pull outdoors onto the driveway to warm up, and never sit idling parked or with snow-or-mud-packed exhaust.

sec12-card-sec12-R33.question_text: Which window habits and exhaust-system check keep carbon monoxide out of your cabin on everyday drives?
sec12-card-sec12-R33.teaching_text: Maintaining leak-free, unblocked exhaust pipes while cracking windows periodically prevents stale cabin air from trapping fumes.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: What is Minnesota's baseline rule on driving while impaired by alcohol or any other substance?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Minnesota's impairment ban reaches beyond beer and liquor to cover every substance that degrades safe driving.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: Which person dies most frequently in alcohol-related crashes, and which demographic drives impaired most often?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: Contrary to the myth that drunk drivers walk away unscathed, impaired drivers themselves top fatality counts.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: How does alcohol involvement correlate with the severity of Minnesota traffic crashes?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Delayed braking, higher speeds, and unbuckled belts make alcohol-linked wrecks far deadlier than sober fender-benders.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: Beyond illegal street drugs, which pharmacy and home items count under Minnesota's impaired-driving ban?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Over-the-counter cold syrups, allergy tablets, prescriptions, and inhaled household products carry identical DWI exposure.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: How does drug impairment compare with alcohol danger, and what physical and legal fallout can follow?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Drowsiness and sluggish reflexes from drugs trigger crashes, arrests, heavy fines, and jail time.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: Why can a harmless-feeling legal medication suddenly wreck your driving if combined with a drink?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Synergistic reactions turn mild medications into potent intoxicants with alcohol, so never mix drugs with driving.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: Under what medical guidance and label habits may you legally drive with a prescribed medication?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Confirming safe driving directly with your physician and obeying bottle warnings keeps prescribed treatment lawful.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Why should you never pop stimulants to mask road drowsiness, and what actually fixes fatigue?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Stimulants merely disguise exhaustion briefly before sudden microsleeps strike; genuine sleep is the sole cure.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: What drug class is alcohol, what term names its blood share, and how many drinks start impairment?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: Alcohol slows central nervous activity rather than stimulating it, degrading driving skill after a single drink.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: How does alcohol trick your self-assessment and erode four basic defensive driving habits?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Drinkers feel sharper than reality while speeding, misjudging stops, skipping seat belts, and dropping defensive habits.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: What three changes does alcohol inflict on eye movement, side awareness, and clarity?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Sluggish eye tracking and shrunken side vision hide cross-street hazards long before high concentrations blur sight.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: How does alcohol degrade your reflexes, steering path, sensory intake, and body control?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Dulled sights and sounds paired with weakened coordination make impaired drivers react late and yank the wheel.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: Which four common beverage servings hold roughly the same amount of pure alcohol?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Switching from cocktails to twelve-ounce beers or five-ounce wines puts equal alcohol into your bloodstream.
sec14-card-sec14-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Twelve beer, five wine, nine-cooler, cocktail

visual_sync.text_span: Twelve beer, five wine, nine-cooler, cocktail

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: Why can counting glasses mislead you on mixed cocktails and different beers?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Bartenders often pour past one-point-five liquor ounces, and craft or light beers swing up to forty percent.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: How do you convert a bottle's proof number into its actual percentage of alcohol?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Dividing eighty proof in half reveals forty percent pure alcohol inside every shot.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: What happens in your bloodstream whenever you consume more than one standard drink per hour?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Unburned alcohol backs up in your blood whenever intake outpaces your liver's hourly processing speed.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: What is the sole way to bring alcohol concentration down, how fast does it clear, and do coffee or showers help?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Hot coffee, workouts, or cold showers merely produce a wide-awake impaired person while the liver works hourly.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: How much alcohol does the liver oxidize, and how does the remaining five percent leave your body?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Because ninety-five percent waits on liver oxidation, deep breathing or sweating cannot rush sobriety.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: If two people weigh the exact same, why does the one with higher body fat hit a higher alcohol concentration?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Fat tissue absorbs very little alcohol, concentrating more of the drink inside the bloodstream.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: Which seven biological or situational traits make alcohol hit people differently, even the same person on different days?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Skipping dinner or feeling stressed can spike impairment faster than the exact same drink last weekend.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: How does muscle-versus-fat tissue explain one reason alcohol affects men and women differently?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Because men typically carry higher muscle mass and fat resists absorbing alcohol, bloodstream concentrations differ.
sec14-card-sec14-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Muscle keeps more out of blood

visual_sync.text_span: Muscle keeps more out of blood

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: What simple rule separates drinking from driving, and when must you lock in your plan?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Waiting until after drinks start lets alcohol's false confidence talk you into driving yourself home.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: What five practical options replace impaired driving for yourself or an impaired friend?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Lining up a sober driver, cab, family pickup, overnight stay, or taking a friend's keys saves lives.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: Why must your ride home from social drinking be settled before taking your very first drink?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Social gatherings trigger most impaired drives because the first drink starts eroding sound judgment.

sec14-card-sec14-R20.question_text: At what minimum age may a person legally purchase and consume alcohol in Minnesota?
sec14-card-sec14-R20.teaching_text: Anyone under twenty-one faces underage purchase bans plus strict zero-alcohol driving rules.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: Does a vehicle have to be moving for a DWI arrest, and what standard and commercial thresholds apply?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Sitting in physical control of a parked car at zero-point-zero-eight, or zero-point-zero-four commercially, triggers DWI arrest.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: How low can a noncommercial driver's alcohol concentration be and still bring a DWI arrest?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Staying under zero-point-zero-eight offers no safe harbor when an officer links your driving mistakes to alcohol.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.question_text: Compare Minnesota's DWI alcohol thresholds for general drivers, commercial rigs, and drivers committing alcohol-caused errors?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.teaching_text: Grouping commercial operation and proven-error arrests together at zero-point-zero-four keeps every threshold clear.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: When an officer has probable cause to suspect impairment, which three tests fall under implied consent, and what is refusal?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Driving in Minnesota carries automatic consent to chemical testing on probable cause, making refusal a standalone crime.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: Which three arrest, roadside-breath, or crash situations authorize an officer to request an alcohol test?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Refusing or failing a preliminary breath screen, or being in an alcohol-linked crash, unlocks formal testing.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: Beyond highway cars and trucks, which recreational machines fall under Minnesota's DWI and implied-consent statutes?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Operating an ATV, snowmobile, or motorboat impaired risks criminal DWI and chemical-test mandates.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: How many years of license revocation follow refusing an implied-consent test, and what sets the duration?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Prior offenses stretch a test-refusal revocation all the way from one year up to six years.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: How does a roadside preliminary breath test differ in courtroom use from the post-arrest blood, breath, or urine test?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Roadside breath units mainly guide probable cause, whereas post-arrest chemical tests serve as full trial evidence.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.question_text: Pair Minnesota's pre-arrest breath screen and post-arrest chemical test with each test's main job?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.teaching_text: Keeping the roadside gauge separate from the post-arrest evidentiary test prevents mixing them up on exams.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.question_text: How can blowing zero on a roadside preliminary breath test protect a sober driver having a medical episode?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.teaching_text: Diabetic shock or stroke symptoms can mimic slurred intoxication until a clean breath check alerts officers to call medics.

sec14-card-sec14-R13.question_text: Which two separate penalty tracks hit every impaired-driving offense, and what shapes their severity?
sec14-card-sec14-R13.teaching_text: Drivers face courtroom criminal sentences alongside DPS license actions scaled to priors and arrest facts.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: What dollar fee, application step, and possible starter device apply after an alcohol-related revocation?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Regaining your license after an alcohol revocation costs six hundred eighty dollars before reapplying or installing interlock.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: Which five record, concentration, passenger, age, or roadside factors trigger harsher Minnesota DWI penalties?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Blowing double the limit at zero-point-one-six or carrying a child under sixteen sharply escalates DWI punishment.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: How many days does a temporary license last before revocation kicks in after failing at point-oh-eight or refusing?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: That brief seven-day window lets drivers arrange alternate transit before full license revocation starts.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: What revocation length, guilty-plea reduction, and jail or fine ceiling apply to a first DWI?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Even a first DWI carries at least ninety days revoked, thirty on a DWI guilty plea, plus up to ninety jail days or one thousand dollars.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: How long must a first-time DWI offender wait for a work permit, and what alcohol reading blocks it completely?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Reaching zero-point-one-six percent bars a standard work permit completely, while lower readings still wait fifteen days.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: What revocation floor, jail-or-fine maximum, and license-plate action hit a second DWI within ten years?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Picking up a second DWI inside a decade jumps to a one-year revocation, three-thousand-dollar fine exposure, and seized plates.

sec14-card-sec14-R14.question_text: Step through Minnesota's minimum revocation floors for a first, second, and third DWI within ten years?
sec14-card-sec14-R14.teaching_text: Memorizing ninety days, one year, and three years locks down Minnesota's ten-year repeat-offense ladder.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: Which license, treatment, interlock, and vehicle-loss penalties hit a third DWI within ten years?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: A third strike in ten years cancels your card, mandates assessment and interlock, impounds plates, and forfeits the vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-R16.question_text: What custody or pre-trial release conditions can accompany a third DWI offense?
sec14-card-sec14-R16.teaching_text: Courts pair third-offense prosecutions with either jail time or maximum bail under electronic monitoring.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.question_text: Which three ten-year arrest counts or prior convictions elevate a Minnesota DWI to a felony charge?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.teaching_text: Reaching four DWI arrests in ten years, or carrying any prior felony DWI or impaired vehicular homicide, triggers felony charges.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.question_text: What maximum prison term, conditional-release tail, and dollar fine can follow a Minnesota felony DWI?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.teaching_text: Felony DWI carries up to seven years in state prison, five years supervised afterward, and fourteen thousand dollars.

sec14-card-sec14-R19.question_text: How long can a fourth DWI strip your license, and what is required before it ever returns?
sec14-card-sec14-R19.teaching_text: Waiting out four unlicensed years is not enough until formal rehabilitation and every reinstatement requirement finish.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.question_text: At what breath alcohol concentration does an ignition interlock device block your engine's starter?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.teaching_text: Wired straight to the starter, an interlock locks out ignition at a tiny zero-point-zero-two reading.

sec14-card-sec14-R17.question_text: Rank Minnesota's interlock lockout cutoff against the commercial and general DWI thresholds?
sec14-card-sec14-R17.teaching_text: Interlock's zero-point-zero-two lockout sits at half the commercial limit and one-quarter of the standard DWI threshold.

sec14-card-sec14-R15.question_text: How does ignition interlock shift from optional to mandatory across first, second, and third DWIs?
sec14-card-sec14-R15.teaching_text: Tracking optional, possibly required, then strictly required matches interlock rules to your offense count.
sec14-card-sec14-R15.must_match_memory_hook: Optional first, possible second, required third

visual_sync.text_span: Optional first, possible second, required third

sec14-card-sec14-R18.question_text: How can a first-time offender who blew zero-point-one-six or higher regain driving privileges when work permits are barred?
sec14-card-sec14-R18.teaching_text: Opting into ignition interlock gives high-concentration first offenders a legal way back onto the road.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.question_text: For how many years must drivers canceled as inimical to public safety use ignition interlock to earn full privileges?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.teaching_text: Restoring full privileges after public-safety cancellation demands three to six monitored years on interlock.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.question_text: How much alcohol may a driver under twenty-one have in their system, and what suspensions hit first and second convictions?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.teaching_text: Any detectable trace under twenty-one brings a thirty-day suspension first and one hundred eighty days second.

sec14-card-sec14-F35.question_text: What happens to a commercial driver caught operating a commercial rig at point-oh-four, or with any detectable alcohol below it?
sec14-card-sec14-F35.teaching_text: Reaching zero-point-zero-four costs the CDL for at least a year, while any trace below benches the driver twenty-four hours.

sec14-card-sec14-R21.question_text: Which five first-offense violations, including in a personal car at point-oh-eight, strip a CDL for at least one year?
sec14-card-sec14-R21.teaching_text: CDL holders lose commercial privileges for a year even when impaired, refusing tests, or fleeing crashes off-duty.

sec14-card-sec14-R22.question_text: When does a CDL disqualification stretch to three years, and which offenses erase a CDL permanently?
sec14-card-sec14-R22.teaching_text: Placarded hazmat loads triple a first disqualification to three years, while any second strike or drug felony ends a CDL forever.

sec14-card-sec14-R23.question_text: If a CDL holder is arrested for DWI in their family car, can they get a limited work permit to drive a commercial rig?
sec14-card-sec14-R23.teaching_text: Limited licenses never cover commercial vehicles during an alcohol withdrawal, even after an off-duty passenger-car arrest.

sec14-card-sec14-F36.question_text: How does Minnesota treat driving while impaired by cannabis, low-potency hemp edibles, synthetic cannabinoids, or THC?
sec14-card-sec14-F36.teaching_text: Legal adult cannabis or hemp-edible sales never legalize driving impaired by any natural or artificial cannabinoid.

sec14-card-sec14-F37.question_text: May anyone smoke, vape, or consume cannabis flower or hemp-derived products inside a vehicle on a public road?
sec14-card-sec14-F37.teaching_text: Active consumption of any cannabis or hemp product inside a vehicle on streets or highways breaks Minnesota law.

sec14-card-sec14-F38.question_text: Where must opened or partly used cannabis or hemp packages ride in a car, and which dash spot is banned?
sec14-card-sec14-F38.teaching_text: Stashing an unsealed gummy bag in the glove compartment violates Minnesota's trunk-or-unoccupied storage law.

sec14-card-sec14-R24.question_text: Under what sole storage condition is an opened cannabis or hemp package legal inside a private vehicle on the road?
sec14-card-sec14-R24.teaching_text: Once a package seal breaks, keeping it within passenger reach on a public road becomes an open-package violation.

sec14-card-sec14-R25.question_text: Does stepping away from or lending out your car excuse you as owner if unsealed cannabis sits in the cabin on a street?
sec14-card-sec14-R25.teaching_text: Vehicle owners cannot allow or keep opened cannabis packages in the passenger cabin on public roads even when absent.

sec14-card-sec14-F39.question_text: May either the driver or a passenger drink or hold an open alcoholic container in a vehicle on a public road?
sec14-card-sec14-F39.teaching_text: Open cans, bottles, or cups of alcohol are banned throughout the cabin, and drivers cannot let passengers drink either.

sec14-card-sec14-F40.question_text: Which three actions involving controlled substances inside a motor vehicle does Minnesota prohibit?
sec14-card-sec14-F40.teaching_text: Possessing, using, or dealing controlled substances inside a car carries criminal and license-revocation exposure.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What does Minnesota law allow motorcycles to do between adjacent lanes, and what must drivers avoid doing?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Squeezing your car toward the lane stripe out of annoyance breaks the law and risks knocking a rider down.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Where are you most likely to spot motorcycle lane sharing, and how else may riders pass slow traffic?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Checking both side mirrors before inching over at red lights or in congestion prevents clipping a passing bike.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: Since riding between lanes is legal for motorcyclists in Minnesota, how should a car driver respond?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Treating a filtering motorcyclist like a line-cutter leads to dangerous swerves instead of steady, predictable lane holding.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: What active hazard do flashing red lights atop a school bus signal to nearby drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Children can step off the curb or dart out from ahead of the bumper at any moment once red lights flash.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: What is the closest distance you may stop from a school bus displaying flashing red lights?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Stopping two car lengths away gives small kids a wide safety zone where the bus driver can see everyone.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: Do you still have to halt for a school bus with flashing red lights if its side stop arm stays folded in?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Frozen hinges or mechanical glitches can keep the octagon arm tucked in while children are already stepping off.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: Under what single road-and-direction combination are you not required to stop for a bus's flashing red lights?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Painted yellow lines never excuse stopping; you must be going the opposite way across an actual divided highway.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: Which two financial and licensing penalties can hit if you blow past a school bus flashing red lights?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Running school-bus reds risks both a steep ticket and losing your license outright.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: Pair Minnesota's school-bus stopping distance with the lone highway situation where oncoming traffic keeps rolling?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Every undivided multi-lane street still demands a twenty-foot stop in both directions.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Between the stop arm and the flashing red roof lights, which signal legally triggers your twenty-foot school-bus stop?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Test makers bait drivers with a folded stop arm to verify you react to the flashing red lights alone.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: Which three traffic patterns require extra alertness in a work zone, and why are crews and machines so exposed?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Workers stand feet from live bumpers while heavy rigs swing wide or back up without warning.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: Name the trio of hazards grouped together in Minnesota's work-zone safety reminder?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Spotting orange cones early gives you time to drop phone distractions, merge smoothly, and track temporary lane lines.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: How does Minnesota law treat interfering with or obstructing a Driver and Vehicle Services employee?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Blocking or disrupting licensing staff crosses straight into criminal charges under state statute.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Which five customer behaviors are banned inside a DVS office, and what two actions follow if someone crosses the line?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Losing your temper with slurs, harassment, or refusal to follow staff directions ends your visit with law enforcement.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: Are interfering with DVS staff and obstructing them covered by separate laws or one shared criminal statute?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Whether someone actively blocks a counter or interferes with duties, the exact same criminal subdivision applies.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: How does the Commissioner frame driving, and which three core road duties protect everyone around you?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Every safe trip boils down to buckling up, respecting posted speeds, and driving completely alcohol-free.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: What two advantages does finishing the DVS online pre-application give you before stepping into an office?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Arriving with your data entered and the exact document list verified keeps your counter visit quick.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Within how many days before your visit should you start the online pre-application, and what must you carry in?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Starting too early lets the digital entry expire, forcing you back onto clipboards and paper forms at the office.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: Which four languages does drive.mn.gov's virtual assistant support, and what can you track inside a MyDVS account?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Checking license and registration status from home beats standing in line for routine record questions.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: What does the thirty-day DVS window actually control, and what licensing milestone should you never confuse it with?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Thirty days only keeps your online form active so you skip paper; permit holding runs in months.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: What scheduling and online preparation steps belong on your Class D written-test checklist, and on what timeline?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Completing your MyDVS pre-application inside the thirty days right before your booked slot keeps everything linked.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which three personal or payment items do you need ready alongside your appointment for the written test?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Forgetting fee payment, valid ID documents, or your Social Security number stalls your application at the desk.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: What is the minimum age for an applicant under eighteen to sit for Minnesota's written knowledge test?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Fourteen-year-olds may start driver ed classes, yet nobody takes the state knowledge exam before turning fifteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: Which two colored driver-education cards qualify an under-eighteen applicant for the written test, and what does each prove?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Traditional courses hand out Blue after full classroom completion, while integrated programs issue Pink after fifteen hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: Alongside age fifteen and a Blue or Pink Card, what optional certificate and adult signature rule apply to teen written testers?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: When an approved adult other than a parent signs your application, bringing supporting legal paperwork is mandatory.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: Contrast the exact driver-ed milestone behind a Blue Card versus a Pink Card when heading to the written test?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Either colored card unlocks the knowledge exam, provided behind-the-wheel is arranged or concurrent enrollment is active.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: Why must you separate age fifteen on the written-test checklist from the road-test checklist age?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Age fifteen only gets you into the permit stage; standard provisional road testing waits until sixteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: Besides your appointment and pre-application, who must accompany you to the road test or risk cancellation?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Because you still hold only a learner's permit, rolling up solo gives the station grounds to cancel your exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: Which driving credential do you hand directly to the examiner when checking in for your road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Leaving your plastic instruction permit on your dresser at home stops your road test before you reach the car.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: Which doors, restraints, lights, and registration rules must your road-test vehicle satisfy?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: A passenger door that will not unlatch from both sides or a dead brake bulb ends your test in the lot.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: Which three forms of vehicle insurance proof are accepted at the Minnesota road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Pulling up coverage on a phone or insurer portal works just like bringing the paper card or declaration sheet.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: Does Minnesota accept electronic proof of insurance displayed on a device when you check in for the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Make sure the screen or website loads clearly before your turn so check-in moves without delay.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: What minimum age and driver-education completion card must an under-eighteen applicant bring on road-test day?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Finishing both classroom and behind-the-wheel training earns the White Card required to test at sixteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: For how long must a teen hold a permit before the road test, and which convictions reset eligibility?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Any moving ticket or alcohol or controlled-substance conviction during those six months blocks road-test eligibility.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: What document proves road-test eligibility if part or all of a teen's six permit months happened in another state?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Minnesota credits clean permit time earned elsewhere once an official certified record from that state verifies it.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: Which two parent-signed items must an under-eighteen applicant present at the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Showing up with logged hours left unsigned forces a reschedule until a parent or guardian signs off.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: How long must an eighteen-year-old hold an instruction permit before the road test compared with someone nineteen or older?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Eighteen-year-olds often assume adulthood cuts the wait to three months, missing that three months starts at nineteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: Why won't a Blue Card or Pink Card get a sixteen-year-old into the road test?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Blue and Pink only prove class enrollment for the permit; the White Card proves all driver education is finished.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: Group all road-test applicants by whether they owe six months or three months on an instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Drawing the dividing line right at birthday nineteen keeps teens, eighteen-year-olds, and older adults straight.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: What extra violation-free requirement attaches to a teen's six-month permit hold on the road-test checklist?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Teens must pair six calendar months with a spotless moving and substance record to unlock provisional testing.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: What two status requirements must your driver's license meet whenever you drive on Minnesota public streets or highways?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: An expired plastic card in your wallet leaves you unlicensed the day after its expiration date passes.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: Which four steps in order must someone complete if they have never been licensed anywhere?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Nobody skips straight to the road test without clearing knowledge and vision checks and practicing on a permit.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: Which tests are required before reapplying if your Minnesota license expired between one and five years ago?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Letting an expired card sit past one year triggers retesting on traffic laws and eyesight before renewal.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: What does a new resident aged twenty-one or older holding a valid U.S., territory, or Canadian license need to get a Minnesota license?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Moving in before your prior card expires saves you from sitting for both the written and road exams.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: How do required tests change for that adult new resident if their former license expired under one year ago versus over one year?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Crossing the one-year expiration mark adds a full road test on top of the written knowledge exam.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: Within how many days after becoming a Minnesota resident must a regular driver versus a commercial driver get licensed here?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Commercial drivers get only half the grace window that standard passenger drivers receive after moving in.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: Which tests must a newcomer moving from outside the U.S. and Canada pass even with a valid home-country license?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Reciprocity waives written and road exams for Canada, whereas drivers arriving from other countries complete all three.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: What must you do with all other driver's licenses and ID cards you hold before DVS issues your Minnesota license?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Drivers are not allowed to stockpile active licenses from multiple states at the same time.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: At what minimum age may a nonresident visitor drive in Minnesota using a valid home-state or home-country license?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Even though Minnesota provisional licenses start at sixteen, a validly licensed fifteen-year-old visitor may drive while visiting.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: Under what age, vehicle-registration, and day-limit rules may someone from a country that does not license drivers drive here?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Every single condition must hold at once—age eighteen, current home-country registration on that car, and ninety days max.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: Contrast the testing rules for a valid-license newcomer from Canada against one from outside the U.S. and Canada?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Grouping Canada with U.S. states and territories avoids guessing all three exams for a Canadian transfer.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: Compare the newcomer licensing deadline for a regular Class D driver against a commercial driver?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Remembering commercial deadlines cut the sixty-day standard window in half keeps those two numbers locked.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: How does the minimum age for a validly licensed visitor compare with the age and cap for a visitor from a non-licensing country?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Holding an official home license unlocks visiting privileges three years younger than the rare ninety-day exception.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: Which three categories of farm, winter, or rail equipment can be operated without a Minnesota driver's license?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Notice farm tractors are exempt only while moving temporarily on public roads, alongside snowmobiles and rail equipment.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: Which three identification, testing, or comprehension failures bar someone from receiving a Minnesota license?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Safe traffic flow relies on every licensed driver reading official road signs and understanding state traffic rules.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: Below what age will Minnesota refuse to issue any driver's license or instruction permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Even special farm or medical credentials never drop below the statewide fifteen-year-old floor.
sec02-card-sec02-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Zero permits or licenses under fifteen

visual_sync.text_span: Zero permits or licenses under fifteen

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: What must an applicant under eighteen prove to get licensed if they do not hold a valid out-of-state license?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: Without a valid transfer license from another state, completing approved teen driver ed is non-negotiable.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: Below how many months of permit holding is a license refused to someone eighteen or younger versus nineteen or older?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Applying a single week before your six- or three-month permit minimum results in an automatic refusal.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: How does an active suspension, revocation, or cancellation affect applying for a new license?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Applying at a different counter never bypasses an open suspension, revocation, or canceled status.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: For what disability, safety, or court-ordered reasons can a Minnesota license be refused?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Licensing authorities must step in whenever medical limits, unsafe conduct, or court findings show public danger.

sec02-card-sec02-R19.question_text: What happens if you falsify medical answers on an application, and what might DVS request for a real condition?
sec02-card-sec02-R19.teaching_text: Disclosing honestly usually just needs a doctor's safety statement, whereas lying risks losing driving privileges.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.question_text: What must a permit or license holder submit—and within how many days—after a new diagnosis of epilepsy or blackouts?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.teaching_text: Prompt medical review within thirty days ensures sudden loss-of-consciousness conditions are managed safely.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: What personal details must test ID verify, and what is required whenever names across documents do not match?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Even a missing middle-name link or marriage surname shift needs certified legal paperwork connecting every step.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: What is DVS policy on laminated, altered, photocopied, or fraudulent identification documents?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Bringing a phone photo or photocopy gets turned away, and handing over fake papers gets them seized.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: How long past expiration can a Minnesota photo card versus a non-photo card still verify identity for a standard card?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Having your photograph printed on the expired Minnesota credential stretches its ID usefulness fivefold.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: If you do not have a qualifying Minnesota card, what pair of documents must you bring and what must one display?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: Pairing one primary document with one secondary document proves identity as long as full name and birth date appear.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: Compare the post-expiration ID window of a photo Minnesota card against one without a photo?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Keep five years tied to photo cards and one year tied to non-photo permits or credentials.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.question_text: Which certified records prove a legal name change, and what applies if your name changed multiple times?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.teaching_text: Skipping an earlier marriage or court order leaves a broken paper trail that DVS cannot accept.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.question_text: Which four statements must a translator certify when translating a non-English document for DVS?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.teaching_text: Having a bilingual relative translate your birth certificate gets rejected because family members are barred.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: Under Minnesota's Driver's License for All law, how does immigration status affect getting a standard card?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: Standard permits, IDs, and licenses focus on identity and safe-driving tests regardless of immigration status.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: Which documents and information must you bring in person to obtain a REAL ID compliant Minnesota card?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Federal REAL ID rules add legal-presence verification, Social Security knowledge, and two Minnesota address proofs.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: What is the key proof difference between a Driver's License for All standard card and a REAL ID card?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Standard applicants skip legal-presence proof, whereas REAL ID demands both legal presence and two residency papers.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: Who is eligible for a Minnesota enhanced license or ID, what proofs are required, and what address prints on it?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Because enhanced cards double as border-crossing credentials, U.S. citizenship and your physical state residence are mandatory.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: What extra residency count, interview step, and surcharge apply when applying for an enhanced card?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Budget fifteen extra dollars and expect an interview questionnaire on top of standard counter steps.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: How is your Social Security number handled on a DVS application, on the card itself, and if an eligible person refuses it?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Your number never appears on the plastic or chip, yet withholding an issued SSN halts processing.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.question_text: When can someone in a jail or correctional facility renew a Minnesota license or ID by mail?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.teaching_text: Mail renewal covers people serving over six months in facilities lacking an existing DVS renewal arrangement.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.question_text: How long does a temporary post-prison reintegration license last, and what cancels it early?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.teaching_text: This fifteen-month bridge helps released residents return to work, provided they keep their driving privileges clean.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: Where and how is the Class D written test administered, and what question styles and subjects appear?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Expect both multiple-choice and true-or-false items covering Minnesota traffic laws and road signs.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: Which language and audio accommodations are available at computer written-test stations?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: Putting on station headphones lets you listen to each question read aloud as you read the screen.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: How many written tests can you attempt in one day, and what percentage score is required to pass?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Missing eighty percent means studying overnight because DVS caps written attempts at one per day.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: After how many consecutive written-test failures does a retest fee start, and how much does each extra try cost?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Attempts one and two carry no extra retest charge, while try three and beyond cost ten dollars apiece.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: How does the classroom driver-education rule for the written test differ at age eighteen versus under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Turning eighteen drops mandatory classroom enrollment before the written test, whereas younger teens need Blue or Pink.
sec02-card-sec02-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Adults skip class, teens show cards

visual_sync.text_span: Adults skip class, teens show cards

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: State the exact trigger and dollar amount for Minnesota's written-test retest fee?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Keep written retests tied to ten dollars so you never mix them up with the twenty-dollar road retest.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: What central acuity and peripheral side-vision minimums must you meet at DVS vision screening?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Passing requires both clear straight-ahead reading at twenty over forty and wide side awareness at one hundred five degrees.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: What process follows if you fail vision screening or score below one hundred five degrees of side vision?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: An eye specialist examines you and sends findings to the Driver Evaluation Unit to set lenses or restrictions.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: If you read twenty over forty clearly, can narrow peripheral vision under one hundred five degrees still trigger a referral?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Tunnel vision misses cross-traffic and pedestrians, so falling short on side degrees alone requires an eye doctor's report.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: Which three parts make up the Minnesota road test, and what promise applies to examiner instructions?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Examiners check car gear first, low-speed maneuvers second, and traffic driving third—never asking anything illegal.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: Alongside your permit and insurance proof, what vehicle rules govern neighborhood electric cars and rentals at the road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: Showing up in a rental car where your name is missing from the contract cancels the test.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.question_text: How may you use a backup camera during the road test without losing points?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.teaching_text: Using the screen as a helper is fine, whereas staring solely at the display without looking back fails.
sec02-card-sec02-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Glance at camera, still look back

visual_sync.text_span: Glance at camera, still look back

sec02-card-sec02-F34.question_text: Which four cabin habits, companions, or automated parking features are prohibited during the road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.teaching_text: Even interpreters, pets, or hands-free self-parking systems must stay off or out during scoring.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.question_text: Which cabin and exterior controls can the examiner inspect first, and what happens if your car fails that check?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.teaching_text: Checking wipers, horn, defroster, parking brake, beams, flashers, mirrors, and fuel beforehand saves your test slot.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.question_text: When must adaptive or restriction-required equipment work on your road-test car, and what is the lone exception?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.teaching_text: Unless today's road test is specifically to lift that restriction, every required aid must function properly.

sec02-card-sec02-R17.question_text: If your test vehicle has automatic headlights, what must you still demonstrate during the pre-drive equipment check?
sec02-card-sec02-R17.teaching_text: Leaving the dial on auto without knowing how to turn beams on by hand stumps unprepared drivers.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.question_text: Alongside traffic skills, hill parking, and parallel parking, what exact backing maneuver and stall width are graded?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.teaching_text: Practicing ninety-degree backing between cones spaced ten feet apart builds muscle memory for Minnesota's signature stall.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.question_text: Which five on-road mistakes or refusals cause immediate failure on the Minnesota road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.teaching_text: Notice even an avoidable crash where the other driver broke the law still fails your exam immediately.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.question_text: What retest fee kicks in after two failed road tests, and what training is required after four failures?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.teaching_text: Four failed road tests freeze further tries until a licensed instructor logs at least six behind-the-wheel hours.
sec02-card-sec02-F38.must_match_memory_hook: Twenty after two, training after four

visual_sync.text_span: Twenty after two, training after four

sec02-card-sec02-F39.question_text: Before booking another shot after a failed road test, what requirement from your score sheet must you complete?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.teaching_text: Examiners assign targeted practice time based on your weak spots before you may test again.
